title: Ultrasound Technologists (Diagnostic Medical Sonographers)
description:
At Canada Diagnostic Centres, we are driven by helping Canadians access diagnostic services and providing remarkable experiences to our patients every day. Our care is compassionate, accurate and timely to help patients make progress in their health journey. We live by a mantra of “Remarkable Care. Remarkable Careers.”
We are currently looking for CRGS certified, or soon to be certified, Ultrasound Technologists (Diagnostic Medical Sonographers) to join our expanding outpatient clinic practice in a full-time or part-time position. Working collaboratively with radiologists and other healthcare professionals, you’ll explain procedures, position patients, adjust equipment, and capture diagnostic images. Bringing compassion and clarity to each patient interaction, you’ll help ensure remarkable care every visit.
What You’ll Be Doing

Perform Ultrasound Exams: Conduct routine and specialized sonography imaging under the direction of Radiologists and referring Physicians, while adhering to departmental protocols and guidelines.
Provide Remarkable Care: Explain exams and procedures, address questions, ease concerns, and help patients feel comfortable.
Collaborate with Clinic Teams: Partner with radiologists and other teams to help deliver a seamless and thoughtful experience.
Expand Expertise: Engage in ongoing professional development to refine existing skills, build new competencies, and specialize in additional skillsets such as Interventional, MSK, and Breast.
Ensure Compliance: Follow privacy, confidentiality, safety, and other regulatory requirements.
Monitor and Troubleshoot Systems: Track ultrasound equipment performance, document findings, and resolve basic issues.
Prepare and Maintain Work Areas: Prepare and stock exam rooms for exams and procedures; report low inventory as needed.

What We’re Looking For

Professional Membership: Certified Registered Generalist Sonographer (CRGS) through Sonography Canada, or eligible to obtain. Current registration with the Alberta College of Medical Diagnostic and Therapeutic Technologists (ACMDTT), or eligibility for registration.
Ultrasound Experience: Clinical competency as a generalist sonographer, with an interest in refining and expanding skills in advanced practice areas such as MSK, OB/GYN, vascular and cardiac exams, and interventional procedures.
Specialized Knowledge: Experience in breast, MSK, OB/GYN, vascular, cardiac ultrasound exams, or in interventional procedures, is considered an asset.
A Compassionate Approach: A history of remarkable care, collaboration, adaptability, and flexibility.

What We Offer

Competitive Pay: Industry-leading wages and unique additional earning opportunities.
Sign-On Bonus: A welcome incentive for joining our team (terms and conditions apply).
Relocation Allowance: Financial assistance for eligible candidates to help with moving expenses.
Generous Time Off: Vacation, personal days, sick leave, and paid time off for your birthday.
Health & Wellness: Medical, dental, and vision benefits, plus access to our Employee & Family Assistance Program.
Learning & Development: Specialized training opportunities, along with an annual education allowance.
Long-Term Savings Program: RRSP/TFSA plan.
Professional Licensing Support: Funding available for Sonography Canada membership fees.

Additional Information

Position Types: Full-time or part-time options to align with your schedule and career goals. Part-time schedules include three or four fixed days per week, depending on FTE.
Consistent Schedule: Daytime, Monday to Friday.
Work Location: Clinic assignments will be discussed during the candidacy process and guided by operational needs and professional development, with preferences considered where possible.
Out-of-Province Applicants: Eligibility for registration with the ACMDTT is required.
Students and Recent Graduates: Applications welcome.

About Canada Diagnostic Centres
With a network of over 50+ community clinics across British Columbia, Alberta, Saskatchewan, and Ontario, we have been a leader and innovator in radiological services for more than 30 years. At the core of our work is a simple belief: Clarity Through Caring. This means diagnostic imaging that is compassionate, accessible, and grounded in quality.

In 2025, we supported more than 900,000 patients through their diagnostic journey. Our expertise spans a full range of imaging and interventional services, including MRI, CT, Ultrasound, Echocardiography, Nuclear Medicine, Mammography, X-Ray, Breast Imaging, Bone Mineral Density, Fluoroscopy, Maternal Fetal Medicine, Pediatric Imaging, Gastrointestinal Studies, and image-guided pain management procedures.

Our services are delivered by collaborative interdisciplinary teams that bring clarity through caring to life. Inspired by what our teams make possible, we create opportunities for development, provide reliable equipment, and continuously improve how care is delivered.

The care we extend to our patients and teams shapes how we welcome applicants. We actively invite applications from all individuals and are committed to equitable hiring practices. If you require accommodations at any stage of the hiring process, please contact us at talentacquisition@canadadiagnostics.ca.

Please note that only those selected for an interview will be contacted. All applicants must have legal authorization to work in Canada.

title: Lighting Design Intern/Co-op Spring 2027 - Energy Solutions
description:
CMTA is one of the fastest growing engineering firms in the U.S. with nationally recognized expertise in sustainable, high-performance building engineering. We are a collaborative, competitive, innovative, and energetic group of engineers and team leaders who incorporate a holistic approach towards consulting engineering, performance contracting, and zero energy projects. We focus on finding engineers whose personalities lead them to excellence, and we provide exceptional opportunities for our employees.
The core business of our Energy Solutions division is the delivery of Guaranteed Energy Savings Performance Contracts (ESPCs). Simply put, our ESPCs are a viable way to upgrade and renovate facilities in a budget-neutral or even budget-positive way. The process diverts money already being spent on utilities and directs it into facility upgrades, covering scope development, design, bidding, construction management, commissioning, measurement and verification, and even ongoing energy management services. We have experience in designing the nation’s most energy efficient buildings, including many zero energy buildings. Our knowledge is unparalleled in the Guaranteed ESPC market, which allows us to dive deeper than our competitors. CMTA Energy Solutions has a robust co-op program for college students pursuing a degree in engineering. We offer an immersive experience in the world of Guaranteed Energy Savings Performance Contracting for one or more semesters. Our co-ops build competitive industry skills in a hands-on environment through collaborative project tasks with full-time engineers while under the direct supervision of Professional Engineers. Our program is designed to develop students into full-time caliber employees that contribute to the company’s growth. The ideal candidate will possess excellent interpersonal skills and will be able to work well both as a team member and independently. Our program stands apart from the typical, rehearsed co-op rotation in which every co-op gains the same experience because it is designed for co-ops to stand out and take on challenging projects. Co-ops will be involved with multiple Guaranteed Energy Savings Performance Contracts and will have a role in every stage of their development. Each stage offers a variety of valuable experiences, from initial development through implementation. Whether co-ops are interested in building their skill set in identifying and calculating energy savings measures, developing renovation documents, or hands-on field experience, CMTA Energy Solutions is bound to overcome expectations. Lighting Co-ops can expect to get hands on experience with commercial lighting systems.
By the end of the program co-ops will have gained the experience to be able to deliver a full LED lighting upgrade design from scratch. Our Lighting co-op will directly support our lighting project managers. Job Functions: (may include but are not limited to)

  • Assist in all aspects of the project development phase – including site visits, building audits
  • Energy calculations in relation to lighting upgrades
  • Produce detailed construction documents using CAD for LED lighting upgrades
  • Support material procurement and construction management staff during implementation of lighting upgrades
  • Field verify proper installation and implementation of LED lighting upgrades

Requirements:

  • Pursuing a BSEE, preferably a sophomore (2nd year), or junior (3rd year),
  • CAD experience is helpful but not required
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Word and Excel
  • Ability to work both independently and as a team member and
  • Ability to travel for field work.

title: CMM Operator / Programmer
description:
M&M Industries is a U.S.-based manufacturer of plastic pails and packaging solutions. We operate in a fast-paced manufacturing environment where precision, quality, and continuous improvement are essential to meeting customer expectations.
The CMM Operator / Programmer is responsible for inspecting finished goods, gauges, test stands, fixtures, and related items to ensure conformance to drawings, specifications, and quality standards. This role programs, sets up, operates, and optimizes Coordinate Measuring Machine (CMM) equipment while supporting new product development through the creation and revision of inspection programs.
Schedule: Monday-Thursday, 7:00AM-5:00PM
Key Responsibilities

  • Responsible for the programming, setup, calibration, and operation of the Coordinate Measuring Machine (CMM)• Troubleshoots CMM programs, probes, fixtures, and measurement issues• Maintains the condition of all CMM equipment and accessories• Optimizes existing CMM programs to improve efficiency• Identifies opportunities to improve measurement methods and inspection processes• Interprets GD&T requirements and product specifications• Verifies specified dimensions of products and raw materials using calipers, CMM, height gauges, scales, and other precision measuring equipment• Measures dimensions including diameter, height, wall thickness, and other critical characteristics• Conducts First Article, In-Process, Incoming, and Final Inspections• Conducts new product validation activities• Documents inspection results by completing reports, maintaining logs, and entering data into quality databases• Executes timely and accurate disposition of nonconforming material• Supports root cause analysis and corrective action activities• Performs QC Technician duties as assigned• Provides support to other departments for quality planning, process development, and related activities• Performs other duties as assigned

Qualifications
Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills• Ability to read and interpret GD&T blueprints, CAD models, and technical drawings• Ability to utilize manual and visual inspection equipment including calipers, gauges, digital indicators, surface plates, optical comparators, and CMM equipment• Proficient in Microsoft Excel and Word• Ability to analyze data to support process optimization• Strong understanding of Zeiss Calypso software; experience with MCOSMOS is a plus

Education

  • High School Diploma or GED required

Experience

  • Three (3) to five (5) years of Quality Assurance or Quality Control experience utilizing a Coordinate Measuring Machine (CMM) required

Licenses & Certifications

  • Certified Quality Engineer (CQE) or Certified Quality Technician (CQT) preferred but not required

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to lift and handle a minimum of 20 pounds repeatedly and up to 45 pounds occasionally• Ability to stand for extended periods of time• Ability to work in a manufacturing environment that may be hot or cold• Ability to wear required PPE at all times (safety glasses, safety shoes, etc.)

What We Offer
M&M Industries offers a competitive benefits package designed to support our employees and reward the work that drives our success. Full-time employees may elect medical, dental and vision coverage effective on their first day of employment. We also offer paid vacation and discretionary time off (DTO), with the amount and timing based on position and tenure; paid company holidays after 90 days; and a 401(k) with company match beginning on the first day of the month following 90 days of employment. Educational reimbursement is available after one year of employment. Eligible employees may also participate in quarterly profit sharing when company performance thresholds are met. Hourly employees who work on a recognized holiday receive time-and-a-half for all hours worked. Benefits and eligibility are subject to applicable plan documents and company policies.

title: Hospitality Aide (PWLWR)
description:
Role Overview

A Hospitality Aide plays a vital role in supporting the daily life and well-being of residents in a senior living or healthcare community. This role focuses on assisting with meal service, housekeeping, and resident engagement in activities, fostering a positive and comfortable environment. By building meaningful relationships and honoring each resident’s individuality, the Hospitality Aide helps create a home where residents feel valued, engaged, and connected.

Key Accountabilities

Assist with meal service by setting up, serving, and cleaning dining areas while ensuring mealtimes are an enjoyable and social experience for residents.
Preparing and providing appropriate texture modified meals and dietary requirements
Supporting mealtime service to residents as required by fostering a warm and inviting dining experience.
Cleaning and maintaining kitchen equipment daily
Maintaining environmental public health standards and provincial standards for regulatory bodies
Participating in community committees and working groups to support community initiatives
Maintain cleanliness and organization of dining and common areas. May require assistance in the cleaning of resident rooms.
Provide non-clinical support to residents, helping with mobility and participation in activities.
Engage with residents to build positive relationships and encourage socialization by listening to their stories, honoring their experiences, and creating moments of joy.
Follow safety and hygiene standards, ensuring compliance with community policies.
Collaborate with staff to report residents' needs and concerns while advocating for their personal preferences and comfort.
Ensure the proper use of personal protective equipment (PPE) as necessary.

High school diploma or equivalent (preferred but not mandatory).
Food Safety Handling Certificate (such as ServSafe or Food Safe) required.

Required Skills

Strong interpersonal and communication skills to interact effectively with residents and staff.
Compassion, patience, and a service-oriented mindset.
Ability to work in a fast-paced environment while maintaining attention to detail.
Organizational skills to ensure efficient operations in dining and community areas.
Ability to work collaboratively within a team.

Additional Preferred Education and Skills Asset

Prior experience in senior living, hospitality, or food service is beneficial but not required.
CPR or First Aid Certification is a plus.
WHMIS (Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System) training is beneficial for handling cleaning chemicals.
Physical ability to stand, walk, lift (up to 50 lbs), and assist residents as needed.

Pipe wrenches
Tape measure
Manlift

Computer and software
Calculator
Temperature reading devices

PHYSICAL ACTIVITY REQUIRED FOR THIS POSITION:

Climbing, ascending or descending ladders, stairs, scaffolding, ramps, poles and the like, using feet and legs and/or hands and arms. Body agility is emphasized.

Balancing, maintaining body equilibrium to prevent falling when walking, standing or crouching on narrow, slippery or erratically moving surfaces.
Stooping, bending body downward and forward by bending spine and waist. Example: Changing paper in printer, copier machine.
Kneeling, bending legs at knee to come to a rest on knee or knees.
Crouching, bending the body downward and forward by bending leg and spine.
Crawling, moving about on hands and knees or hands and feet.
Reaching, extending hand(s) and arm(s) in any direction. Example: Giving signals, reaching for material or handle on item.
Standing, particularly for sustained periods of time. Example: Making copies, giving presentations, directing traffic.
Walking, moving about on foot to accomplish tasks, particularly for long distances.
Pushing, using upper extremities to press against something with steady force to thrust forward, downward or outward.
Pulling, using upper extremities to exert force to drag, haul or tug objects in a sustained motion.
Lifting, raising objects from a lower to a higher position or moving objects horizontally from position to position. (5 lbs. to 50 lbs.)
Fingering, picking, pinching, typing or otherwise working primarily with fingers rather than the whole hand or arm as in handling.

Feeling, perceiving attributes of objects such as size, shape, temperature or texture by touching with skin, particularly that of fingertips.
Talking, expressing or exchanging ideas by means of the spoken word; via face to face or telephone.

title: Production Planner
description:
M&M Industries is a U.S.-based manufacturer of plastic pails and packaging solutions. We operate in a fast-paced manufacturing environment where production accuracy, material flow, and on-time delivery are critical to meeting customer expectations.
The Production Planner coordinates and expedites the flow of work and materials within and between departments according to daily and weekly production schedules. This role supports safe and efficient operations by reviewing production and shipment schedules, monitoring inventory levels, collaborating with department supervisors, and resolving production-related issues to ensure customer requirements are met.
Key Responsibilities

Follow M&M safety policies and procedures to ensure a safe work environment
Support the manufacturing team to ensure daily production requirements are achieved and customer expectations are met
Drive performance related to On-Time/In-Full (OTIF) KPI, with accountability included in performance reviews
Provide expected completion dates for incoming orders with the goal of meeting customer requested dates
Analyze and prepare production-related documentation
Monitor material supply flow and identify shortages or bottlenecks
Create production schedules and prioritize job orders to optimize production efficiency
Maintain production schedules and required reports
Follow up with cross-functional teams to expedite material and document flow to meet schedule and customer expectations
Complete status reports related to production progress, work-in-process (WIP), and raw material inventory
Interact daily with shop floor management to resolve manufacturing efficiency issues and respond to requests from Manufacturing, Customer Service, and Accounting
Ensure work orders are released in ShotScope to provide visibility for planning and purchasing requirements
Ensure special notes are included on work orders to prevent customer service misses
Assist in reviewing the accuracy of Bills of Materials (BOMs)
Maintain a clean and organized work area
Perform other duties as assigned, including tasks requiring higher or lower levels of proficiency

Qualifications
Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Strong written and verbal communication skills, both internal and external
Strong math and analytical skills
Ability to work within production tracking programs (e.g., ShotScope/RJG platforms)
Detail-oriented and highly organized
Proficient in Microsoft Office, including Excel, Outlook, and Word

Education

High School Diploma or GED required
College degree or equivalent work experience preferred

Experience

Three (3) years of experience in a manufacturing environment required
One (1) year of experience with MRP systems preferred

Physical Requirements

Ability to work in a manufacturing environment that may include hot or cold conditions
Ability to wear required PPE at all times (safety glasses, etc.)
Duties may require occasional lifting, extended standing, and walking

What We Offer
M&M Industries offers a competitive benefits package designed to support our employees and reward the work that drives our success. Full-time employees may elect medical, dental and vision coverage effective on their first day of employment. We also offer paid vacation and discretionary time off (DTO), with the amount and timing based on position and tenure; paid company holidays after 90 days; and a 401(k) with company match beginning on the first day of the month following 90 days of employment. Educational reimbursement is available after one year of employment. Eligible employees may also participate in quarterly profit sharing when company performance thresholds are met. Hourly employees who work on a recognized holiday receive time-and-a-half for all hours worked. Benefits and eligibility are subject to applicable plan documents and company policies.

title: Process Technician
description:
At M&M Industries, we take pride in producing high-quality plastic packaging solutions that make a difference in everyday life. Our success starts with the people who make it all happen — from the production floor to our technical and engineering teams.
The Process Technician is responsible for performing die, color, and material changeovers while starting up, maintaining, and optimizing injection molding machines. This role ensures that molding processes run efficiently, meet company quality standards, and achieve production targets. The Process Technician also supports troubleshooting efforts, assists with new mold trials, and maintains accurate records of process adjustments and results.

Process Technician Pay Structure
Starting pay is based on relevant experience and demonstrated technical skills. Candidates may be placed at the level that best aligns with their qualifications, with opportunities for pay progression at established intervals, including 90 days and one, two, and three years.

Process Technician I: $26.90 per hour
Process Technician II: $29.00 per hour
Process Technician III: $31.37 per hour
Process Technician IV: $34.22 per hour
Process Technician V: $36.00 per hour

Shift Differential: An additional $1.00 per hour for second and third shifts.

Key Responsibilities:

Follows all safety policies and Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures to ensure a safe work environment.
Sets up and adjusts injection molding machines, auxiliary equipment, and tooling for production runs.
Monitors and optimizes molding processes to ensure consistent part quality and cycle efficiency.
Troubleshoots and resolves molding defects, process deviations, and equipment malfunctions.
Performs mold and material changeovers, ensuring proper setup, documentation, and communication with the team.
Maintains detailed records of process parameters, adjustments, and troubleshooting activities.
Uses a forklift and/or overhead crane to pull, change, or set molds safely and efficiently.
Maintains a clean and organized work environment in accordance with 5S principles.
Collaborates with the Engineering Team to develop samples for new molds and materials.
Performs machine testing, process validation, and assists in continuous improvement initiatives.
Utilizes knowledge of processing various grades of plastic to produce quality parts that meet customer expectations.
Performs other duties as assigned.

Competencies (Knowledge/Skills/Abilities):

Proficient mechanical aptitude and understanding of injection molding processes.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Basic proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Word.
Comprehensive understanding of Food Safety, GMP, PRP, and HACCP requirements as they relate to food-contact packaging (where applicable).
Basic understanding of decoupled molding (preferred).

Education:

High School Diploma or G.E.D. (required)

Experience:

Required years of experience may vary based on qualifications, skills, and level within the role.

Licenses & Certifications:

Forklift Certification (required; in-house training provided)
RJG Training or Certification (preferred)

Physical Requirements:

Work is performed in a manufacturing environment that may be hot or cold and requires PPE at all times (safety glasses, ear protection, etc.).
Ability to lift and handle 45–55 pounds.
Ability to perform work in standing or sitting positions as required.
Ability to work in tight or confined spaces.

Educational reimbursement is available after one year of employment. Eligible employees may also participate in quarterly profit sharing when company performance thresholds are met. title: Lead, Distribution
description:
BASIC PURPOSE AND SCOPE OF POSITION
Supervise and assist in all shift responsibilities, this may include shipping, receiving, cycle counting and bin maintenance. These duties contribute to the shipping success and productivity level of the wholegoods department.

PRINCIPAL ACTIVITIES: This position does the following in accordance with all applicable Federal, State and local laws / regulations and the Company’s policies, procedures and guidelines:

Responsible for securing the building perimeter twice a day. Locking doors, turning off lights, etc. Setting up the building alarm system when leaving, making certain all security zones are clear and building is locked.
Make certain all daily parts orders are completely picked, packed, and loaded for shipment. When shipping needs to be completed assign employees to designated areas to complete the work load. Confirming all shipping transfer orders in SAP. Run daily shipping reports through the clippership program and FedEx standalone system. Check the picking status program to ensure all late day emergency orders are completed. Delegate replenishment of shipping supplies to the work stations, also clean the shipping area. This shipping procedure is the key to supplying our dealers.
Assign employees to receive in and replenish multiple parts venders. Expedite all receiving inquiries from other depots and corporate office via lotus notes. Confirming all daily receiving transfer orders in SAP. Check daily bin to bin transfers in SAP. Class daily moves and new products in the material master in SAP. Run daily class reports for storage sections to ensure parts are in the correct designated areas after put away process. File daily paperwork according to vendor, separate all claims for senior lead person. Run weekly spot checks to ensure work is adequate and reaches safety regulations. When work load is great, assist in the receiving and replenishment process. The receiving process is critical, this ensures that the product is available for ordering.
CYCLE COUNTING-Create inventory documents to be counted in SAP. Assign employees to designated areas to inventory cycle counting documents. Completely check all inventory discrepancies and generate recounts in SAP. Once documents are complete, run all variance reports and unblock designated bins in SAP. File all daily inventory data. Keep all inventory production data in Excel spreadsheets. Inventory counts are critical to the success of our shipping percentage and customer service.
30 DAY RETURNS-Record all packages returned by the dealers by sender and tracking number. Thoroughly check returned items for damage and information provided by the dealer, put returned items away in their designated location. Enter returned parts into our stock manually using SAP. All damaged claims are filed with FedEx via telephone or online. Excel spreadsheets are processed showing all 30 day dealer returns with the reason for the return, this data is sent monthly to the corporate office for review. All daily paperwork is filed alphabetical by dealer and month. The dealer receives credit for the returned items and these items are entered into our stock.
PIERCE, TERMINATIONS-Paperwork provided by dealer is checked for part locations. Parts are thoroughly checked and put away according to their designated area. Final paperwork is given to Operations Supervisor for credit and the entering process. The dealers receive credit for returned items and these items are entered into our stock.
BIN MAINTNANCE-Monthly reports are ran in SAP to find part class changes. Assign multiple reports to employees to bin to bin transfer. Check and change storage type and section with all bin to bin transfers in SAP. This procedure helps promote speed and efficiency in the shipping process.
TRAINING-Teach and assist all new temporary hires and full time employees. This includes multiple uses of SAP system, barcode scanners, all forms of equipment operation, and safety procedures and regulations.
Other duties as assigned by management.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

High school education or equivalent required.

At least 3 years in a high-volume distribution environment required.
Manage and meet multiple tasks and deadline skills.
The ability to use a computer to enter and/or retrieve multiple amounts of information.
Some experience operating in a SAP system preferred.
Knowledge, skill, and ability to safely operate and train others on all forms of equipment in the warehouse.

EQUIPMENT OPERATION (% of time, description, nature of service):

Computer, RF barcode scanners, Intermec 3400 printers, Zebra printers, Electric fork lifts, Propane fork lifts, Stock picker, Reach truck, Pallet jack, Shrink wrap machine, Cardboard compactor, Trash compactor
Office equipment including copier, fax, phone, printer – No service.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:
Warehouse environment. The position will require walking, standing and sitting at a computer.

This job is intended to include the current essential functions of the job. title: Chill Vancouver Program & Community Coordinator
description:
Job Description:
As the Chill Vancouver Program & Community Coordinator (“PCC”), you will deliver Chill’s programs in Vancouver, British Columbia ensuring that every youth participant experiences high-quality programming that aligns with Chill’s mission and core values. You will facilitate programs using Chill’s established person-centered curriculum and engage youth through the principles of both developmentally appropriate experiential learning.
With guidance and support from the Program Leadership team, you will coordinate the day-to-day tasks required for program operations, including scheduling, communicating with agencies and mentors, managing gear, and directly facilitating snowboard, skateboard, stand-up paddleboard, and surf programs (note that Chill hires boardsport instructors to teach the boardsport lessons). You will assist in recruitment efforts, alumni engagement, and data tracking while following existing program structures and guidelines.
This role requires strong communication and organizational skills to effectively collaborate with internal and external stakeholders. You will report to Chill’s Program Management team located in Eastern Time Zones and work within established policies and procedures to ensure successful program execution.
Primary Responsibilities:

Program Coordination (25%)

Coordinate the recruitment and onboarding of new agencies, mentors, and independent contractors, including:

Sending program applications and acceptance notifications via email.
Supporting relationship-building with agencies to encourage participation and engagement.
Conducting in-person orientations using established program guidelines.

Work with team members to coordinate program logistics, including:

Communicating with program partners to confirm details.
Assisting with scheduling and payment confirmations for independent contractors.
Sharing transportation details with partners and working with bus companies on program days.
Attending pre- and post-program meetings to relay updates and gather feedback.

Follow existing guidelines to ensure diversity, equity, and inclusion in relationship-building efforts.

Program Facilitation (25%)

Lead on-site facilitation of Chill’s experiential learning curriculum for groups of 15-45 youth per program, following pre-established lesson plans and activities.
Maintain accurate program records, including attendance, evaluations, and data submissions using Salesforce.
Provide guidance to volunteer mentors and agency leads during program sessions.
Ensure program quality by adhering to Chill’s established standards and completing required evaluations.
Represent Chill in community settings as a program facilitator.

Gear Management (20%)

Maintain program gear, storage spaces, and inventory according to organizational guidelines, including:

Conducting seasonal cleaning and organization.
Transporting gear to and from storage locations as needed.

Ensure all equipment is available and in working condition for program use.

Agency, Mentor, and Alumni Engagement (30%)

Advance agency and mentor relationships through timely communication and scheduled check-ins.
Support outreach efforts to program alumni, ensuring they are aware of engagement opportunities.
Help coordinate new and ongoing initiatives for alumni, following guidance from the leadership team.

Additional Responsibilities:

Capture and share marketing content (photos, testimonials) with Chill’s Marketing team as directed.
Provide program-related content for grant applications and reports as needed.
Perform other program-related duties as assigned to support the Programs Team.

Education, Experience & Knowledge:
Candidate Requirements:

Must have a commitment to Chill’s Mission: to inspire young people through boardsports and build a more equitable outdoor community and embrace Chill Values: Honesty, Equity, Progression, & Fun
Youth Experience:

Must have 2+ years of professional experience working with youth in various settings; possess solid understanding of youth programming and relationship management and strong understanding of youth needs to ensure a positive youth experience during and after programs. Preference for candidate with experience leading groups of 20+ youth and applying trauma-informed, equity-based approaches.

Location:

Must live in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada with a hybrid balance of work-from-home and in-person time for programs/community engagement.
Candidates with 2+ years of residency in Vancouver are strongly preferred due to the nature of this role requiring familiarity with the local community and city.

Education & Experience:

Generally, 2-4 years of related work experience and generally, a Bachelor’s degree

or a Bachelor’s degree can be substituted with 2 years of related work experience and a 2-year higher education degree

or a 2-year higher education degree can be substituted with 4 years of work experience and a high school degree

Technology Skills:

Proficiency in Microsoft Office 365 (Outlook, Teams, Word and Excel)
Willingness to learn special software skills specific to the role which are required - including Salesforce or similar programs management databases

Organizational & Communication Skills:

Must be organized, self-motivated and detail-oriented with strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to provide demonstrated experience.

Certifications:

Must obtain CPR and First Aid Certification, SafeSport Training, Concussion Training, Youth Mental Health First Aid, and other certifications as assigned (Chill will cover these costs)

Physical Requirements:

Must be able to work nights and/or weekends during program facilitation (time/day of week dependent on program site and sport)
Comfortable facilitating curriculum on a moving charter bus during programs and working outdoors in all weather conditions
Ability to lift and transport program gear/equipment (up to 50lbs; up to 160lbs for mobile skate park equipment)
Must have a valid driver’s license and access to a vehicle for commuting and gear transport
Must be able to use personal cell phone for work related tasks

Age Requirement:

All Chill employees must be 18+

Candidate Preferred Skills:

Youth Leadership:

Experience managing and leading groups of at least 20 youth; experience and knowledge providing a trauma-informed, equity seeking approach to youth and community care
Experience working with youth in at least 2 different settings (ie. youth agency, probationary programs, rehab facilities, schools, outdoor education, experiential education, etc.); experience working with youth of diverse identities and backgrounds

Problem Solving, Decision Making, Autonomy & Communication:

Experience managing time efficiently and setting own schedule; experience holding diversity, equity and inclusion at the forefront of decision-making; adaptable and effective working with multiple personalities and backgrounds
Experience recruiting, managing, or leading adults, volunteers and external partners

Boardsports Experience:

Basic familiarity with snowboarding, skateboarding, stand-up paddleboarding, or surfing is preferred. Willingness to learn new boardsports (Chill will provide training & equipment)

Certification/Education:

Background in social work, psychology, education, recreation, adventure learning, or youth programming is a plus

Compensation and Benefits
We aim for our compensation and benefits package to be clear, fair, and equitable.

With a start date by October 19, 2026, this position is:

Year-round, hourly, non-exempt, part-time (20 hours per week) position.
This role is not currently eligible for benefits, which begins at a part time of 24 hours/weekly.
The hiring rate for this role is $25.87 per hour (equivalent to a yearly part time (20 hrs/week) salary of $26,904). The full range for pay rate for this role is $25.87 - $31.05. We construct our salaries in such a way that staff can in the future move through the range as they grow within their level. Candidates will start at the specified hiring rate of $25.87 per hour. Chill follows a non-negotiation policy for salaries that applies to both current and new hires, as research shows that salary negotiations may lead to negative outcomes for individuals from non-dominant groups.

Candidates must reside in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. Chill’s agency partners are located within the city, and this position requires regular travel throughout Vancouver to support program recruitment and facilitation. The role includes a mix of work-from-home time and in-person engagement at program sites and community events. Relocation assistance and commuter benefits are not provided.
Candidates must have a current driver’s license in good standing and must have access to a personal vehicle for driving to and from programs, agencies and partners. Mileage is reimbursable.
A Chill laptop will be provided for use throughout the duration of employment.
This role is not eligible for benefits, which begins at a part time of 24 hours/weekly.
Your employment includes a paid time off package which includes:

Paid time off vacation accrual beginning at 10 hours/month – accumulating up to 15 days of PTO in the first year, up to 16 hours of volunteer time off, approximately 11 holidays per year and 3 floating holidays (these hours are prorated depending on date of hire and part-time hours worked – Burton/Chill’s fiscal year starts on May 1st).
In addition, ‘Flex Friday Summer Hours’ which includes 4 hours of Paid Time Off on Friday afternoons between Memorial Day and Labor Day each summer (these hours are pro-rated based on part-time working hours).

Other perks include a flexible working schedule, $450 USD season pass reimbursement to any mountain resort, significant Burton employee discounts on most Burton hard and soft goods, industry pro-deals with Burton and Chill’s partners, and 1 to 2 “Ride Days” annually where all staff has a paid day off to enjoy the outdoors.
In addition, Chill offers access to an employee assistance program (EAP), Partial Gym Membership, Training or Fitness Purchase Reimbursement.
New staff also receive a Chill branded Burton jacket, snowboard pants (if needed), first layer top, Chill hoodie, beanie, and trucker hat, 2 Chill t-shirts, Chill branded Burton backpack, used Burton snowboard/boots/bindings if available, Anon helmet and goggles if available, and assorted apparel & accessories throughout the year when available.

How do I apply?
Phase 1:

Submit RESUME and COVER LETTER via Burton/Chill Jobs portal
Phase 1 candidates may be asked to a screening email, form, or phone call
Phase 1 candidates may be asked to a virtual video interview with Hiring Manager
Offer to move to Phase 2 or declination of an offer to move to Phase 2 to be made by Hiring Manager at the completion of all Phase 1 candidate interviews

If moved on to Phase 2 (up to 3 candidates):

Phase 2 candidates may be asked to a 2nd interview with 1 or more members of the Programs Leadership Team
Offer or declination of an offer of the position to be made to Phase 2 candidates by Hiring Manager at the completion of all Phase 2 candidate interviews

title: Software Engineer, Senior
description:
What you’ll do
As a Senior Software Engineer at Forj, you’ll do more than write code. In this role, you’ll lead software development on cross-discipline engineering teams, be trusted to translate our client’s vision into embedded software reality, shape system software architecture, make thoughtful tradeoffs across functionality, performance, cost and maintainability – all while ensuring safety and security. You will combine hands-on technical contributions with leadership and influence – including significant autonomy in design choices and the responsibility to guide your software team through the full software development lifecycle.
Core responsibilities include:

Apply a thorough understanding of FDA regulations & IEC 62304 to bear on the safety and cybersecurity of software system designs.
Lead definition, analysis, and allocation of requirements – directly in conversation with clients and collaboration with cross-functional leads in electrical, mechanical, system, test, and quality engineering.
Provide detailed estimates in support of project milestones and software deliverables.
Apply a unique feature-focused method of breaking down software system functionality; you’ll iteratively lead your software team through architecture, design, implementation, testing and integration of software features in an agile workflow.
Provide leadership to a team of software engineers through work planning, task delegation, and coordination of execution against project milestones and budget.
Design, implement and test project source code.
Own the technical quality of all software artifacts – ensuring architectural integrity, code quality and design robustness through technical reviews, mentoring and leading by example.
Lead and support software initiatives - including process improvements and internal library contributions.

You’ll have a chance to make a meaningful impact on the lives of patients – our recent products help clinicians treat cancer, sustain life and alleviate pain.
To top it off, we think you’ll enjoy working with other smart, curious and talented engineers as you bring medical devices to life.
What you bring
We’re more interested in a balance between breadth and depth than checking every box, but helpful experience includes:

BS, MS, or equivalent degree in Computer/Software Engineering, Computer Science or similar field.
5-9+ years’ experience in embedded software development in Medical Device or other regulated industry, ideally in a lead role with a track record leading small software teams with an inspirational and effective leadership style.
The ability to communicate technical concepts clearly and build trust with clients and peers.
Significant experience with embedded Linux development on SoMs – particularly with Yocto Project/BSP and driver configuration.
C++, C#, and/or C object-oriented programming with expert-level understanding of multithreading and multi-process applications. Familiarity with common Design Patterns is a bonus!
Demonstrated proficiency in solving high-complexity software problems – including a methodical, reasoned approach to reproducing and fixing bugs.
Graphical User Interface application development, including associated design patterns (e.g. MVC, MVVM, MVP) – ideally using the Qt Framework/QML.
Microcontroller programming (ideally using ThreadX or other RTOS) including device driver development and use of debuggers, emulators, communication analyzers, oscilloscopes, and logic analyzers.
Expertise in software architecture, design and test (at the unit, integration and system levels).

How we work
Project teams are led by a Program Manager / Systems Engineer; technical leads from Software, Electrical, Mechanical, Test and Quality (to name a few) collaborate on projects for clients ranging from established companies to small startups.
We foster a strong engineering culture and operate under mature software & product development processes.
We invest in tools, automation and continuous improvement.
We work at an efficient, sustainable pace – taking time for fun along the way!

Compensation: The expected starting salary for this position is $120,000 to $150,000 depending on qualifications. As part of your overall rewards, we offer a comprehensive benefits program.

title: Lead Engineer
description:
Lead Engineer
Department: Technology
Location: Remote
FLSA Status: Exempt
People Leader: No
Travel: Less than 10%
Summary
Company Summary
Accuity partners with hospitals and health systems through a technology-enabled, physician-led model that improves clinical documentation integrity, coding accuracy, reimbursement optimization, and quality outcomes.
Job Summary
The Lead Engineer leads the design and delivery of assigned epics and initiatives within Accuity’s application engineering organization, including work across Amplifi and related products and platforms. Reporting to the Vice President, Engineering, this role operates as a player-coach, personally building a meaningful share of the work while directing the engineers who form into a pod around the initiative for its duration.
Pods form around initiatives and flex with the work rather than existing as permanent teams. The Lead Engineer is accountable for the technical design, sequencing, quality, and delivery of the initiatives they lead, and for the effectiveness of the engineers contributing to them, without carrying formal direct reports.
The Lead Engineer builds within the patterns, standards, and reference implementations set by the Technical Lead and the engineering organization, and escalates cross-cutting technical questions rather than resolving them locally in ways that diverge from the rest of the estate.
Responsibilities
Technical Delivery Leadership

  • Own the technical design and delivery of assigned epics and initiatives from requirements through production.
  • Break initiatives into workable increments, sequence them realistically, and surface dependencies and risks early.
  • Direct the day-to-day technical work of the engineers assigned to the initiative pod, without formal reporting authority.
  • Personally build a meaningful share of the work rather than only coordinating it.
  • Ensure delivered work meets the quality, security, performance, and documentation standards defined for the organization.
  • Communicate progress, blockers, risks, and tradeoffs clearly to the Vice President, Engineering.

Engineering Craft and Quality

  • Write, review, and maintain high-quality production code.
  • Uphold code review, automated test coverage, static analysis, and definition of done standards within the pod.
  • Build within the established patterns, standards, and reference implementations for the application estate, and escalate to the Technical Lead where a genuine case exists to deviate.
  • Instrument services for monitoring, alerting, and troubleshooting, and take ownership of the health of what the pod ships.
  • Identify and remediate technical debt within the areas of ownership rather than deferring it indefinitely.

Product and Platform Contribution

  • Partner with Product and business stakeholders to translate requirements into workable technical designs, surfacing feasibility, effort, and tradeoffs early.
  • Identify functionality being built repeatedly and raise it as a candidate for shared platform capability rather than solving it locally one more time.
  • Contribute to application convergence and modernization work, including migration onto the modern data foundation.
  • Support the planned retirement of components, interfaces, and internal tools that the pod’s work replaces.

Collaboration and Mentorship

  • Mentor engineers on the pod through pairing, code review, and design discussion.
  • Work with Platform Management on delivery, environment, and test needs, using shared platform capability rather than building parallel tooling.
  • Coordinate with other Lead Engineers and with the Technical Lead on shared interfaces, dependencies, and overlapping work.
  • Support the onboarding of new engineers into the codebase, the domain, and the standards they are expected to work within.

Quality, Security, and Compliance

  • Design and build to HIPAA, HITRUST, and PHI protection requirements applicable to Accuity’s applications and client environments.
  • Follow secure development practices, including vulnerability remediation and dependency management.
  • Support incident response and root cause resolution for production issues in owned areas.

Other Duties as Assigned

  • Perform additional responsibilities as needed to support engineering, technology, and organizational goals.

Qualifications
Education and Credentials

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, software engineering, or a related technical field preferred; equivalent professional experience may be considered.
  • Relevant technical certifications preferred.

Experience

title: Teaching Artist YOLA - HOLA (Clarinet)
description:
Position: Teaching Artist – Clarinet

Department: Learning – YOLA Status: Part-Time Reports to: Associate Operations Director Instrument Focus: Clarinet Primary Work Location: Heart of Los Angeles (HOLA), Los Angeles, CA FLSA Grade: Non-Exempt

About Learning at the LA Phil

Leading the LA Phil's strategic engagement with youth and education across Los Angeles, the Learning programs at the LA Phil champion the organization's investment in the larger arts ecosystem while providing thought leadership and advocacy for youth engagement program models that uplift and inspire.

About the YOLA Program

Mission Statement

YOLA provides transformational and equitable access to music education for young people from underserved communities, to support their personal development, their communities, and beyond.

The work of YOLA is focused in two areas:

Local programs, which directly serve communities across Los Angeles.

National programs, which provide opportunities for young musicians, teaching artists, program administrators, and other stakeholders to learn from and create community with one another.

YOLA Vision for Impact

By 2035, YOLA is serving well over 4,000 students across LA County. Thousands of alumni believe the transformative experience of playing music with the YOLA community contributed to their personal development, a path to excellence, and a deep and lasting love of music, motivating them to meaningfully contribute as adults to the creative industry ecosystem.

Program Summary

YOLA (Youth Orchestra Los Angeles) is LA Phil's signature education program, inspired by El Sistema and led by Gustavo Dudamel. YOLA provides over 1,700 students annually with access to instruments, high-quality music instruction, performance opportunities, and holistic support at no cost.

The work of YOLA focuses on:

Local programs serving communities across Los Angeles

National programs supporting musicians, educators, and administrators

About Heart of Los Angeles (HOLA)

Heart of Los Angeles (HOLA) provides underserved youth with exceptional programs in academics, arts, and athletics within a nurturing environment, empowering them to develop their potential, pursue their education, and strengthen their communities. HOLA's core values are Respect, Responsibility, Positive Communication, Inclusion, and Support.

As a long-standing YOLA partner site, HOLA supports students and families in the Rampart District through comprehensive youth development programming and access to high-quality music education opportunities.

Position Summary

The Clarinet Teaching Artist is a core member of YOLA's faculty, delivering high-quality, culturally responsive instruction at the Heart of Los Angeles (HOLA) site. This role includes private lessons, sectionals, ensemble rehearsals, and classroom instruction while fostering a supportive, inclusive, and student-centered musical environment.

The Teaching Artist brings strong artistic and pedagogical expertise in clarinet instruction, working with students across multiple skill levels. Instruction is primarily delivered after school during the academic year, with occasional evening and weekend rehearsals, performances, and community events.

YOLA's educational outcomes are grounded in:

Artistic Formation

Community & Life Skills

Opportunity & Access

Position Elements

Teach group classes, sectionals, private lessons, and ensemble coaching with a focus on clarinet tone production, embouchure development, breath support, articulation, finger technique, intonation, musicianship, and stylistic interpretation.

Deliver culturally responsive, sequential instruction aligned with YOLA curriculum, benchmarks, and student learning outcomes.

Develop foundational and advanced clarinet skills while fostering musical independence and ensemble awareness.

Coach students toward measurable growth through juries, assessments, rehearsals, performances, and individualized learning goals.

Support orchestra, wind ensemble, chamber ensemble, and sectional rehearsals by modeling and performing within the clarinet section as needed.

Collaborate with conductors, faculty, and curriculum leads on repertoire selection, instructional strategies, and student development.

Foster an inclusive, respectful classroom environment that builds confidence, belonging, creativity, and artistic identity.

Promote leadership, accountability, discipline, and community engagement among students.

Communicate proactively with families, site staff, and YOLA leadership regarding student progress, attendance, and engagement.

Prepare students for auditions, honor bands, honor orchestras, youth ensembles, summer programs, and other advanced musical opportunities.

Identify and address barriers to participation, access, and student success.

Participate in professional development, peer observations, training opportunities, and faculty meetings.

Uphold YOLA's Code of Conduct and professional standards at all times.

Support performances, concerts, family engagement activities, community events, and HOLA site-based programming.

Collaborate with HOLA staff and YOLA leadership to support student recruitment, retention, and overall program success.

Evaluation & Professional Growth

Set and track individualized professional goals.

Participate in coaching, feedback cycles, and cross-site learning communities.

Engage in structured evaluations including classroom observations and stakeholder feedback.

Receive support and performance benchmarks when necessary.

Incorporate feedback from observations, students, families, and leadership to continuously improve instructional practice.

Mandated Reporter & Code of Conduct

As a Teaching Artist working with minors, this role is designated as a mandated reporter under California law. Responsibilities include:

Reporting suspected child abuse or neglect.

Maintaining appropriate professional boundaries.

Supporting a safe, inclusive, and respectful environment.

Seeking guidance when concerns arise.

Shared YOLA Values

Self-Respect and Respect for Community

Safety (for Self and Community)

Curiosity

Inclusion

Collaboration

Creativity

Position Qualifications

Bachelor's degree (or equivalent experience) in Music Performance, Music Education, or a related field with a focus on clarinet.

Minimum two years of teaching experience in private lessons, classroom instruction, youth orchestras, bands, or ensemble settings.

Strong knowledge of clarinet pedagogy across beginner, intermediate, and advanced levels.

Experience working with diverse student populations and fostering equitable learning environments.

Commitment to culturally responsive, student-centered teaching practices.

Strong classroom management skills and ability to adapt instruction to varying student needs and learning styles.

Excellent communication, collaboration, organizational, and relationship-building skills.

Experience working within youth development, community music, after-school, or El Sistema-inspired programming preferred.

Bilingual Spanish/English preferred.

Equal Opportunity Employer

The Los Angeles Philharmonic Association is committed to diversity and inclusion and does not discriminate on any legally protected basis. Reasonable accommodations are provided in accordance with applicable laws, including the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and the California Fair Employment and Housing Act.

title: Director, Origination
description:
Lorval Capital Management is an established family office that provides support services (finance expertise, payroll, HR) and a strong backing to our Vancouver-based Attivo Capital brand.
Attivo Capital is a Vancouver-based commercial real estate mortgage banking and direct lending firm. We specialize in creative, solution-driven financing for commercial real estate projects, structuring, negotiating, and monitoring debt products that maximize value for borrowers, lenders, and partners alike.
Our team combines deep experience across real estate development, capital raising, funding, brokerage, and construction. We maintain strong relationships with a network of 75+ lenders (including MICs, non-bank financial institutions, banks and credit unions, private lenders, life insurance companies, and trustees) alongside relationships with Canada’s leading developers, private investors, and construction professionals. This differentiated network powers a robust and distinctive deal-flow pipeline.
Our lending focus:

Loan profile: Commercial loans with mortgage security, 1st or 2nd ranking, generally greater than $10M (smaller opportunities considered case-by-case).

Asset focus: Major asset classes (multi-family residential, industrial, and retail) with office and alternative assets (seniors housing, self-storage, student housing, hotel/gaming) considered case-by-case.

Geographic focus: Primary and secondary markets in British Columbia, Ontario, Alberta, and Quebec, in municipalities with a population greater than 100,000.

The Role
The Director, Origination drives new commercial mortgage origination and deepens our borrower, broker, and lender relationships. This is a senior, revenue-generating role for someone who already operates fluently in Canada’s commercial real estate debt market and brings an established book of relationships with developers, sponsors, brokers, and capital providers.
This role owns the front end of the deal pipeline, sourcing and qualifying opportunities, structuring indicative terms in collaboration with our underwriting and partner teams, and shepherding transactions from first conversation through to funding. The person in this role is a self-starter who thrives in an entrepreneurial, relationship-driven environment and is motivated by uncapped earning potential tied directly to the value they create.

Duties and Responsibilities
Origination and Business Development

Source, originate, and close new commercial mortgage opportunities across Attivo’s target asset classes and geographies, with a focus on loans greater than $2M.
Build and execute a territory and account plan to grow deal flow, including proactive outreach, networking, and a disciplined pipeline-management cadence.
Develop and maintain a strong personal pipeline of borrowers, developers, and real estate sponsors, converting relationships into funded transactions.
Represent Attivo at industry events, conferences, and networking forums to raise the firm’s profile and generate referrals.

Relationship Management

Cultivate and manage relationships with mortgage brokers, referral partners, developers, private investors, and intermediaries to create a recurring source of quality deal flow.
Strengthen and expand Attivo’s network of 75+ lenders (MICs, non-bank lenders, banks, credit unions, private lenders, life insurance companies, and trustees) to match opportunities with the right capital.
Act as a trusted advisor and primary point of contact for borrowers and partners throughout the transaction lifecycle, delivering a high-touch, professional client experience.

Deal Structuring & Execution

Conduct preliminary review and qualification of opportunities, assessing fit against Attivo’s lending parameters (ranking, LTV, asset class, geography, sponsor strength).
Collaborate with underwriting, credit, and partner teams to structure indicative terms, prepare term sheets, and present financing solutions to borrowers.
Negotiate terms and commitment letters, and manage the deal through due diligence, documentation, and funding in coordination with internal and external stakeholders (legal, appraisers, and lenders).
Maintain accurate records of pipeline, activity, and closed transactions in the firm’s CRM and reporting systems.

Market Intelligence & Strategy

Monitor commercial real estate, capital markets, and interest-rate trends to identify opportunities and inform Attivo’s positioning and product strategy.
Provide feedback to the Partners on market conditions, competitor activity, borrower demand, and lender appetite.
Contribute to the continuous improvement of origination processes, marketing materials, and the firm’s value proposition.

Required Qualifications

Minimum of five to seven years of experience in commercial mortgage origination, business development, or commercial real estate lending, with a demonstrated track record of sourcing and closing transactions.
An established book of relationships with developers, sponsors, brokers, and/or capital providers in Canadian commercial real estate.
Eligibility to register, or current registration, as a sub-mortgage broker with the BC Financial Services Authority (BCFSA), and/or equivalent provincial licensing (e.g., FSRA in Ontario, RECA in Alberta). Willingness to obtain required licensing in coverage provinces.
Strong understanding of commercial mortgage products, deal structuring, underwriting fundamentals, loan-to-value and debt-service metrics, and the commercial real estate capital stack.
Excellent sales, negotiation, communication, and relationship-building skills, with the credibility to engage sophisticated borrowers and institutional capital providers.
Self-motivated, entrepreneurial, and results-oriented, comfortable owning targets and working with autonomy in a fast-paced environment.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in business, finance, real estate, economics, or a related field; relevant designations (e.g., AMP, CFA, MBA) are an asset.
Experience originating loans greater than $2M and/or structured, mezzanine, bridge, or construction financing.
Familiarity with Attivo’s core markets (BC, Alberta, Ontario, Quebec) and existing relationships in those regions.
Proficiency with CRM and loan-origination tools, and comfort building and managing a pipeline against KPIs.

title: X-Ray Technologists (Medical Radiation Technologists)
description:
At Canada Diagnostic Centres, we are driven by helping Canadians access diagnostic services and providing remarkable experiences to our patients every day. Our care is compassionate, accurate and timely to help patients make progress in their health journey. We live by a mantra of “Remarkable Care. Remarkable Careers.”
We are currently looking for certified, or soon to be certified, X-Ray Technologists (Medical Radiation Technologists) to join our expanding outpatient clinics in a full-time or part-time position. Working collaboratively with radiologists and other healthcare professionals, you’ll explain procedures, position patients, adjust equipment, and capture diagnostic images. Bringing compassion and clarity to each patient interaction, you’ll help ensure remarkable care every visit.
What You’ll Be Doing

Perform X-Ray Exams: Conduct standardized and complex imaging under the direction of Radiologists and referring Physicians, while adhering to departmental protocols and guidelines.
Provide Remarkable Care: Explain exams and procedures, address questions, ease concerns, and help patients feel comfortable.
Collaborate with Clinic Teams: Partner with radiologists and other teams to help deliver a seamless and thoughtful experience.
Expand Expertise: Engage in ongoing professional development to refine existing skills, build new competencies, and cross-train in additional modalities such as Bone Mineral Density, Mammography, or specialized procedures in Fluoroscopy.
Ensure Compliance: Follow privacy, confidentiality, safety, and other regulatory requirements.
Monitor and Troubleshoot Systems: Track X-Ray equipment performance, document findings, and assist in resolving basic issues.
Prepare and Maintain Work Areas: Prepare and stock exam rooms for patient exams and procedures; report low inventory as needed.

What We’re Looking For

Professional Membership: Active registration (or eligibility) with CAMRT & ACMDTT or CSCLXT & ACCLXT.
X-Ray Experience: Clinical competency in radiography with an interest in refining and expanding skills.
Specialized Knowledge: Exposure to mammography with CAMRT Breast Imaging 1 or equivalent, is an asset. Exposure to fluoroscopy, bone mineral density or interventional X-Ray procedures is also valuable.
A Compassionate Approach: A history of remarkable care, collaboration, adaptability, and flexibility.

What We Offer

Competitive Pay: Industry-leading wages, vacation pay, and unique additional earning opportunities.
Sign-On Bonus: A welcome incentive for joining our team (terms and conditions apply).
Relocation Allowance: Financial assistance for eligible candidates to help with moving expenses.
Generous Time Off: Vacation, personal days, sick leave, and paid time off for your birthday.
Health & Wellness: Medical, dental, and vision benefits, plus access to our Employee & Family Assistance Program.
Learning & Development: Specialized training opportunities, along with an annual education allowance.
Comprehensive Onboarding: Hands-on structured training.
Long-Term Savings Program: RRSP/TFSA plan.
Parking: Convenient onsite access.
Professional Licensing Support: Funding for CAMRT and ACMDTT, or CSCLXT and ACCLXT, memberships and insurance.
Income Protection: Short-term and long-term disability coverage.
Life Insurance: Employer-paid coverage.

Additional Information

Position Types: Full-time or part-time options to align with your schedule and career goals. Part-time schedules include three or four fixed days per week, depending on FTE.
Work Location: Clinic assignments will be discussed during the candidacy process and guided by operational needs and professional development, with preferences considered where possible.
Out-of-Province Applicants: Eligibility for registration with CAMRT and ACMDTT, or CSCLXT & ACCLXT is required.
Students and Recent Graduates: Applications welcome.

About Canada Diagnostic Centres
With a network of over 43 community clinics across Alberta, Saskatchewan, Ontario, and British Columbia, we have been a leader and innovator in radiological services for more than 30 years. At the core of our work is a simple belief: Clarity Through Caring. This means diagnostic imaging that is compassionate, accessible, and grounded in quality.
In 2025, we supported more than 900,000 patients through their diagnostic journey. Our expertise spans a full range of imaging and interventional services, including MRI, CT, Ultrasound, Echocardiography, Nuclear Medicine, Mammography, X-Ray, Breast Imaging, Bone Mineral Density, Fluoroscopy, Maternal Fetal Medicine, Pediatric Imaging, Gastrointestinal Studies, and image-guided pain management procedures.
Our services are delivered by collaborative interdisciplinary teams that bring clarity through caring to life. Inspired by what our teams make possible, we create opportunities for development, provide reliable equipment, and continuously improve how care is delivered.
The care we extend to our patients and teams shapes how we welcome applicants. We actively invite applications from all individuals and are committed to equitable hiring practices. If you require accommodations at any stage of the hiring process, please contact us at talentacquisition@canadadiagnostics.ca.
Please note that only those selected for an interview will be contacted. All applicants must have legal authorization to work in Canada.

title: Vice President, Mission
description: About UsMake-A-Wish® Canada creates life-changing wishes for children with critical illnesses. We are on a quest to bring every eligible child's wish to life because a wish is an integral part of a child's treatment journey. Research shows children who have wishes granted can build the physical and emotional strength they need to fight a critical illness.Since 1983, Make-A-Wish Canada has granted over 38,500 wishes across the country, over 1,000 last year alone. As an independently operating affiliate of Make-A-Wish International, Make-A-Wish Canada is part of the network of the world’s leading children’s wish-granting organization. We serve children in every community in Canada, and in more than 50 countries worldwide.ContextIt continues to be a very exciting time at Make-A-Wish Canada! Over the past two years, we have grown wish delivery by 100%, reaching 2,011 children in 2024 with the healing power of a wish—this was more children than any previous year in the history of our organization. Despite this success, we currently have over 3,700 children currently waiting in our program, with more being referred every day. A new child is diagnosed with an eligible critical illness every two hours, and we aim to build a program where we can reach every eligible child with an impactful wish experience that improves their health outcomes.A wish is more than just a moment in time, it is a carefully curated journey designed to complement the medical journey of a child to bring them strength, confidence, and hope when they need it the most.To respond to this challenge, we are defining our next three-year strategic plan with an intentional focus on financial sustainability, mission impact, and operational efficiency. For this exciting role, the incumbent will play a formative role in driving our mission strategy in support of these goals. This will require strong leadership, innovative thinking, and commitment to carefully evolving our program to ensure our wish journey is delivering measurable impact to the health and wellness children and families in need of the transformational benefits of a wish. If this mandate excites you, please read on!Role OverviewReporting to the Chief Executive Officer, this role oversees 2 Directors directly, and 20 indirect reports. The successful candidate will have accountability for strategic planning, national mission operations, and collaboratively support execution of all mission related goals. As a member of the organization’s Senior Leadership Team, this leader will contribute nationally and collaborate across the country. Our successful candidate will demonstrate the skills and experience to lead strategically and compassionately with the overall goal of elevating the efficiency, impact and reach of our wish delivery program.This role can be based out of any of our offices in Canada, with a preference for Toronto. This is a full-time, permanent, hybrid role.What you will doMission Strategy & InnovationCollaboratively develop and execute short and long-term goals for mission delivery, maximizing the capacity, efficiency and impact of our wish program.Coordinate with Make-A-Wish International (MAWI), Make-A-Wish America (MAWA) and the global affiliate network to identify best practices which can support delivery of Make-A-Wish Canada goals.Consolidate and track overall wish granting activity and measurable KPIs nationally, including financial management of the national mission budget, and make recommendations on how to improve mission operations and delivery, optimizing reporting and analytics toward achievement of strategic goals. Facilitate innovation within the wish delivery program, inspiring engagement.Support wish granting teams related to complex wishes, enhanced medical reviews and crisis and emergency intervention.Partner with the Vice President, National Development in identifying, securing and retaining mission critical gift in kind partnerships.Wish Delivery & National Shared ServicesCoordinate with Make-A-Wish International (MAWI), Make-A-Wish America (MAWA) and the global affiliate network in development and implementation of best practices and delivery of International Wish Assists. Coach and lead the mission shared services teams including travel, wish assist, qualification and referral and alumni management/wish family engagement.Lead the design and delivery of wish programs, including group wishes, which elevate our efficiency and wish impact for high demand wish types.Develop and implement standardized training programs for new and developing wish coordinators to improve consistency, excellence, and ensuring implementation of best practices across the countryWish Impact, Inclusive Reach and Health System AlignmentSupport development of a referral partner program which cultivates and sustains relationships across the country to increase mission awareness year-over-year and drive wish referrals, aiming to enhance inclusivity beyond our present geographical and demographic reach, broadening our impact for wish children and volunteers. Lead work with the Medical Advisory Committee who provide advice and counsel to the Board and management on medical issues, as they relate to the Foundation’s principles, policies and programs.Lead development of a mission impact evaluation program including collecting and evaluating data to elevate the health impact of the wish journey and guide a formal wish research program.Monitors trends in impact measurement and evaluation to collaborate with the Medical Advisory Committee to drive a wish research agenda that enriches our wish program and strengthens donor communications. Wish Alumni ProgramSupport the Director, Wish Family Engagement in the development and execution of short- and long-term goals for wish family and alumni engagement, advancing the organization’s ability to raise money and grant wishes.Support development and oversight of all aspects of MAWC’s Wish Family Engagement and Wish Alumni Engagement Programs and end-to-end wish journey experience.Accountable for thoughtful engagement of the organization’s STARboard to engage the feedback and advice of wish alumni in organizational decision making, fundraising and ambassadorship. Support the development and execution of a comprehensive engagement program, providing a fulsome experience for wish families and wish alumni including post-wish stewardship, wish kid/wish family ambassadorship opportunities, development of a library of wish stories to support storytelling and fundraising activities, and development of fundraising opportunities for wish families. Volunteer ServicesSupport the Director, Volunteer Engagement in the development of annual and long-term strategies and business plans with an objective to grow and to enhance the volunteer experience in support of organizational objectives.Develop KPIs and measurable criteria upon which to track the success of the Volunteer Engagement program.What you bringAs the successful candidate, you are a strategic, collaborative, and inspirational leader who can influence and motivate stakeholders at all levels in the organization. You bring at least 10 years of mission delivery or social services experience in a comparable organization with strong interpersonal, written, verbal communication skills. Although not a requirement, preference will be given to candidates with experience in a multi-level not-for-profit organization. Your educational background in social work, social services, or nonprofit business equips you to lead strategically and compassionately in this role. You have the skills and experience necessary to effectively support children and families facing critical illnesses, including strong communication and problem-solving skills, along with the ability to organize information, set healthy boundaries, and navigate complex situations in a highly dynamic environment.As a leader, you are keen to empower and develop your team, engaging in clear objective setting, on-going performance feedback, recognition and coaching. You are someone with integrity and can successfully maintain confidential information.How to applyIf everything you’ve read so far sounds like you, we encourage you to apply now! The deadline to apply is May 9th, 2025, at 11:59pm ET.To apply, please navigate to: https://jobs.dayforcehcm.com/en-CA/makeawishca/CANDIDATEPORTAL/jobs/961 Make-A-Wish Canada provides equal opportunity in employment and encourages applications from all qualified candidates. Reasonable accommodations due to disability are available on request at any stage of the hiring process. Our Commitment to IDEAMake-A-Wish Canada (MAWC) is committed to Inclusion, Diversity, Equity, and Access (IDEA). We believe that it is essential to our mission that we build a diverse, balanced, and vibrant workforce that reflects the diversity of the communities we serve and seek to serve. Research has shown that candidates from underrepresented groups often only apply when they feel 100% qualified. Therefore, we ask that even if you do not see yourself fully reflected in every job requirement listed on this posting, to still apply.
