title: Specialist in Maternal Fetal Medicine
description:
Embark on a rewarding career with Canada Diagnostic Centres (CDC), a trailblazer in diagnostic imaging since 1993. As a leading provider of diagnostic services and image-guided procedures in Western Canada, we take pride in our 38 physician-led community clinic sites strategically positioned across Edmonton, Calgary, Saskatoon, rural Alberta, Saskatchewan, and Vancouver. Join our dynamic team and contribute to our comprehensive suite of services, including Ultrasound, Maternal Fetal Medicine, MRI, CT, Echocardiography, Nuclear Medicine, Mammography, X-ray, Bone Density, GI Fluoroscopy, image-guided biopsies, and state-of-the-art pain management procedures.
Canada Diagnostic Center (CDC) is inviting applications for one part-time clinical sub-specialist position in Maternal-Fetal Medicine (MFM) to our community-based Maternal Fetal Medicine clinic in Calgary, Alberta, a vibrant quickly growing city close to Banff and the Rocky Mountains with affordable housing and excellent international air service.
The CDC Maternal Fetal Medicine unit is an integrated outpatient consultative and ultrasound program which offers care to patients in Calgary through our Pacific Place clinic. The CDC MFM service is led by our Maternal Fetal Medicine Specialists and focuses on fetal diagnosis, assessment, and surveillance via specialized MFM ultrasounds as well as planning assessment and management of complicated pregnancies in collaboration with obstetricians, radiologists, family physicians, midwives, prenatal genetics, pediatric surgeons, pediatric urologists, neonatologists, and other specialties. Care is provided to patients in a collaborative and patient focused model with experienced registered nurses and diagnostic medical sonographers.
We have an immediate need for an MFM specialist one day per week in this setting. We would like to grow the practice further with the successful applicant.
What You’ll Be Doing

Ultrasound diagnosis
Ultrasound fetal assessment
Fetal surveillance
Assessment of complicated pregnancies
Work in collaboration with obstetricians, family physicians, radiologists, midwives, prenatal genetics, pediatric surgeons, pediatric urologists, neonatologists, and other providers
Sonographer, radiologists, and/or resident education

What We’re Looking For

Certification in Obstetrics and Gynecology with the Royal College of Physicians of Canada
Applicable Subspecialty Certification with the Royal College in Maternal Fetal Medicine
Eligible for licensure with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Alberta
Strong ultrasound skills expected.

What We Offer

One day per week flexibility to start with (open to increase)
Outpatient clinic based: no weekends or nights
No on-call work
Flexible start date
Flexible vacation
Remuneration for this position is provided as a fixed percentage of your fee for service billing.

Canada Diagnostic Centres is committed to attracting and developing a diverse and inclusive workforce. While we encourage all applicants to apply, only those selected for an interview will be contacted. Applicants must be legally entitled to work in Canada.
We are a contracted provider of services to Workers' Compensation Board Alberta and contribute to numerous charitable organizations in the communities we serve.

The LA Phil is many things—an orchestra, a collection of venues, a youth education program—all with one core belief: That everyone should have access to experience the power of live music. The Los Angeles Philharmonic and YOLA

Programs, initiatives, and extensions

The Digital team at the LA Phil leads the strategy and execution for the organization's digital presence—including laphil.com, hollywoodbowl.com, theford.com, mobile apps, email communications, and more. We collaborate across departments to create impactful digital experiences and campaigns that reflect every aspect of the LA Phil, including over 300 events programmed each year. We also manage special digital projects and provide technical guidance for analytics and innovation.

Position Summary:
The Digital Content Coordinator supports content execution across our websites and apps, with a focus on informational website pages and app content. Reporting to the Senior Manager, Digital Marketing, this role is ideal for someone organized, communicative, proactive, detail-oriented, and passionate about web design and layout, digital marketing, content management, and technology. A good handle on content management systems (CMS) and best practices, website layout (UI/UX), web technologies, and marketing is required. You’ll work across multiple platforms and systems, collaborate with various teams, and make a tangible impact on our brand, concert sales, digital campaigns, and more—while gaining hands-on experience in digital marketing, content management, and process optimization.

Position Elements:

Website Content Management: Build, maintain, update, and design informational and blog pages across our websites (700+ pages) within our CMS, ensuring content is accurate, on-brand, up-to-date, and well-structured within the page layout.
Stakeholder Collaboration & Request Traffic: Serve as a point of contact for stakeholders across the organization requesting website page edits and builds—managing intake, prioritization, timelines, and communication from request through to publish.

Process Optimization: Streamline, improve, and create new documentation processes across teams to enhance efficiency.
Visual Quality Assurance: Conduct regular QA checks to ensure content displays correctly across different browsers and devices.
Other Duties as Assigned: Participate in a team culture of supporting one another by being trained in duties outside of your day-to-day as a backup when team members are out, or bandwidth and priorities shift temporarily. Backup duties include email production and digital tools and systems.

Relationships:

Interacts With: Marketing, Learning, Philanthropy, and other department stakeholders

1-2 years experience with CMS platforms, basic HTML/CSS
1-2 years of experience in digital content, web management, performing arts, a digital agency, or marketing/communications

Strong attention to detail and organizational skills
Self-starter with a proactive mindset
Strong verbal and written communication skills
Comfortable managing multiple projects and deadlines
Collaborative and team-oriented

title: Campaign Fundraising Specialist - Visionaries of the Year - Fresno
description:
How many people can answer the question, "What do you do for a living?" with the answer, "I help find cures for cancer." At Blood Cancer United, employees take our mission seriously. Whether you work in one of our regions, are an accountant at the national office or a specialist in our Information Resource Center, you work each day on making our bold goal a reality: to enable patients with blood cancer to gain more than one million years of life by 2040. Join us and give new meaning to the word, "job."
Summary: Blood Cancer United is a mission centric, locally delivered and nationally powered organization, relentlessly pursuing cancer cures. To help achieve this mission, this role is responsible for logistics, data management and coordination for Blood Cancer United designated market and peer-to-peer fundraising products to exceed revenue goals for Blood Cancer United mission, within a designated market area.

Core Responsibilities/ Primary Duties

Mission Integration

Partner with Education, Services and Health Research department to effectively communicate the Blood Cancer United overall mission, programs, resources, and priorities.

Event Logistics

Act as an on-site manager during the campaign fundraising event, overseeing activities, staff, vendors, and volunteers to ensure satisfaction of participants, and resolutions of problems.
Oversee logistics, timelines, and other operational elements for assigned fundraising campaigns.
Provide input into the development of a strategic plan for the peer-to-peer fundraising products, including revenue, budget, goals, and timelines.
Responsible for managing expense budgets as related to logistics.
Research and recommend event venues and location sites based on campaign standards and in coordination with National Shared Services, Logistics Team.

Volunteer Development

Responsible for assigned peer-to-peer fundraising teams to achieve overall revenue goals.
Works in conjunction with Volunteer Coordinator and collaborate with local relationship team and national shared service partners throughout Blood Cancer United.

Data Management

Manage data entry to ensure CRM and fundraising systems are accurate. Update systems in a timely manner. Provides reports to fundraising relationship team as needed.
Connect with vendors to secure the best rate or in-kind donation of services as needed.

#LI-HybridMinimum Requirements

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience
2 - 4 years’ experience in a related role

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Incumbents are expected to demonstrate a solid understanding of business processes and apply resources efficiently.
Works under moderate supervision, demonstrating the ability to manage some project work, and may be responsible for fundraising activities.
Work typically requires interpretation or deviation from standard procedures and involves communicating complex information.
Successfully demonstrates the following:

Knowledge of MS Office Suite
Use of digital and social media
Collaboration skills
Strong written and verbal communications skills
Ability to supervise and lead a group of volunteers
Ability to manage multiple priorities and timelines effectively

Work Environment & Physical Demands

Physical demands are minimal and typical of similar jobs in comparable organizations.
Work environment is representative and typical of similar jobs in comparable organizations.
May be required to move Campaign materials weighing up to 15 pounds for various events.
Travel within designated area.
Required to work some evenings or weekends.

Employee Value Proposition:As a valued member of Blood Cancer United, you are eligible for a comprehensive benefits package. Our offerings include medical, dental, and vision insurance; life insurance; flexible spending accounts; a 403b retirement plan along with generous paid time off. In addition, we observe federal paid holidays throughout the year, and offer a wellness program and an employee assistance program.We are excited to share the base pay range for this hourly paid, non-exempt position is $28/hr ($51K/yr) to $31/hr ($58K/yr). The offered compensation may vary based on factors such as geographic location, business need, market conditions, proficiencies, skills, education, and experience. Additionally, at Blood Cancer United we place a high value on internal pay equity and will consider the current compensation of similarly situated roles and direct team members. Base compensation is only one component of our Total Rewards program, which also includes an annual incentive plan and a competitive benefits package.
The statements herein are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees, and are not to be construed as an exhaustive list of responsibilities, duties, and skills required of employees. Furthermore, they do not establish a contract for employment and are subject to change at the discretion of the Company. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Disclaimer
Blood Cancer United is an equal employment opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion in its workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender, gender identity and expression (including transgender status), sexual orientation, pregnancy, age, race, color, creed, national origin/ancestry, citizenship, religion, genetic predisposition or information, physical or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Blood Cancer United seeks such skilled and qualified individuals to share our mission and where they will join a cohort of others who have chosen to call Blood Cancer United home. Blood Cancer United complies with all applicable laws which prohibit discrimination and harassment in the workplace, and is committed to maintaining a diverse and inclusive environment supportive of all of our employees and the communities we serve.

title: Call Management Associate
description:

Work with the District Managers in assigned region to understand technician and overall region objectives and desired targets/results for technician efficiency and customer satisfaction. Perform call management functions to contribute to these overall objectives and targets.

Team centered / work well with co-workers to resolve issues and problems.

Analysis and problem solving.

Punctual and reliable.

Multi-tasking.

Attention to detail.

Initiative.

This is largely a sedentary role, requiring use of typical office equipment such as computer, laptop, and cell phone.

Office position.

Effective use of Microsoft applications including Windows, Outlook, Excel, and Word.

title: Game Production Instructor (Sessional Faculty)
description:
Position Summary
LaSalle College Vancouver is seeking a Game Production Instructor with significant industry experience in game development to lead senior-level production and post-production courses. These courses represent the culmination of the program, where students work in multidisciplinary teams to deliver a fully realized game project.

The ideal candidate has first-hand experience shipping games or working through full production cycles and is comfortable mentoring teams through scope management, agile workflows, milestone delivery, QA, polish, and release preparation. They understand the realities of production pressure, cross-disciplinary collaboration, and iterative development—and can translate that experience into structured academic guidance.

This role requires a coach-mentor mindset rather than traditional lecture delivery. The instructor acts as a studio lead, providing direction, feedback, accountability, and professional expectations while allowing students to take ownership of their projects.

Teaching Scope
The successful candidate may teach one or more of the following senior courses:

Pre-production– Concept development, design definition, technical planning, and setting up the pipeline
Production Team I – Initial production phase and playable build
Production Team II – Continued production, iteration, QA, and polish
Post-production – Feature lock, optimization, post-mortem, and release preparation

Key Responsibilities
Teaching & Studio Leadership

Teach a minimum of one and a maximum of five sections* per term, as assigned by the Program Director and/or Chief Academic Officer (Sections are subject to change)
Lead student teams through a studio-style production pipeline, from planning to shipped build
Facilitate weekly sprint cycles, including:
Sprint planning
Task estimation and assignment
Sprint reviews and retrospectives
Milestone and feature-lock enforcement
Guide students in:
Scope definition and management
Time and resource planning
Cross-disciplinary collaboration (programming, art, audio, design)
Risk identification and mitigation
Review and provide feedback on:
Playable builds and weekly submissions
Production documentation (TDDs, design documents, art bibles, sprint reports)
QA plans and testing results
Enforce professional production standards, including:
Version control discipline
Build stability and submission requirements
Naming, organization, and documentation practices
Support post-production activities such as:
Feature lock and stabilization
Bug fixing and optimization
Post-mortem analysis
Marketing materials and presentation preparation
Provide clear, actionable feedback while holding students accountable to deadlines and quality expectations
Maintain accurate grading, attendance, and progress tracking

Student Mentorship

Mentor students transitioning from academic exercises to professional production workflows
Model professional studio behavior, communication, and accountability
Support teams through conflict resolution, prioritization challenges, and production setbacks
Prepare students for industry expectations, including:

Team roles and responsibilities
Production pacing and iteration
Portfolio and showcase readiness

Key Relationships

Chief Academic Officer
Program Director / Program Lead / Program Coordinator
Academic Advisors
Faculty
Students

Required Qualifications

Master’s degree in computer science, Software Engineering, Game Programming, or a related field, or equivalent industry experience
5+ years of professional experience in the game industry or interactive media production
Demonstrated experience working through full game development cycles, from concept to release
Strong understanding of:

Agile and Scrum methodologies
Game production pipelines
Cross-disciplinary team collaboration
Scope, scheduling, and milestone management

Experience working with Unity and/or Unreal Engine in a production context
Ability to mentor, guide, and evaluate team-based student projects
Strong communication and leadership skills

Note: International academic credentials will only be accepted if accompanied by a WES assessment or an equivalent evaluation. Any costs associated with obtaining this assessment are the candidate’s responsibility, and the evaluation must be completed prior to the official hiring date.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience shipping one or more commercial or publicly released games
Prior experience in a leadership role (Producer, Lead Developer, Technical Director, or similar)
Teaching, coaching, or mentorship experience in an academic or studio setting
Familiarity with QA processes, post-mortem practices, and portfolio development

All employees at LaSalle College Vancouver are defined by key attributes which we value. These attributes are: action oriented, innovative/creative, resourceful, respects peoples’ individuality and differences, engaging/effective communicator, committed to sharing knowledge and best practices, have a global perspective, embraces change, client/customer focused, and resilient.
Equity and diversity are vital to achieving academic excellence. A welcoming and inclusive community helps amplify voices that have historically been underrepresented or silenced. We actively encourage applications from individuals belonging to groups that have experienced marginalization, as outlined in the B.C. Human Rights Code. This includes, but is not limited to, individuals based on sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, racialization, disability, political belief, religion, marital or family status, age, and/or identity as a First Nations, Métis, Inuit, or other Indigenous person.
If you, or someone in your network, is interested in pursuing these exciting career opportunities, please submit a PDF compatible resume along with a cover letter that contains the expectations.
We would like to take this opportunity to thank all applicants in advance but only those applicants who meet the specific job requirements will be contacted.

title: MRO Buyer
description:
About the company:
Viant is a global medical device partner providing design, development, manufacturing, and assembly services through capabilities in materials, plastics, metals, extrusion, and automation. With nearly 6,000 employees across 24 locations worldwide, it delivers high-quality, life-enhancing products with the scale and expertise to bring devices to market efficiently. Learn more at Viant Medical’s website or on LinkedIn.

Benefits (Eligible for benefits effective date of hire!)

Medical, dental, and vision benefits
Company-paid life insurance and disability benefits
Generous Paid time off and 10 paid Holidays
401k Plan with Company Match
Tuition Reimbursement
Voluntary Universal Life and Long-Term Care
Voluntary Legal Plan
Pet Insurance

About the site:
Our Wheeling facility combines precision machining and assembly capabilities to deliver high-quality medical device components and finished products.

About the role:
Schedules, orders and coordinates the delivery of materials, equipment and services used in support of Viant sites and product manufacturing according to production plans. Controls the management of assigned MRO items in support of site requirements and in accordance with management objectives. Expedites requirements as needed (e.g., order action, open orders, late order reports). Negotiates purchase price, establishes delivery dates and payment terms for approval by management. Assist in the selection of particular vendors/suppliers with whom to place orders and acts as primary contact with vendors/suppliers. Resolves problems with assigned suppliers, materials, equipment or service orders. As a cross-functional team member, represents supply base and takes actions necessary to support quoting, production, cost savings initiatives, quality/complaint investigations and other supply chain related activities.

Work Model: Monday – Friday, 100% onsite 8:00 AM

We offer market competitive compensation. Potential salary range for this role is $65k-$82k. Actual pay will be determined based on experience, qualifications, geographic location, and other job-related factors permitted by law.

What you'll do:

Prepare instructions and oversee purchasing systems and procedures; reviews purchase order claims and contracts for conformance to company policy.
Responsible for tactical procurement in support of the sites’ production schedules, as well as purchase order releases on blanket agreements negotiated with the Viant Global Sourcing team.
Prepares management reports as required (Procurement Spend analysis/cost savings program; material and services cost reduction tracking, etc.); Tracks and updates operating/expense budget.

Procures all materials and services to necessary dock dates to ensure on-time support of site requirements
Ensures purchase orders are properly managed to insure on time delivery and proper supplier relationship management both internally and externally.
Works with Global Sourcing to develop cost reduction programs with suppliers to ensure an annual reduction is achieved per facility objectives for both common Viant materials and services working with Global Sourcing as well as indirect spend activities.
Timely sourcing and cost-effective procurement of MRO items factory/office supplies, as well as outside services.
Analyzes contractual commitments, customer specifications, design changes, and other data to plan and develop planning and procurement activities from conceptual stage through life cycle of product.

Responsible for site procurement activities (services as well as expense items).
Managing and maintaining supplier programs, including the implementation of Vendor Managed Inventory for MRO items, Blanket Purchase Orders for high volume MRO & Service Items.
Global Sourcing – actively participates with Viant Global Sourcing Commodity Management team on Strategic Supplier partnerships and agreements in support of Viant Strategic Goals.
Participates with Strategic Sourcing Commodity management on Supplier Relationship Management (SRM quarterly / bi-annual reviews with key suppliers for the site, as well as participates in Global Sourcing SRM meetings as required.
Supplier Performance Management – responsible for working with site personnel and global sourcing on supplier report cards to ensure that plans of action are developed and implemented for improving poor performing suppliers.
In support of global procurement objectives, develop supplier programs to ensure necessary materials / services are on site.

Responsible for assisting and in development implementation/maintenance of Lean Manufacturing initiatives, including Kanban/Pull systems with vendors and production for MRO items.
Participates in cross-functional teams chartered to perform Global Strategic Sourcing related continual improvement and/or problem solving.

Requirements
Education/Certification:

Associate’s degree required; Bachelor’s degree preferred
Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office applications (Excel, Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint)
APICS Certification preferred
Strong sales, service, and customer relationship management acumen
1–3 years of relevant customer operations, customer service, or order management experience, preferably in a manufacturing or regulated environment
Oracle or similar ERP system experience preferred

Skills/Competencies

Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to communicate effectively within all levels of the organization
Conflict management and the ability to negotiate
Organized and the ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities
Highest ethical standards and professional integrity
Demonstrated decision making skills
Hands on, collaborative, decisive self-starter, team oriented
Effective presentation skills and able to deliver insightful messages to external and internal audiences
Ability to effectively communicate with suppliers and internal business partners
Must be able to handle multiple tasks/projects and manage priorities accordingly
Instills a sense of urgency and drives problems towards resolution
Excellent written, oral and presentations skills
Computer literacy in Microsoft WORD, EXCEL and POWER POINT

Viant provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, marital status, amnesty, or status as a covered veteran in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws. Viant complies with applicable state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment in every location in which the company has facilities.

title: Communications Specialist
description: "The best prescription I've ever given is a wish."-Dr. Jeremy Friedman, Associate Paediatrician-in-Chief, SickKids Hospital & Medical Advisor for Make-A-Wish® Canada WHAT IS YOUR BIGGEST WISH?Is it to be part of an organization that is child-focused, values employee experience and is an inspiring workplace? If so, Make-A-Wish is for you!Make-A-Wish® Canada creates life-changing wishes for children with critical illnesses. We are on a quest to bring every eligible child's wish to life because a wish is an integral part of a child's treatment journey. Research shows children who have wishes granted can build the physical and emotional strength they need to fight a critical illness.“It’s been wonderful to have this wish to look forward to... It’s wonderful to see [Rowan] with something that brings him pure joy after all he’s been through and missed out on!” –Melissa, mom to wish kid Rowan (age 5, leukemia), who wished for an indoor jungle gym.MISSION, VISION AND VALUESOur mission is, together, we create life-changing wishes for children with critical illness. Supported by our vision to grant the wish of every eligible child. Our values are Child-Focused, Integrity, Impact, Innovation, and Community.WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU?Meaningful opportunities to make an impact and change the lives of children with critical illnesses within your community and across CanadaA collaborative team environment where you feel valued and inspiredAn attractive compensation package that includes group health and dental premiums which are fully covered by the Foundation, RRSP, & Wish paid hoursAnnual vacation starting at three weeks & additional paid leavesWork/life balance and flexibilityHybrid working environmentEmployee Wellness ProgramCorporate discountsContinuous learning, development and internal training opportunitiesFun employee activities, contests, and more!Make-A-Wish® Canada is committed to fostering a culture that aims to change lives while offering a rewarding employment experience where your contributions make a true difference every day!WHERE YOU COME IN We are looking for a Communications Specialist to join our team at Make-A-Wish Canada. Reporting to the Sr Manager of Influence & Engagement, in this role you will play a vital role in enhancing the organization’s visibility and engagement through strategic communication initiatives and media relations, with a focus on growing brand awareness in the Southern Alberta and Saskatchewan chapters. This position is responsible for developing and executing comprehensive communication plans, as well as managing media relations and content development strategies for various fundraising events and initiatives, ensuring consistency of message and brand and directly contributing to raising funds. This role is based out of Calgary and is a full-time, permanent, hybrid position.WHAT YOU WILL DO EVENT COMMUNICATIONS SUPPORT:Develop and execute strategic communication plans, including key messaging, media outreach materials and social media calendars/metrics for national signature events and regional events, with support to select third-party fundraising initiatives.Review fundraising event materials for brand compliance.Prepare regional crisis communications and issues management plans where relevant and co-lead reactive media statements.Act as a media liaison at events and spokesperson where appropriate.Support event content creation and/or source, coordinate, and handle photographer and videographer vendors for regional events/wishes where appropriate.Liaise with and prepare wish families for event participation as required.MEDIA RELATIONS:Develop and manage relationships with media outlets, identify local editorial media opportunities, solicit paid, discounted or gratis awareness and fundraising advertising from media partners in the community, in conjunction with, and support of national media relations activities.Use Meltwater to create media lists, disseminate media releases, monitor and evaluate coverage, and prepare reports for internal distribution.Coordinate and prepare stakeholders for media interviews, prepare a briefing document with key messages. CONTENT DEVELOPMENT AND MANAGEMENT:Create and manage content for regional initiatives for all local channels.Participate in social media editorial meetings, providing social media metrics. Create engaging wish stories and oversee volunteer and freelance writers. Partner with select influencers and content creators to support local/regional initiatives in compliance with the national influencer strategy.Manage, organize, and maintain video, story and photo archive and other communications materials for internal and external use. GENERAL:Develop new avenues for awareness initiatives within the region(s). Oversee the training and management of seasonal interns.Collaborate with development and mission staff, volunteers, and committees.Other duties as assigned.WHAT YOU BRINGDegree or diploma in communications, marketing, public relations, or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience.3-5 years of work experience in communications or related roles.Proven ability to generate media coverage, and the ability to be persistent in approaching and communicating with the media and the public.Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build solid relationships with journalists, internal stakeholders, external stakeholders, wish families, and more.Experience writing communications plans, strategies and tactics.Attention to detail and accuracy, including strong proofreading skills.Strategic thinker with strong organizational and project management skills, capable of working independently to deadlines.Proficiency in MS Office, social media content creation and community management. Canva, Meltwater, Salesforce, and Dropbox proficiency, an asset.Bilingual in French and English is an asset.Experience in supporting fundraising professionals, and experience in issues management in relation to public relations and brand image, an asset.A commitment to and passion for children’s health and charitable work. Understanding the nonprofit landscape is an asset. A clear Criminal Background Check will be required.YOUR WORK ENVIRONMENT Hybrid work environment (2 days in-office, 3 days remote per week) with occasional requirements to work outside of regular office hours.Occasional regional travel required for meetings with media outlets and attendance at first-party events several times per year.Physical/Mental EffortWork under pressure with multiple tight deadlines, demands, high volume workload, and dynamic/overlapping priorities.May be subjective to sensitive situations regarding wish children and families.How to applyIf everything you’ve read so far sounds like you, we encourage you to apply now! The deadline to apply is October 14th, 2025, at 11:59pm ET.To apply, please navigate to: https://jobs.dayforcehcm.com/en-CA/makeawishca/CANDIDATEPORTAL/jobs/1152 Make-A-Wish Canada provides equal opportunity in employment and encourages applications from all qualified candidates. Reasonable accommodations due to disability are available on request at any stage of the hiring process. Our Commitment to IDEAMake-A-Wish Canada (MAWC) is committed to Inclusion, Diversity, Equity, and Access (IDEA). We believe that it is essential to our mission that we build a diverse, balanced, and vibrant workforce that reflects the diversity of the communities we serve and seek to serve. Research has shown that candidates from underrepresented groups often only apply when they feel 100% qualified. Therefore, we ask that even if you do not see yourself fully reflected in every job requirement listed on this posting, to still apply.Recruitment processOur recruitment process is swift in pace. Once applications are reviewed, we will contact our shortlisted candidates. Our typical process includes a phone screen, one or two interviews, and reference checking, followed by an offer and a criminal background check for the successful candidate.We would like to thank all applicants for their interest in working with us!ABOUT MAKE-A-WISH® CANADASince 1983, Make-A-Wish Canada has granted over 40,000 wishes across the country, over 2000 last year alone. As an independently operating affiliate of Make-A-Wish International, Make-A-Wish Canada is part of the network of the world’s leading children’s wish-granting organization. We serve children in every community in Canada, and in more than 50 countries worldwide.JOIN OUR ONLINE COMMUNITYFor more information on how you can support Make-A-Wish® Canada or get involved please visit our website at makeawish.ca.

title: Optometric Technician
description:

description:

title: SAFETY COORDINATOR C
description:
TITLE: Safety Coordinator C

POSITION OBJECTIVE: The primary function of this position is to engage and guide plant personnel in continued safe work practices. This role will lead activities with the primary focus on improving safety within the facility including production, maintenance and shipping areas. The employee will work to develop, implement and train employees on safe practices.

QUALIFICATIONS:

High School Diploma or equivalent required.
Ability to communicate with employees and management at all levels.
Computer skills, Excel, Word, PowerPoint.
Good interpersonal skills.
Ensure consistent, dependable attendance and demonstrate a willingness to accommodate non-standard work hours as necessary
Capable of effectively managing job-related stress and fostering productive workplace interactions

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:

Generate Personnel Injury Report.
Generate Accident Investigation when needed.
Conduct and maintain monthly inspections and records.
Train and test all CFP employees according to the Annual Safety Training schedule.
Maintain OSHA 300 Log.
Handle all environmental issues pertaining to CFP/Cast Film Plant.
Implement the machine-guarding program by checking specific line features and their safeguarding.
Conduct routine Safety & Health inspections in CFP/Cast Film Plant.
Issue Safety violations when necessary.
Maintain MADS records.
Team participation in ISO Audits.
Keep plant safety rules updated.
Issue flame, hot work and construction permits when necessary.
Work closely with all CFP personnel to continue having a safe working atmosphere.

title: Business Analyst
description:
About the Job

The Business Analyst at IntouchCX plays a critical role in transforming operational and client data into actionable insights that drive decision-making across Operations, Quality, Training, and Client-facing teams.

This role is highly analytical and insight-driven, with a strong emphasis on data exploration, metric design, trend analysis, and storytelling through data. The Business Analyst partners closely with Operations leaders and internal stakeholders to understand business questions, analyze complex datasets, and clearly explain what is happening, why it is happening, and what actions should be taken.

Unlike traditional project-focused BA roles, this position is not centered on project coordination or heavy documentation, but rather on hands-on data analysis, insight generation, and analytical support to the business.

As a Business Analyst, You Will…

Analyze large and complex operational, quality, and performance datasets to identify trends, risks, and opportunities.

Design, calculate, and maintain key performance metrics aligned with business and client objectives.

Use data to explain the root causes behind operational issues and performance changes.

Support ad-hoc and recurring analytical requests from Operations, Quality, Training, and Client teams to uncover patterns, anomalies, and drivers of performance.

Partner with stakeholders to translate business questions into analytical approaches

Design and develop dashboards and reports using BI tools (Looker Studio).

Ensure reports are intuitive, accurate, and focused on driving decisions rather than just displaying data.

Continuously improve existing dashboards by refining metrics, visual design, and clarity.

Support the operationalization of insights by tailoring outputs to different audiences.

Act as a thought partner to Operations by proactively identifying insight opportunities within available data.

Provide clear, concise explanations of analytical findings to non-technical stakeholders.

Support business reviews, performance deep dives, and client-specific analyses.

Collaborate with other teams to align data definitions and analytical approaches.

Clean, transform, and validate raw data from multiple sources to ensure analytical accuracy.

Identify opportunities to combine and “slice & dice” multiple data sources for deeper insights.

Work with incomplete or imperfect data, applying sound analytical judgment and clear assumptions.

As a Business Analyst, You Need…

Bachelor’s degree (or higher) in Mathematics, Statistics, Engineering, Finance, Business Analytics, Data Science, or a related quantitative field.

3+ years of experience in a Business Analyst, Data Analyst, or Business Intelligence role.

Experience working with operational or performance data in fast-paced environments is strongly preferred.

Strong experience in data analysis, including data cleaning, transformation, and interpretation.

Solid understanding of statistical concepts and their practical application in business analysis.

Proficiency in SQL; experience with BigQuery is highly preferred.

Hands-on experience with BI tools such as Looker Studio

Experience using Python for data analysis and data visualization.

Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.

Ability to translate complex analyses into clear, business-oriented narratives.

Comfortable presenting insights through charts, dashboards, and executive-ready summaries.

Strong visual sense for creating clear and compelling analytical outputs.

TITLE: Slitter Operator C

POSITION OBJECTIVE: Machine Operators are critical members of our team. They set up, operate, and tend machines that extrude and coat flat films from synthetic materials.
In this position you will set up and operate production equipment including blown film extruders, silicone coaters, and slitter/rewinders. You will work both independently and with a team to meet and exceed customers’ specifications and timeframes.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Operation Monitoring - Watching gauges, dials, or other indicators to make sure a machine is working properly.
Operations -Controlling operations of equipment or systems.
Controls -The ability to adjust the controls of a machine or a vehicle to precise positions.
Ability to Detect Problem -The ability to tell when something is wrong or is likely to go wrong. It does not involve solving the problem, only recognizing there is a problem.
Able to work holidays.
Eligible to work in the U.S.
Be familiar with rulers, scales, gauges, and other measurement tools.
Problem Solving - Identifying problems and reviewing related information to troubleshoot or to alert supervisor.
Coordination - The ability of fingers of one or both hands to grasp, manipulate, or assemble very small objects.

Ensure consistent, dependable attendance and demonstrate a willingness to accommodate non-standard work hours as necessary.

Capable of effectively managing job-related stress and fostering productive workplace interactions

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:

Set up, operate, or tend machines such as rewind/slitter, and auxiliary equipment to convert flat films.
Observe machine operations, control boards, and gauges to detect malfunctions such as roll quality, silicone continuity and dimensional tolerances. Adjust machine controls, tensions, and operational parameters as necessary.
Load materials into extruding and coating machines, by proper weighing, and adjust feed mechanisms to set feed rates.
Follow Standard Operating Procedures to determine correct film production parameters and quality specifications. Record details of machine malfunctions.
Keep machinery and work area clean. Wipe finish rollers with cloths and wash finish trays with solvent when necessary.
Ensure quality of film and raw materials meets and exceeds customer and company standards with training in a lab as a QA tester.

OTHER INFORMATION:

After offer is accepted, background check and drug screen are required.
Retention bonus $1250
Offers employees a paid apprenticeship

Able to stand, bend, squat, lift up to 30-50 pounds.

description:

description:
HVAC Ductwork, HVAC Piping & Plumbing Quality Control Representative
Position Overview
Yearout Mechanical is seeking an experienced HVAC Ductwork, HVAC Piping & Plumbing Quality Control Representative to support mechanical construction projects. This role is responsible for ensuring HVAC, piping, plumbing, and related mechanical systems are installed in accordance with contract documents, project specifications, applicable codes, manufacturer requirements, and company quality standards.
The Quality Control Representative serves as the primary quality resource for assigned projects, performing inspections, coordinating testing and commissioning activities, reviewing technical documentation, and proactively identifying and resolving quality issues. This position works closely with project management, field personnel, owners, architects, engineers, inspectors, and general contractors to support successful project delivery.
Key Responsibilities
Quality Control & Inspections

Develop and implement project-specific Quality Control Plans.
Review drawings, specifications, submittals, RFIs, and contract documents to identify quality requirements.
Conduct field inspections of HVAC ductwork, mechanical piping, plumbing systems, equipment installations, supports, seismic bracing, firestopping, and related mechanical work.
Verify compliance with project specifications, approved submittals, manufacturer requirements, company standards, and applicable codes.
Identify deficiencies and ensure corrective actions are completed.

Testing, Commissioning & Documentation

Coordinate and witness testing and commissioning activities, including pressure testing, duct leakage testing, TAB, start-up, and functional performance testing.
Maintain inspection logs, testing records, deficiency logs, and daily quality reports.
Document findings through written reports and photographs.
Support project closeout activities and turnover documentation.

Project Coordination

Collaborate with Project Managers, Engineers, Superintendents, Foremen, Owners, Architects, Engineers, Contractors, and Commissioning Agents.
Review shop drawings, fabrication drawings, BIM models, submittals, RFIs, and as-built documentation.
Participate in coordination meetings and support resolution of quality concerns throughout project execution.

Continuous Improvement

Identify recurring quality issues and recommend process improvements.
Support development of company quality standards and installation best practices.
Assist with quality training and mentoring of field personnel.

Desired Skills and Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Mechanical Engineering, Engineering Technology, or a related field preferred, or equivalent industry experience.
OSHA 30-Hour Certification preferred.
7+ years of commercial or industrial mechanical construction experience.
3+ years in a Quality Control, Quality Assurance, or field leadership role.
Experience with healthcare, laboratory, industrial, manufacturing, mission-critical, or similar complex facilities preferred.

Technical Knowledge
Strong understanding of:

HVAC systems and air distribution
Mechanical piping systems
Plumbing systems
Equipment installation and commissioning
Construction drawings and specifications
Industry codes and standards, including IMC, IPC, IBC, SMACNA, ASHRAE, NFPA, and OSHA requirements

Software Skills
Experience with:

Procore
Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC)/BIM 360
Bluebeam Revu
Microsoft Office Suite
Microsoft Teams

Professional Skills

Strong communication and interpersonal skills
Excellent organizational and documentation abilities
Attention to detail and problem-solving skills
Ability to read and interpret construction drawings and specifications
Root cause analysis and conflict resolution abilities
Ability to work independently and collaboratively in fast-paced construction environments

Additional Notes
This position requires frequent work on active construction sites and the ability to walk sites, climb ladders, work in varying weather conditions, and wear required PPE.

Performance may be measured by:

First-time inspection pass rates
Reduced punch list and rework items

Successful testing and commissioning outcomes

On-time project turnover

title: Systems Administrator
description:
Systems Administrator
Department: Technology
Location: Remote
FLSA Status: Exempt
People Leader: No
Travel: Up to 10%
Summary
Company Summary
Accuity partners with hospitals and health systems through a technology-enabled, physician-led model that improves clinical documentation integrity, coding accuracy, reimbursement optimization, and quality outcomes.
Job Summary
The Systems Administrator is responsible for the day-to-day operation and support of Accuity’s enterprise IT environment. Reporting to the Manager, IT Operations, this role is the primary hands-on owner of employee technology support, account and access administration, endpoint management, and routine systems maintenance for a fully remote workforce.
This role works alongside Accuity’s managed service provider as the internal point of contact who triages incoming issues, routes and escalates work appropriately, and follows provider work through to resolution rather than duplicating it. It is the first line of support for employees and the day-to-day execution layer beneath the Manager, IT Operations.
Because Accuity operates in a HIPAA and HITRUST regulated environment, the Systems Administrator works within defined security and compliance controls at all times, particularly around identity, access, endpoint configuration, and evidence of the work performed.
Responsibilities
End User Support and Service Delivery

  • Serve as the primary internal point of contact for employee technology support, including intake, triage, prioritization, and resolution or escalation.
  • Resolve common issues such as password resets, multifactor authentication enrollment and recovery, account lockouts, mailbox and file access, connectivity, and software installation.
  • Meet defined response and resolution expectations, and keep employees informed of status through to closure.
  • Document issues, actions taken, and resolutions in the ticketing system so history is complete, searchable, and reportable.
  • Identify recurring issues and recommend permanent fixes, automation, or documentation rather than repeating manual remediation.
  • Build and maintain self-service guidance and end user documentation for common tasks.

Identity, Access, and Account Administration

  • Administer user accounts, groups, and licenses in Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft 365, including creation, modification, and disablement.
  • Execute employee onboarding and offboarding, including timely provisioning of accounts, licenses, groups, and equipment, and complete, verified deprovisioning on departure.
  • Process access requests against approved role-based entitlements and least privilege, escalating anything outside standard entitlement to the Manager, IT Operations.
  • Support multifactor authentication, conditional access, and password policy administration.
  • Maintain accurate access records and produce evidence for periodic access reviews and audits.

Endpoint, Device, and Asset Management

  • Administer endpoints through Microsoft Intune, including enrollment, configuration baselines, compliance policy, patch deployment, and remote remediation.
  • Manage the device lifecycle, including procurement support, configuration, shipment to remote employees, return, secure wipe, and disposal.
  • Maintain accurate IT asset and software license inventory, including assignment, status, and periodic reconciliation.
  • Ensure operating system, security agent, and application updates are applied on schedule and verified as applied.
  • Support secure remote access and virtual desktop configuration for employees working in client environments.

Systems Operations and Maintenance

  • Perform routine administration and monitoring of Microsoft 365 services, Azure tenant services, file and collaboration platforms, and related enterprise systems.
  • Execute scheduled maintenance, backups, restores, and recovery testing according to documented procedures.
  • Monitor system health and alerts, respond within defined thresholds, and escalate promptly when an issue exceeds the scope of the role.
  • Support telephony, conferencing, and collaboration tooling used across the organization.
  • Follow change management procedures for production systems, including documentation, approval, and rollback planning.
  • Participate in scheduled maintenance windows and an after-hours or on-call rotation as required to maintain service availability.

Service Provider and Vendor Coordination

  • Serve as the day-to-day internal coordinator with Accuity’s managed service provider, triaging what is handled internally versus routed to the provider.
  • Track provider tickets through to resolution, verify the quality of work delivered, and escalate delays or repeat issues to the Manager, IT Operations.
  • Support vendor coordination for hardware, software, licensing, warranty, and support cases.
  • Maintain accurate records of vendor interactions, entitlements, and open issues.

Security and Compliance Support

  • Operate within Accuity’s security controls at all times, including least privilege, endpoint protection, application control, data loss prevention, and monitoring tooling.
  • Support HIPAA and HITRUST control operation by executing assigned procedures consistently and producing accurate, timely evidence of the work performed.
  • Report suspected security incidents, phishing, and policy violations immediately per established procedure, and assist with containment and documentation.
  • Support security awareness activities, including phishing simulation follow-up and workforce training administration.
  • Handle protected health information and other sensitive data strictly in accordance with policy.

Documentation and Continuous Improvement

  • Create and maintain runbooks, standard operating procedures, and configuration documentation for the systems and processes supported.
  • Keep documentation current as environments, tools, and procedures change.
  • Recommend and implement improvements to support processes, tooling, and automation that reduce manual effort.
  • Track and report service metrics reflecting responsiveness, resolution quality, and employee satisfaction.

Other Duties as Assigned

  • Perform additional responsibilities as needed to support enterprise IT, technology, and organizational goals.

Qualifications
Education and Credentials

  • Associate or bachelor’s degree in information systems, computer science, or a related technical field preferred.
  • Equivalent professional experience, technical training, or a combination of education and relevant experience may be considered.
  • Relevant certifications in Microsoft 365, Azure, endpoint administration, or identity administration preferred.

Experience

  • 3+ years of hands-on systems administration, IT support, or service desk experience in a business environment.
  • Demonstrated experience administering Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Entra ID, including account, group, and license administration.
  • Experience with endpoint management, preferably Microsoft Intune, including enrollment, configuration policy, and patching.
  • Experience supporting a fully remote or geographically distributed workforce.
  • Experience working alongside a managed service provider or outsourced support partner.
  • Experience in a healthcare or other regulated environment handling protected health information preferred.
  • Familiarity with HIPAA, HITRUST, or comparable control frameworks preferred.

Core Competencies

  • Service Orientation: Treats employee support as the product, communicates clearly, and leaves people better able to do their work.
  • Ownership and Follow-Through: Carries issues to resolution, including those handed to a vendor, rather than considering the handoff the finish line.
  • Triage and Prioritization: Judges urgency and impact accurately, works the right item first, and escalates early when something exceeds scope.
  • Technical Troubleshooting: Diagnoses issues methodically across identity, endpoint, network, and application layers, and fixes root cause where possible.
  • Security Awareness: Recognizes that routine administrative actions carry real security consequences and follows controls without needing reminders.
  • Discretion: Handles protected health information, credentials, and personnel-related access with consistent care and confidentiality.
  • Documentation Discipline: Records what was done and why, and maintains procedures others can follow without asking.
  • Communication: Explains technical issues and next steps clearly to non-technical colleagues, in writing and verbally.
  • Continuous Improvement: Notices repetition and converts it into a fix, a script, or a documented procedure.
  • Adaptability: Adjusts to new tools, changing priorities, and evolving security requirements without losing reliability.
  • Remote-Work Effectiveness: Communicates proactively, stays responsive, documents decisions, and maintains visibility in a fully remote organization.

Additional Requirements
1) Physical Requirements: The requirements described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job with or without reasonable accommodations. Unless otherwise indicated, Accuity positions require interaction with people and technology while either sitting or standing. Employees must be able to communicate via phone, email, etc. and sit for extended periods of time, with or without reasonable accommodations. Physical effort and exposure to physical risk are limited to that of an office role / environment.
2) Position and Employment Statement: While this job description is intended to be an accurate reflection of the job requirements, management reserves the right to modify, add or remove duties from a job and to assign other duties as necessary and at any time. All positions at Accuity Delivery Systems, LLC, are at-will employment, and a position description is not a guarantee of a job or of job responsibilities.

title: Director of Supply Chain
description:
Position Summary
The Director of Supply Chain is a transformational leader responsible for end-to-end supply chain strategy and operations, including Spare Parts Logistics, Parts Procurement, Fleet and Sub-Contractor relationships. This leader drives operational excellence, digital transformation, and continuous improvement, ensuring the supply chain delivers exceptional customer experience, cost efficiency, and resilience. The Director will champion innovation, sustainability, supplier governance, and collaboration across all supply chain functions, aligning strategy with organizational goals and growth.
The Director of Supply Chain will establish structure, cadence, routines, and expectations for each functional area of responsibility. The Leader will focus on delivering exceptional customer experience, workforce development, cost efficiencies, and profitability. As a member of the Operations leadership team, the Director Supply Chain sets annual goals and quarterly objectives for their teams, providing direction, resources, communication, and coordination in support of the wider organization. This role partners closely with the Field Operations, Part Repair Depot, Technology and Customer Success Teams to drive profitable growth and a positive customer experience.

Salary commensurate upon skill set, experience, and competency in leadership roles.
Position is bonus eligible based on individual and company performance.

Essential Functions & Key Responsibilities
Strategic Leadership

Develop and execute comprehensive supply chain strategies supporting business objectives, customer satisfaction, and long-term growth.
Lead transformation initiatives to automate and integrate supply chain functions, leveraging recent investments in systems and tools, i.e. AI.
Foster a culture of innovation, professional development, and continuous improvement within the supply chain team.
Engage in strategic customer discussions in support of operational excellence and customer/partner executive escalations and/or representing CI initiatives in direct to customer communications.

Spare Parts Logistics

Oversee warehousing, distribution, reverse logistics, and repair processes to maximize fill rates, minimize resolution times, and optimize inventory levels.
Build scalable, digitally-enabled logistics operations supporting just-in-time replenishment and real-time inventory visibility.
Own all freight-related elements, including cost management, quality impact, and service performance.

Parts Procurement

Lead the parts purchasing group, establishing supplier/vendor selection processes, scorecards, and governance review cadence.
Negotiate strategic supplier agreements to drive cost efficiency, improve margins, and secure favorable terms.
Drive continuous improvement and innovation initiatives across procurement practices, i.e. vendor managed inventory.

Fleet & Supplier Governance

Develop and implement standardized processes for supplier evaluation, selection, and onboarding, including scorecards and governance review cadence.
Ensure suppliers meet all required qualifications, certifications, and compliance standards (insurance, legal, ethical, and sustainability requirements).
Set clear expectations through service-level agreements (SLAs) and key performance indicators (KPIs).
Manage the administration, order and forecasting fleet vehicles
Conduct regular performance reviews and audits to ensure suppliers meet quality, timeliness, cost, and compliance standards.
Maintain accountability and drive consistent results through transparent reporting and escalation processes.
Proactively identify, assess, and mitigate supplier-related risks, including financial stability, regulatory compliance, and operational continuity.
Develop contingency plans and maintain open communication channels to navigate potential disruptions or challenges.
Ensure all suppliers adhere to company policies, legal requirements, and industry regulations, including anti-bribery, anti-corruption, and supplier diversity initiatives.
Champion supplier diversity by setting targets for spend with diverse suppliers and ensuring certification and reporting requirements are met.
Promote sustainability by encouraging suppliers to adopt eco-friendly practices and support local communities.
Establish tiered governance structures for strategic, operational, and tactical supplier oversight, with clear roles, responsibilities, and escalation paths.
Foster collaboration and joint problem-solving with suppliers to unlock innovation, efficiency gains, and mutual value creation.
Maintain complete and accurate records of supplier activities, contracts, and compliance documentation to support audits and reviews.

Governance & Performance

Develop and monitor KPIs and dashboards to track supply chain performance.
Drive continuous improvement and expense control through identification and elimination of waste.
Lead DEI and sustainability efforts within the supply chain function.

Risk Management & Compliance

Coordinate risk management efforts, including contingency planning for disruptions, shortages, or other unforeseen challenges.
Ensure compliance with legal standards, corporate social responsibility commitments, and supplier diversity policies.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Proven ability to drive, monitor, and report on supply chain management and governance processes.
Strong leadership and team-building skills; ability to foster a shared purpose and positive culture.
Expertise in analytics, Six Sigma, and structured problem-solving.
Excellent communication, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills, including senior leaders and external partners.
Technologically fluent with a passion for innovation and digital enablement.

Education and Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Business, or related field strongly preferred.
MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive operations and supply chain leadership experience, preferably in services or industrial sectors.
Ideal candidate should possess Six Sigma certification or equivalent process improvement training.
Deep expertise in ERP, AI/ML, inventory planning, and supply chain platforms.

Physical Requirements and Working Conditions

Professional office environment or remote work; up to 40% travel required.

Other Duties

title: Senior Safety Representative (HSE)

Company: C2OLocation: Various Locations – Northeastern United StatesEmployment: Project-Based / Full-TimePosition Status: Contingent Upon Contract Award
Position Overview
C2O is seeking an experienced Senior Safety Representative to support major Transmission & Distribution (T&D), high-voltage upgrade, and substation construction projects at various locations throughout the Northeastern United States.
The Senior Safety Representative will provide field safety leadership and oversight for construction crews performing high-risk transmission, distribution, and substation activities. The successful candidate will have strong experience developing and implementing site-specific safety programs, working directly with construction leadership and craft personnel, identifying hazards, and ensuring compliance with company, client, and regulatory safety requirements.
This position is contingent upon contract award.
Key Responsibilities

Develop, implement, and maintain site-specific safety plans for high-voltage transmission, distribution, and substation construction activities.

Provide daily field safety oversight and enforce applicable company, client, OSHA, and project safety requirements.

Conduct safety inspections, observations, audits, and hazard assessments.

Develop and review Job Safety Analyses (JSAs), Pre-Task Analyses (PTAs), and Activity Hazard Analyses (AHAs).

Develop and deliver toolbox talks and safety training for field personnel.

Establish and enforce PPE requirements based on project hazards and work activities.

Promote Stop Work Authority and ensure unsafe conditions and behaviors are addressed promptly.

Investigate incidents, injuries, near misses, and property-damage events and ensure proper documentation and reporting.

Track safety observations, incidents, corrective actions, and lost-time events.

Coordinate with project management, supervisors, contractors, clients, and medical personnel regarding safety-related matters.

Support pre-mobilization planning, required safety documentation, emergency response plans, and site evacuation plans.

Implement programs to identify jobsite hazards, potential exposures, and appropriate mitigation measures.

Assist with developing project and departmental safety procedures, handbooks, orientation materials, and new-hire requirements.

Promote safety awareness and employee engagement through recognition and incentive initiatives.

Provide safety leadership across multiple projects or sites when required.

Participate in client and company safety audits and ensure identified corrective actions are completed.

Preferred Qualifications

Significant safety experience supporting Transmission & Distribution, high-voltage, substation, utility, or major construction projects.

Strong working knowledge of OSHA construction standards and electrical/construction safety requirements.

Experience with JSAs/JHAs, PTAs, AHAs, toolbox talks, incident investigations, and corrective-action management.

Turnaround Planning and Execution

Develop detailed turnaround schedules, resource plans, and cost estimates.

Lead post-turnaround reviews and capture lessons learned for continuous improvement.

Small Capital Project Management

Develop project charters, execution plans, budgets, schedules, and risk assessments.
Coordinate engineering design, procurement, construction, startup, and project closeout activities.
Ensure projects meet technical specifications, quality standards, and operational requirements.
Evaluate project alternatives and provide recommendations to optimize cost, schedule, and performance.

Budget and Cost Management

Develop and manage project budgets, forecasts, and expenditure tracking.
Monitor project costs and identify risks or opportunities affecting financial performance.
Prepare capital authorization requests, project justifications, and status reports.
Ensure effective management of contractor and vendor costs.

Safety and Compliance

Promote a strong safety culture and ensure compliance with company safety policies and regulatory requirements.
Lead project risk assessments, job safety analyses, and pre-job planning activities.

Ensure environmental and regulatory compliance throughout project execution.

Facilitate project meetings and ensure alignment across cross-functional teams.
Build and maintain strong relationships with operations, maintenance, engineering, and external partners.

Strong understanding of project controls, budgeting, scheduling, and contractor management.
Experience using project scheduling software such as Primavera P6 or Microsoft Project.

Experience with turnaround management processes and best practices.
Knowledge of reliability and maintenance methodologies.

Experience with Management of Change (MOC) processes.

title: Engineer, Electrical
description:
Electrical Engineer
Reports to: Engineering Manager
Work Location: Durham, NC
FLSA Status: Exempt
Position Summary: The Electrical Engineer is responsible for supporting the design, maintenance, troubleshooting, and continuous improvement of electrical systems and equipment in a heavy manufacturing environment. This role ensures safe, reliable, and efficient operation of production systems, utilities, and automation equipment while supporting plant uptime and operational performance goals.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Handles projects of a high profile, complex nature that may involve groups inside and outside of the organization
  • Support operation, maintenance, and optimization of plant electrical systems and equipment
  • Troubleshoot and resolve electrical and controls issues affecting production and facility systems
  • Design, modify, and improve electrical systems including power distribution, motor control systems, and automation equipment
  • Support and lead capital projects including equipment upgrades, installations, and commissioning activities
  • Develop and maintain electrical drawings, schematics, and technical documentation
  • Work with PLC, HMI, and SCADA systems to support automated manufacturing processes
  • Collaborate with maintenance and operations teams to improve equipment reliability and reduce downtime
  • Conduct root cause analysis (RCA) on electrical failures and implement corrective and preventive actions
  • Support preventative and predictive maintenance programs for critical electrical assets
  • Ensure compliance with applicable electrical codes and safety standards, including NFPA 70 (NEC) and OSHA requirements and operate in accordance with Kymera Environmental, Health & Safety policies
  • Analyze equipment performance and recommend improvements for energy efficiency and process optimization
  • Generates new/updated Standard Operating Procedures and similar documents, accountable for improvements and new product activities which ensure workers safety, compliance with environmental regulations and integrate with the Company quality systems.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or related discipline
  • 2 years of experience in heavy manufacturing, industrial, or process environments
  • Strong knowledge of industrial electrical systems (power distribution, motor controls, instrumentation)
  • Experience with PLC systems (e.g., Siemens, Rockwell Automation / Allen-Bradley)
  • Familiarity with variable frequency drives (VFDs), motors, and control systems
  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills in industrial environments
  • Direct experience within a melt or metal powder environment
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license, preferred

Skills and Competencies

  • Deep technical problem-solving in high-energy systems
  • Ability to diagnose complex interactions between electrical, thermal, and mechanical systems
  • Strong sense of urgency in minimizing downtime and improving processes
  • Cross-functional collaboration with operations, maintenance, and metallurgy teams
  • Continuous improvement mindset focused on yield, efficiency, and equipment life
  • Holds self and others accountable to meet commitments
  • Makes good and timely decisions that keep the organization moving forward
  • Actively learns through experimentation when tackling new problems, using both successes and failures as learning opportunities.

Physical Requirements

  • Regularly required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; climb or balance; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl and talk or hear.
  • Frequently required to stand; occasionally required to walk; sit and taste or smell.

•Required to lift and /or move up to 10 lbs. (regularly); 25 lbs. (frequently); 50 lbs. (occasionally).

  • Required to use their close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision and depth perception.
  • Ability to work in hot industrial environments and around energized equipment
  • Ability to work in tight or elevated spaces

Work Environment

  • Frequently exposed to high, precarious places and extreme heat.
  • Regularly exposed to moving mechanical parts and fumes or airborne particles.
  • Occasionally exposed to wet and/or humid conditions, outside weather conditions.
  • Exposed to the risk of electrical shock and vibration and high levels of noise.
  • Exposure to noise, dust, high temperatures, and industrial hazards
  • On-call support for critical melt operations may be required

All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, age, or veteran status.

title: Electrical Engineer, P.E. (Texas) – Data Center Design
description:
Job Title: Electrical Engineer, P.E. (Texas) – Data Center Design
Location: TexasJob Type: Full-Time
About the RoleWe are seeking an experienced Electrical Engineer with an active Professional Engineer (P.E.) license in the State of Texas to support the design and development of mission critical data center facilities. This position is ideal for a technically strong engineer with direct experience in data center electrical design, including utility coordination, medium- and low-voltage distribution, standby generation, UPS systems, grounding, and overall mission critical power infrastructure.
The successful candidate will play a key role in delivering high-quality electrical engineering solutions for complex data center projects, working closely with multidisciplinary teams, clients, vendors, and construction stakeholders to support projects from concept development through detailed design and construction support.
Key Responsibilities

Lead and support the electrical design of data center and other mission critical facilities.
Prepare and review electrical design packages, calculations, specifications, single-line diagrams, and construction drawings.
Design and coordinate systems including utility service entrance, medium-voltage distribution, transformers, switchgear, generators, UPS systems, PDUs, RPPs, grounding, and lightning protection.
Perform electrical load studies, short circuit studies, coordination studies, and arc flash evaluations.
Support design development for reliability configurations such as N, N+1, 2N, and other mission critical redundancy strategies.
Coordinate with mechanical, controls, civil, structural, architectural, and telecom disciplines to ensure integrated project delivery.
Interface with clients, utility providers, OEMs, contractors, and AHJs throughout the design and execution process.
Review vendor submittals and respond to RFIs during design and construction phases.
Provide technical support during procurement, construction, commissioning, start-up, and turnover activities as required.
Ensure designs comply with applicable codes, standards, and client requirements, including NEC, NFPA, IEEE, and local Texas regulations.
Mentor junior engineers and contribute to design quality, consistency, and continuous improvement.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering from an accredited institution.
Active Professional Engineer (P.E.) license in the State of Texas.
Minimum 5+ years of electrical engineering experience, with significant experience in data center or mission critical facility design.
Strong understanding of electrical power systems for mission critical environments.
Experience preparing technical design documents, calculations, and drawing packages.
Familiarity with electrical system modeling and analysis tools.
Strong working knowledge of NEC, NFPA, IEEE, and applicable industry practices.
Ability to work effectively in a multidisciplinary team environment and communicate with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Strong organizational, problem-solving, and technical writing skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience designing large-scale or hyperscale data center facilities.
Familiarity with behind-the-meter generation, backup power systems, and BESS integration.
Experience supporting construction administration, commissioning, and energization planning.
Proficiency with Revit, AutoCAD, SKM, ETAP, or similar engineering software.
Previous experience working with owners, EPC contractors, or mission critical design firms.

What We Offer

Opportunity to support high-profile mission critical and data center projects in Texas and beyond.
Collaborative team environment with strong technical leadership.
Competitive compensation and benefits package.
Opportunity to contribute to complex, fast-paced, and high-growth infrastructure projects.

Work Authorization RequirementApplicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. This position does not offer visa sponsorship or employment-based immigration support now or in the future.
Direct applicants only. We are not engaging staffing agencies for this role
