Full-time employees may elect medical, dental and vision coverage effective on their first day of employment. We also offer paid vacation and discretionary time off (DTO), with the amount and timing based on position and tenure; paid company holidays after 90 days; and a 401(k) with company match beginning on the first day of the month following 90 days of employment. Educational reimbursement is available after one year of employment. Eligible employees may also participate in quarterly profit sharing when company performance thresholds are met. Hourly employees who work on a recognized holiday receive time-and-a-half for all hours worked. Benefits and eligibility are subject to applicable plan documents and company policies.

title: Systems Engineer
location: Orlando, FL, US; Rochester, NY, US
description:
POSITION TITLE: Systems Engineer

Kodak Alaris is seeking a self-motivated Imaging Systems Engineer to join our Kodak Moments Hardware Systems Solutions group. The Imaging Systems Engineer is responsible for the design, integration, testing, and lifecycle support of electrical, mechanical, and systems-level solutions used in Kodak Moments products, including photo kiosks, travel & leisure imaging solutions, and related hardware subsystems.

This position offers a unique opportunity to develop technology that enhances guest experiences in travel, leisure, attraction, entertainment, and hospitality venues around the world. Our products help consumers capture, share, and preserve some of life's most memorable moments, creating engaging engineering challenges that combine imaging, hardware, automation, reliability, and customer experience. Engineers in this role have the opportunity to see their solutions deployed in real-world environments where they directly impact millions of consumer interactions and experiences.

This role covers end-to-end system development spanning system architecture, hardware selection, electrical and mechanical integration, imaging and camera subsystems, prototype evaluation, documentation, commercialization support, and sustaining engineering. The engineer works across hardware, software, service, quality, manufacturing, and supplier teams to translate business, customer, service, regulatory, and manufacturing needs into practical system solutions. Camera and image-capture experience is strongly desired.

Software development is not the primary focus of this role. However, working knowledge of software interfaces, vendor SDKs/APIs, scripting, and prototype development is desirable to support system evaluation, troubleshooting, and proof-of-concept activities.

The successful candidate will possess an inventive spirit, strong technical curiosity, and a passion for solving complex engineering challenges. They will be motivated by the opportunity to transform ideas into practical, scalable solutions and will view technical obstacles not as roadblocks, but as opportunities for innovation.

Regular access to the Rochester NY or Orlando FL office and development labs will be required. Occasional domestic or international travel may be required.

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES

Work with a cross-functional commercialization team throughout product development and lifecycle support
Define system and product requirements and contribute to overall system architecture, including:

Electrical and mechanical subsystem design
Imaging and camera subsystem integration
Hardware/software interfaces
Configuration management and bill of materials development
Evaluate, select, integrate, and validate electrical, mechanical, imaging, and computer hardware subsystems to meet product, customer, service, manufacturing, and regulatory requirements.
Evaluate new technologies, third-party solutions, and imaging platforms for suitability, performance, scalability, and commercialization opportunities.
Design, build, document, and test prototypes to validate system concepts, component selections, integration approaches, and overall system performance.
Troubleshoot and resolve system-level issues using laboratory equipment, structured engineering methods, and root-cause analysis techniques.
Provide end-to-end system design, integration, verification, and commercialization support from concept through sustaining engineering, including pilot builds, field trials, and product lifecycle activities.
Develop and maintain system documentation, drawings, interface specifications, configuration records, and bills of materials.
Support HSE, quality, and regulatory compliance activities as required.
Manage component lifecycle activities, including obsolescence mitigation, alternate part qualification, and component change management.
Collaborate with software and QA teams on system interfaces, SDKs, APIs, drivers, and prototype tools required to support product development and validation.
Work with suppliers, fabricators, customers, and field service teams to define requirements, troubleshoot issues, and support system deployment and ongoing product improvements.
Work with customers to understand needs and work through system design and installation. This may range from calls to in-person visits.
Consistently deliver against project commitments while supporting multiple priorities and programs.

SKILLS AND/OR KNOWLEDGE SPECIFICATIONS

Required

Strong systems engineering experience including requirements definition, system architecture, integration, verification, troubleshooting, and lifecycle support.
Working knowledge of electrical and mechanical system design, including power distribution, cabling, grounding, thermal management, enclosure design, mounting, environmental considerations, manufacturability, serviceability, and regulatory compliance.
Hands-on experience integrating and validating electrical, mechanical, computer hardware, imaging, and peripheral subsystems within commercial products.
Proficiency creating and maintaining engineering drawings, schematics, wiring diagrams, configuration diagrams, interface control documents, bills of materials, and technical specifications.
Experience using CAD and engineering design tools. SolidWorks, SolidWorks Electrical, Altium, AutoCAD, or equivalent experience preferred.
Proficiency with engineering laboratory equipment including digital multimeters, oscilloscopes, programmable power supplies, logic analyzers, signal generators, and data acquisition equipment.
Hands-on experience assembling, modifying, repairing, and troubleshooting hardware using common engineering and technician hand tools.
Experience debugging electrical, mechanical, hardware, and system-level integration issues using structured root cause analysis techniques.
Experience evaluating, selecting, integrating, and validating sensors, cameras, controllers, motors, power supplies, and related subsystem components.
Strong working knowledge of computer hardware systems, interfaces, and peripheral integration.
Broad understanding of imaging systems including camera hardware, optics, lighting, image capture, image quality, and video or still-image workflows.
Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to develop technical documentation, engineering reports, and design specifications.
Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities while consistently delivering against commitments.

Desired

Camera, image-capture, optics, lighting, lens, image quality, video, or still-imaging system experience strongly desired.
Familiarity with SolidWorks PDM, PLM, or related product data management systems.
Experience creating test plans, conducting validation testing, collecting and analyzing results, and documenting findings.
Experience working with suppliers, fabricators, manufacturing, quality, and service organizations to support product development and sustaining engineering.
Experience with Windows and Linux hardware integration and troubleshooting.
Experience working with hardware APIs, SDKs, drivers, or vendor libraries.
Ability to develop prototype software, scripts, test tools, or proof-of-concept applications using Python, C#, .NET, or similar technologies.
Experience with virtual machines, VMWare ESXi, Docker, Arduino, embedded controllers, Azure, AWS, or related development and test environments.
Experience with equipment commercialization and new product introduction (NPI) processes.
Familiarity with photo printing systems, retail kiosks, or commercial imaging products.
Knowledge of quality assurance processes as they relate to product development.
Experience debugging hardware performance bottlenecks and system-level performance issues.
Experience working with international suppliers and contract manufacturers.
Design of Experiments (DOE) and engineering statistical analysis.
Project management experience.
Working knowledge of worldwide regulatory agency approval documentation and testing requirements.
Familiarity with current/sustaining engineering and component obsolescence management.

EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE SPECIFICATIONS

BS Degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Systems Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, Imaging Science, or related engineering discipline.
Experience designing, integrating, testing, and troubleshooting electrical, mechanical, and computer-based systems
Coursework or experience in system integration, imaging systems, camera systems, hardware/software interfaces, or related technologies
Experience using CAD tools, engineering test equipment, and technical documentation processes preferred.

Compensation: $81,000 - $101,000 annually, based on level of experience

title: Director of Strategic Operations
description:
Why This Role Matters
This is a unique opportunity to join an organization as the leader responsible for shaping Chesapeake's operating model. This role sits at the center of how Chesapeake sustainably translates strategic and operational intent into focused action and impact.
At Chesapeake Employers, we believe great strategy only creates value when it is consistently translated into focused execution. We are seeking a Director of Strategic Operations to serve as the enterprise steward of Chesapeake's Growth System; our Four Disciplines of Execution-based (4DX) operating model.
Reporting directly to the President & CEO, this highly visible leadership role is responsible for owning, sustaining, and maturing Chesapeake’s operating model (The Growth System) enabling focused, enterprise-side strategic and operational execution. The Director of Strategic Operations will work closely with executive leaders and teams across the company to ensure priorities are clear, resources are aligned, and the organization's most important work moves forward.
This is an opportunity for a systems designer, disciplined operator, and influential leader who thrives on creating clarity, building alignment, and driving execution in a collaborative environment. This leader will influence not only what Chesapeake achieves, but how it achieves it; helping make the Growth System the Chesapeake Way of working.
What Success Looks Like
A successful Director of Strategic Operations will help Chesapeake mature a disciplined, sustainable operating system for execution. Over time, success in this role will look like:

Maintaining Growth System Standard Operating Procedures: playbooks, templates, tools, processes and communication materials.
Ensuring the Growth System is understood, consistently applied, and continuously improved across the enterprise.
Supporting leaders’ understanding of how the elements of the Growth System work together within Chesapeake’s operating model.
Guiding the senior leadership team to prioritize Strategic Execution Wildly Important Goals (WIGs) aligned to enterprise strategy and scope WIGs into executable programs and projects within the 4DX model.
Orchestrating delivery across the Strategic Execution WIG portfolio.
Coaching leaders on 4DX operating model disciplines, including WIG design, scoreboard development, team kickoffs and syncs, and celebration rituals.
Supporting team leaders in identifying, creating a backlog, prioritizing, and launching Focused Improvement WIGs that deliver targeted, measurable growth and improvement outcomes.
Designing, maturing and running Chesapeake’s Enterprise Project Portfolio Council (EPPC) and overarching governance model that supports Growth System WIG capacity assessment, prioritization decisioning and execution coordination.
Helping leaders assess team capacity, authority, resources, and focus needed to execute WIGs successfully.
Providing executive leaders with clear visibility into progress, blockers, and capacity concerns.
Helping teams see how their work connects to Chesapeake’s purpose and strategy.
The Growth System becomes a trusted way of working.

Be a Part of Inspiring Chesapeake’s Values-Based Leadership Mindset:
Purpose Driven Connects goals, priorities, and execution to a larger mission and helps others understand the impact of their work.
People First Builds trust, listens with curiosity, and helps teams navigate change with empathy and clarity.
Committed to Winning Together Breaks down silos, fosters collaboration, and creates environments where teams succeed together.
A Risk Taker at Heart Fosters curiosity, encourages experimentation and guides the organization to turn bold ideas into meaningful progress.
Join us and shape how Chesapeake sustainably translates strategic and operational intent into focused action and impact.

Position Summary:
The Director of Strategic Operations is an enterprise-wide systems design and execution leader responsible for owning, sustaining and maturing the company’s operating model. Chesapeake Employers’ Growth System is the company’s Four Disciplines of Execution (4DX)-based operating model enabling Strategic and Focused Improvement (operational-level) execution to continuously and sustainably grow stakeholder value.

This role sits at the center of how Chesapeake sustainably translates strategic and operational intent into focused action and impact. The Director of Strategic Operations ensures that Wildly Important Goals (WIGs) are well-formed, appropriately prioritized and resourced, actively managed, and connected to the company’s strategic direction, Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and annual business plan. They ensure the Growth System is not treated as an additional layer of work but becomes The Chesapeake Way of working to focus capacity, surface and address blockers, and achieve desired outcomes to continuously elevate tangible delivery of Chesapeake’s purpose to stakeholders.
The Director of Strategic Operations does not primarily lead through formal authority. Instead, this person must lead through influence, clarity, structure, trust, and disciplined follow-through. They can constructively challenge thinking, influence senior leaders, facilitate challenging prioritization discussions, and establish alignment across varying priorities. They must be able to inspire and motivate others, help leaders understand the “why” and “how” behind the Growth System, and create the conditions for teams to sustainably improve the business solving important, challenging problems together.
Duties and Responsibilities:
Growth System Leadership

Serve as the enterprise owner and steward of Chesapeake’s Growth System.
Maintain fidelity to the 4DX operating model, including WIG selection, lead and lag measures, scoreboards, team syncs, accountability rhythms, and celebrations.
Ensure the Growth System is understood, consistently applied, and continuously improved across the enterprise
Support leaders in understanding how the elements of the Growth System work together within Chesapeake’s operating model.
Coordinate periodic refreshes of corporate-level KPIs and facilitate team-level KPIs development enterprise-wide via process management.
Ensure that team-level KPIs and Focused Improvement WIGs are aligned with corporate-level KPIs.
Monitor and ensure consistent reporting of KPIs and WIGs within Growth System channels.
Maintain and update Growth System Standard Operating Procedures: playbooks, templates, tools, processes and communication materials.

Strategic Execution

Manage the Strategic Execution practices of the Growth System.
Facilitate executive level decisioning to align priorities, resources, capacity and planning with enterprise strategy and operational targets.
Manage the Strategic Execution portfolio and backlog scope and structure WIGs into executable programs and projects within the 4Dx model.
Orchestrate delivery across the Strategic Execution WIG portfolio.
Surface and guide resolution of risks, blockers, capacity constraints, and decision-making through the company’s governance framework.

Operational Excellence & Focused Improvement

Ensure leaders’ consistent adoption of Standard Operating Procedures.
Coach leaders on 4DX operating model disciplines, including WIG design, scoreboard development, team kickoff, team syncs, and celebration rituals.
Support team leaders in identifying, creating a backlog, prioritizing, and launching WIGs that deliver targeted, measurable growth and improvement outcomes.
Guide leaders on identifying and moving appropriate Focused Improvement WIGs to and through the governance model.
Maintain visibility of Focused Improvement WIGs, priority and capacity decisioning across the enterprise.
Monitor the health of Focused Improvement WIGs without over-centralizing ownership of team-level work.

Governance & Enterprise Alignment

Design, mature, and run Chesapeake’s Enterprise Project Portfolio Council (EPPC) and overarching governance model that supports Growth System WIG capacity assessment, prioritization decisioning and execution coordination.
Manage the enterprise-wide backlog of prioritized Strategic Execution and Focused Improvement WIG opportunities, ensuring they are aligned with and responsive to existing backlogs across governance bodies.
Clarify enterprise-wide priority and capacity decision ownership and create feedback loops.
Prepare materials for Enterprise Project and Portfolio Council (EPPC) meetings, including WIG prioritization decisions, in-flight WIG status, risks, blockers, capacity considerations, recommended decisions and measurement of return-on-investment.
Ensure the right leaders have the right level of visibility into the right work at the right time.
Create practices to minimize duplication, overcommitment, and misalignment across enterprise priorities.

Assess Organizational Capacity

Support leaders in distinguishing between availability and true capacity.
Help leaders assess whether teams have the capacity, authority, resources, and focus needed to execute WIGs successfully.
Identify where the organization may be overcommitted or where WIGs need to be narrowed, sequenced, paused, or escalated.
Encourage disciplined prioritization so the Growth System strengthens focus rather than adding unmanageable work on top of the whirlwind.

Change Leadership & Adoption

Serve as a champion and translator of the Growth System across the organization.
Help leaders and teams understand why the Growth System matters and how it enables the organization to continuously and sustainably grow stakeholder value.
Own, sustain, and mature enterprise-wide change management practices.
Communicate in ways that are credible with executives, useful to team leaders, and accessible to team members.
Facilitate conversations that surface resistance, clarify concerns, and move teams toward action.
Surface learnings, recognize progress, and help teams celebrate wins.
Build confidence and consistency in the Growth System over time.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

Enterprise operating system frameworks’ design and execution
Enterprise program management and execution discipline
Familiarity with and capable of applying change management techniques
Governance design and facilitation
Ability to manage complex, cross-functional work
Strong meeting facilitation and operating rhythm design
Ability to coach leaders without relying on positional authority
Strong communication with executives, managers, and frontline staff
Ability to translate strategy into clear goals, measures, and actions
Understanding of lead measures, lag measures, dashboards, and scoreboards
Backlog management and prioritization
Broad stakeholder engagement
Continuous improvement mindset and process improvement experience
Ability to identify risks, blockers, dependencies, and capacity constraints
Strong documentation skills, including SOPs, playbooks, templates, and status reporting
Comfort working in ambiguity while creating clarity for others

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in business, management, organizational leadership or related field required
5 to 8 years of hands-on experience in leading complex management systems design and execution
Experience supporting management operating systems such as 4DX, Objectives & Key Results (OKRs), Hoshin Kanri, Lean, Agile, or similar strategy execution frameworks
Experience creating repeatable management system SOPs, operating rhythms, playbooks, templates, and communications
Experience program and project managing enterprise-wide strategic initiatives with executive engagement
Experience facilitating governance bodies, meetings, and operating rhythms
Experience coaching leaders and teams through change
Experience building dashboards, scoreboards, status reports, or executive visibility tools
Experience managing backlogs, prioritization processes, and cross-functional dependencies
Familiarity with Microsoft tools and enterprise collaboration platforms

Preferred Qualifications:

Deep knowledge of the 4 Disciplines of Execution is a plus
Certification in Agile, Lean, Six Sigma, change management, project management or related disciplines is a plus

Physical Demands:
This job description is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. It is not an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

title: Plastics Cost Estimator
description:
Job Summary:
The Plastics Cost Estimator develops accurate, competitive, and well-supported quotations for injection-molded components, tooling, secondary operations, and related manufacturing services at Forj Medical's Vadnais Heights site. This role evaluates customer requirements and translates technical and operational inputs into clear quotations while partnering with Commercial, Engineering, Tooling, Supply Chain, Quality, Finance, NPI, and Operations to balance customer needs, manufacturability, risk, capacity, and business objectives.
Job Duties and Responsibilities:

Review RFQs, customer drawings, models, specifications, forecasts, and quality requirements to define scope, assumptions, risks, and information gaps.
Will be required to know the current market and be able to estimate tooling and material based on experience and knowledge without soliciting estimates from vendors.
Develop detailed cost models for injection molding, molds and fixtures, purchased materials, labor, machine time, cycle time, scrap, secondary operations, inspection, packaging, validation, preventative maintenance, and outside services.
Partner with Tool Design, Process Engineering, NPI, Quality, Operations, Toolroom, Maintenance, and Supply Chain to establish realistic manufacturing concepts, routings, capacity assumptions, lead times, and project requirements.
Solicit and evaluate supplier quotations for tooling, resin, components, automation, equipment, and external processes; document sourcing assumptions and commercial risks.
Prepare accurate quotation packages, pricing recommendations, investment requirements, and supporting rationale for internal review and customer submission.
Identify cost drivers and recommend design, tooling, sourcing, automation, cavitation, or process alternatives that improve value and manufacturability.
Maintain estimating tools, cost standards, historical data, labor and burden assumptions, quote records, and version control.
Conduct post-award and post-launch reviews comparing estimated and actual cost, cycle time, scrap, labor, capital, and margin; incorporate lessons learned into future estimates.
Support change quotations, annual pricing reviews, make-versus-buy decisions, capital planning, and business-case development.
Communicate assumptions, exclusions, risks, and timing clearly to internal stakeholders and support customer clarification discussions as needed.
Ensure estimates align with applicable quality-system, regulatory, customer, and company requirements.
Manage multiple quotations and deadlines in a fast-paced contract-manufacturing environment.
Perform other duties and support strategic projects as assigned.

Qualifications:
Education

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Finance, Business, Supply Chain, or a related field preferred.
Equivalent combination of education and directly related manufacturing estimating experience may be considered.

Experience

Three or more years of cost estimating, quoting, manufacturing engineering, program management, tooling, or related experience preferred.
Experience estimating injection-molded components, molds, secondary operations, automation, or precision-manufactured products strongly preferred.
Experience in medical device, regulated manufacturing, or contract manufacturing preferred.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Strong financial, analytical, and problem-solving skills with careful attention to detail.
Working knowledge of injection molding, tooling, manufacturing routings, cycle-time analysis, materials, labor, overhead, scrap, and capital-cost drivers.
Advanced spreadsheet skills and proficiency with ERP/MRP, quoting, or cost-modeling tools.
Ability to read technical drawings, specifications, bills of materials, and customer requirements.
Clear written and verbal communication and strong cross-functional collaboration skills.

Working Conditions

Office environment
Manufacturing environment

Compensation

The expected starting salary for this position is $90,000 to $110,000 depending on qualifications. As part of your overall rewards, we offer a comprehensive benefits program.

TITLE: Material Mover B

POSITION OBJECTIVE: The Material Mover is responsible for the safe and accurate movement of spools and carriages between extrusion, work-in-process (WIP), and conversion areas. This role ensures all material movements are properly scanned and reconciled in the IBS system while maintaining organization, FIFO flow, and compliance with safety, security, and quality standards.

QUALIFICATIONS:

Good organizational skills, able to handle multiple tasks
Ability to safely and efficiently move material on a carriage
Good communication skills
Ensure consistent, dependable attendance and demonstrate a willingness to accommodate non-standard work hours as necessary.
Capable of effectively managing job-related stress and fostering productive workplace interaction

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:

Move spools and carriages from extrusion into the WIP area and to conversion machines, including required scanning activities.
Ensure all spool and material movements are accurately scanned and recorded in the IBS system.
Maintain organization of the WIP area, ensuring proper first-in, first-out (FIFO) material flow.
Transport empty spools from the conversion area back to extrusion in a timely manner.
Reconcile physical material movements with IBS system transactions and report discrepancies as needed.
Comply with all OSHA, MSDS, and C-TPAT regulations, as well as the Minigrip safety program and policies.
Maintain a safe, professional, and clean work environment in accordance with Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and a 5S organizational program.
Communicate effectively with extrusion, conversion, and inventory personnel to support production flow.
Perform other duties as requested by management.

title: Category Growth Consultant - Serveware & Buffetware
description: Serveware & Buffetware – Category Growth Consultant Libbey is committed to expanding its presence and accelerating growth within the Serveware & Buffetware category. To support this strategic initiative, we are seeking a Category Growth Leader who will serve as the organization's subject matter expert and strategic leader for the category. As Libbey continues its meaningful entrance into the Serveware & Buffetware market, this role will be responsible for accelerating category knowledge, informing critical strategic and commercial decisions, and establishing a roadmap for sustainable growth. This leader will leverage deep industry expertise to identify market opportunities, guide assortment strategy, strengthen competitive positioning, and help build organizational capabilities within the category. This leader will partner closely with Sales, Marketing, Product Development, Supply Chain, and Executive Leadership to define where Libbey will compete, how Libbey will win, and how success will be measured. RESPONSIBILITIES Lead the development and execution of Libbey's Serveware & Buffetware category growth strategy, establishing a clear roadmap for market expansion and profitable growth. Validate and refine category opportunities through market analysis, customer insights, competitive intelligence, and industry trends. Define Libbey's category positioning, assortment architecture, pricing strategy, and product portfolio priorities. Develop and launch a comprehensive "How to Win" strategy, including target segments, value propositions, and go-to-market recommendations. Partner with Product Development, Marketing, Sales, Supply Chain, and Leadership teams to align category objectives and execution plans. Serve as the organization's subject matter expert on Serveware & Buffetware, providing strategic guidance and category insights. Evaluate competitive offerings and identify opportunities to strengthen Libbey's market position and differentiation. Establish growth metrics, monitor category performance, and recommend actions to drive revenue and market share growth. Build commercial capabilities by developing category education, training, and sales enablement programs. Influence and drive cross-functional decisions that support long-term category growth and customer success. REQUIREMENTS & QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Hospitality, Culinary Management, or a related field – preferred 10+ years of experience within foodservice, serveware, buffetware, hospitality, tabletop, housewares, or related industries. Demonstrated success developing and executing category growth, commercial, or go-to-market strategies. Strong expertise in market assessment, customer segmentation, assortment planning, pricing strategy, and competitive analysis. Experience influencing and partnering with senior leaders across multiple functions. Strong strategic thinking, analytical, and problem-solving capabilities. Excellent presentation, communication, and stakeholder management skills. Proven ability to drive initiatives from concept through execution and deliver measurable business outcomes. COMPETENCIES FOR SUCCESS Behavioral CompetenciesStrategy: Consistently share the importance of connecting your functional strategy to Libbey's strategy, leading to successful completion of business goals. Create engagement and understanding by communicating a clear and compelling vision with a concise roadmap and expectations. Live One Libbey, investing in planning and collaboration across functions for the greater good of the company. Influence: Be a leader who is self-aware, transparent, inclusive, encouraging, and supportive, prioritizing the company's needs. Be a steward of engagement and utilize influence to drive actions that align with Libbey's values. Champion engagement, creating an inclusive, positive, and meaningful experience for all Makers. Develop a legacy of great talent within your function and understand the importance of investing in associates. Lead & Develop: Coach, mentor, and motivate others to drive high levels of productivity, ongoing learning, and achievement. Inspire and empower others to achieve organizational goals and confidently challenge the status quo. Foster an environment of creativity and encouragement to think outside the box, leading to new ideas and innovations. Sales Functional CompetenciesCustomer & Market Understanding: Demonstrates a strong understanding of customers, end users, and the broader market, including key trends, competitive dynamics, and business drivers. Anticipates customer needs by proactively identifying challenges and uncovering opportunities that lead to future projects. Uses insights into customer behavior, product usage, and buying patterns to position Libbey solutions in a way that delivers value beyond the immediate order. Analysis, Insights & Data-Driven Decision Making: Continuously monitors market conditions, category trends, competitive activity, customer performance, and business trends to anticipate opportunities and risks. Uses insights to inform category strategy, identify growth opportunities, and avoid reactive, short-term decision-making. Leverages strong commercial insight to strengthen business recommendations, prioritize opportunities, and improve outcomes. Balances profitability, competitiveness, customer value, and business objectives when making strategic decisions. Cross-Functional Partnership, Negotiating & Communication: Partners effectively across Sales, Sales Operations, Marketing, Customer Service, Supply Chain, Product Development, and other internal teams to deliver a consistent, high-value customer experience. Aligns resources and expertise to execute category strategies, solve business challenges, and drive coordinated outcomes. Demonstrates a One Commercial mindset by ensuring alignment across functions in planning and execution. Leverages Libbey's operating rhythms to drive alignment, accountability, and effective solutions. Assignment Details This is not a direct hire position. This person will not be classified as a Libbey employee. This is a consultant role and requires the individual to work as an independent contractor (1099). The estimated length of the contract assignment is 12 months. This position will require 40%+ travel (to/from Toledo, OH corporate office, customer visits, territory training, tradeshows, etc.). This position will report to the Vice President of Foodservice Sales for the United States and Canada, with high levels of engagement with the Vice President of Marketing for the United States and Canada, and the enterprise’s Chief Commercial Officer.

title: Senior Database Administrator
description:
About the Job

We are seeking an experienced Senior Database Administrator (DBA) to manage and maintain our database systems, ensuring their performance, availability, and security. The ideal candidate will have advanced knowledge of Microsoft SQL Server (MSSQL), MySQL, and MongoDB, along with strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work in a fast-paced environment.

As Senior Database Administrator, You Will…

Design, implement, and maintain database structures and schemas for MSSQL, MySQL, and MongoDB.

Write reusable, testable, and efficient stored procedures code.

Design and implementation of low-latency and high-availability stored procedures, functions, triggers & jobs.

Monitor and optimize database performance, including query tuning and index optimization.

Ensure database security by implementing user roles, permissions, and auditing practices.

Perform regular database backups, restores, and disaster recovery planning.

Collaborate with development teams to optimize database queries and support application performance.

Provide database support for production and development environments, troubleshooting issues as they arise.

Assist in data modeling, data migration, and integration tasks.

Maintain documentation related to database architecture, processes, and procedures.

Stay current with industry trends and best practices in database management.

Report generation is required.

As Senior Database Administrator, You Need…

A graduate with a minimum of 6 years experience as a DBA.

Strong understanding of database design principles and best practices.

Knowledge in developing dynamic-looking graphs/reports.

Knowledge of database backup and recovery techniques and policies.

Experience with database performance tuning, indexing, and query optimization.

Familiarity with cloud database services (e.g., AWS RDS, Azure SQL Database) is a plus.

Experience with automation and scripting (e.g., PowerShell, Bash, Python) for database management tasks.

Effective communication, technical understanding, and teamwork skills.

Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills.

Knowledge of the following:

MSSQL

MySQL

Mongo

Powershell

Bash

Python

Writing Stored Procedures

Stored Functions

MSSQL Job Agent

AWS RDS

Azure SQL Database

title: Peer Specialist I - East Scattered Site
description:
Position Summary
Through lived experience that includes recovery from substance use, homelessness, and/or effective treatment of mental health conditions, the Peer Specialist offers insight & first-hand knowledge to support clients, families, and their integrated teams. You will work to support clients with various challenges to overcome obstacles and achieve their goals by focusing on strengths, empowerment, and advocacy.

Duties/Responsibilities (Essential Functions)

Provides mentorship and support to clients through personal lived experience to build skills in goal setting & problem solving with an emphasis on individual strengths, resilience, and empowerment.
Facilitates counseling and activities for clients in recovery from substance use disorders in individual or group settings to promote connection and agency.
Helps clients coordinate & navigate critical integrated services including healthcare, housing assistance, and behavioral health in partnership with internal teams & outside community partners.
Transports and/or escorts clients to scheduled appointments at Coalition properties and elsewhere as needed using a CCH vehicle or an approved personal vehicle. CCH employees must have access to reliable vehicles outside of CCH fleet.
Collaborates alongside Coalition staff to foster trusting relationships with clients and ensure services provided are timely while aligned to individual goals.
Responsible for ongoing client outreach within the community to monitor needs that are recovery-oriented.

Ensure timely & accurate recording of all clinical/non-clinical services, communications, and tasks in the EHR and other systems as required while maintaining complete up-to-date charts and any future upgrades as directed.
Performs other job duties as assigned.

Education, Licensure and Certifications

Completion of accredited Peer Specialist training program highly preferred.
Basic Life Support Certification required within 30 days of employment.
Bi-lingual English-Spanish and/or ASL preferred
Must have and maintain in good standing, a Colorado driver’s license within 30 days of hire (with the exception of Ft. Lyon & Transitional Housing roles)

Experience

Prior peer mentoring experience serving individuals experiencing behavioral health challenges and/or homelessness highly preferred.
Must be a person with lived experience including substance use disorders, homelessness support services, and/or mental health challenges with prior and/or ongoing recovery activity

Job Competencies

Using lived experience, ability to role-model recovery
Demonstrates a clear understanding of confidentiality protocols & adheres to privacy laws/organizational policies regarding sensitive information.
Engages in meaningful & authentic interactions through active listening, trauma-informed care, and empathy that promote trust.
Recognizes professional boundaries and identifies potential conflicts of interests to maintain ethical standards in interactions with clients, coworkers, and stakeholders.
Establishes trust and rapport with individuals, even in challenging or sensitive situations, to foster openness and respect.
Actively advocates for the needs & rights of individuals/families to ensure access to necessary services, resources, and support systems identified by the clients they are serving.

title: High School Representative
description:
POSITION SUMMARY

The High School Representative (HSR) plays a crucial role in promoting LaSalle College Vancouver to prospective high school students and their families. It is a hybrid campus-based position, working out of LaSalle College Vancouver (LCV) and a home office that markets to High Schools in a given territory to generate interest among students, teachers, guidance counsellors, and principals. HSRs must be able to conduct research, study LCV programs, and deliver educational and entertaining presentations in high school classes.

This position is a 6-month fixed-term contract, with the opportunity for annual renewal for the successful candidate. The final work schedule will be mutually agreed upon, with the ideal arrangement being 4 days per week (Monday to Thursday), 8 hours per day. Candidates who are available to start immediately are preferred.

Key Job Responsibilities:

Meet annual high school visit, presentation, inquiry, and application plans. Collects quality, workable inquiries. Employ good qualifying techniques to meet conversion targets.
Manage high school territory by developing and building rapport with various departments and creating a comprehensive marketing plan.
Schedule and conduct presentations in appropriate classes. Maintains a future calendar, recorded in Outlook. (5 days per week)
Provide one-on-one consultations with prospective students and their families to answer questions and guide them through the admissions process.
Identify appropriate students to schedule appointments with Admission Advisors.
Proactively follow up with inquiries to ensure appropriate service. Assist Admissions and other departments with student matriculation.
Utilize technology, public speaking skills, current industry and LCV school information to deliver effective multimedia presentations.
Participate in appropriate recruitment and enrollment events, which include occasional evenings and weekends.
Assist in organizing and participating in open house events and other on-campus recruitment activities.

Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field or equivalent experience.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with high school students, parents, and educators.
Strong public speaking and presentation skills.
Experience in sales, marketing, or recruitment, preferably in an educational setting.
Excellent organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously.
Familiarity with LaSalle College Vancouver’s programs and campus is an asset.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
Ability to work with people from various social, economic, and cultural backgrounds.
Must have a reliable vehicle, a valid Driver’s License and a clean driving record. Must have good credit and qualify for or possess a credit card.

Working Conditions:

This position requires frequent travel to high schools and community events.
Must be available to work some evenings and weekends to accommodate events and tours.
Must have the ability to complete overnight travel as needed. (seldom)
Driving license & vehicle are required as this position is required frequent travel by themselves within the BC province.

title: Quality Engineer I
description:
The Quality Engineer helps ensure Libbey products consistently meet the highest quality standards. By partnering with suppliers and internal teams, this role drives quality excellence throughout the supply chain.
Quality Engineer responsibilities include establishing and maintaining quality standards, managing product specifications, and ensuring quality documentation remains accurate, current, and accessible to manufacturing locations and suppliers worldwide.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Assist with qualification of new sourced items.
Assist with R&D efforts to improve product quality or the processes and applications.
Report on testing and qualification results through written and oral presentations.
Verification of current and potential sourced product claims for marketing.
Review and update QAPs (Quality Assurance Plans).
Review of PSI (Pre-Shipment Inspection) reports for accuracy and completeness.
Review and update PSS (Product Specification Sheets).
Respond to Customer Questions and Complaints in a Professional Manner.
Investigate and drive resolution to reports of product nonconformities for internal and external customers.
Validate product quality through Lab Testing such as thermal shock, impact and chip resistance, and durability tests.
Support all product channels.
Support Libbey product supply chain during Process and Product Quality audits including third party testing such as Bureau Veritas, SGS, etc.
Coordinate corrective and preventative action responses, activities, and follow up.
Perform gauge reliability and repeatability studies as required.
Stay up to date with relevant compliance and testing standards (such ASTM) for our various product categories and communicate with our suppliers and customer when an appropriates test is recommended.
Assist in the development and implementation of a global Quality Management System.
Other duties as assigned.

REQUIREMENTS & QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor’s degree in a technical field (Engineering, Sciences, Ceramics, Quality, etc.) OR associate degree in a technical field with at least 6 years of Quality or Ceramics Engineer experience
2 years of engineering or lab test experience within a manufacturing industry preferred
Experience in various aspects of quality (corporate, laboratory, operations, supplier, product development and launch, customer satisfaction)
Strong verbal presentation and clear concise written communication skills appropriate to the audience
Proficiency with MS Office
Experience working with engineering and operations on cross-functional projects, facilitating process improvements, ability to streamline/develop and roll-out new processes or product launches preferred
Demonstrated use of structured problem-solving skills, Six Sigma/Lean preferred
Proficient in blueprint reading and GD & T with a working understanding of measurement methods, layout inspection (CMM), gage calibration and industry standards for inspection and testing preferred
Travel up to10% with at least part being international

COMPETENCIES FOR SUCCESS

Take Control: ask for the direction and support you need to attain mastery of your objectives and ownership of your professional development.
Be Engaged & Committed: lean in to learn, engage, and contribute, resulting in increased performance and personal satisfaction from your work.
Be Accountable: hold yourself responsible for achieving your goals and successfully executing against the organization's initiatives.
Continuous Improvement Mindset: Act with curiosity, proactively identifying and implementing changes to enhance work processes and outcomes. Consistently seek opportunities to improve efficiency, quality, and overall effectiveness.

title: Consulting Solution Architect
description:
This is an exciting opportunity to join Experience and Transformation as a Consulting Solutions Architect. We have a wide-ranging client list, working with some of the biggest and innovative brands in the UK across utilities, gaming, publishing, retail and CPG, leisure, financial services and beyond. We are a rapidly expanding team, working at a fast pace, to develop cutting edge solutions for our clients.
Within this role, you will work closely with Business Analysts, Lead Consultants and technical SMEs to advise on architectures. Integral to the role is working to take the requirements from the BA and to work with the client to perform a number of tasks:

Document the As-Is architecture. Gain a comprehensive understanding of the current architecture, so as to help inform capability gaps but also inform any subsequent architecture changes.
Design the To-Be architecture. Design an end state To-Be architecture that meets the client’s requirements.
Phase the To-Be. Must be able to understand the client’s priorities and take into account dependencies and risks to design the phasing of transition between the As-Is and To-Be.
Recommend Components. Alongside designing both Logical and Physical To-Be diagrams, you will be required to recommend potential specific components that meet the client’s functional requirements whilst also fitting into to the broader business requirements.

This is an integral role within the team. We work closely with our technical partners, especially AWS, to define and shape solutions. You will have an exciting opportunity to take a lead on defining a future state for a range of solutions. Increasingly, much of what we are doing is developing architectures that enable organisations to deploy and operationalise AI models. This is, obviously, an ever-changing market, and you’ll be front and centre of supporting on RnD and performing horizon scanning.

Key responsibilities
As referenced in the previous section, you will take lead on a range of technical challenges. However, it is crucial that you are a critical thinker. Much of what you will be doing will be focused on future focused technology, leaning into AI Architecture, and designing solutions that support the delivery of AI models.
Within this role, you will be expected to perform a number of tasks:

Define and assess technical architectures and solutions
Define technical and requirements
Produce high-and-low level technical designs
Define the tools and practices to be used to monitor and support cloud applications
Architect end to end solutions that support the ingestion, processing and storage of data, including, potentially, the deployment of ML or AI models
Architect and make recommendations to rationalise, simplify or optimise architectures
Make recommendations that may support the following:

Digital sovereignty
Compute optimisation
Cost optimisation

This role will touch on many elements, including data platforms, AI architecture, cloud architecture, MLOPs, integration frameworks, DevOps processes.
You will work closely with the BA and Lead Consultant to make strategic recommendations. With the As-Is architecture you will work with the BA to identify where current capability falls short of what is needed for their marketing and data aspirations and will define and recommend a future architecture, along with clear rationale and explanation as to the decisions that have been made.
You will then be required to design a To-Be architecture that not only addresses the desired capabilities whilst also taking into account the client’s maturity and broader business context. You will then work with the BA and Lead Consultant to phase the architecture to align it with business priorities and other dependencies. To To-Be architecture will then be refined by identifying the scope and requirements for each capability area and recommending suitable vendors.
Alongside this role you may be asked to support in the delivery of implementations conducted by our development team. This would see you working with the development team and Head of Development to design Solutions and also guide them on the development to ensure that they are working to specification.
It is imperative that you feel comfortable in front of technical and non-technical clients:

Asking questions to understand the As-Is
Asking questions to gain a full understanding of technical requirements and dependencies
Presenting your proposed architecture
Fielding questions from a range of stakeholders, and “defending” your opinion and design

Skills & experience

Understanding of contemporary software engineering, including the selection and application of appropriate technology and patterns
Confidence working in a team and designing full-stack solutions
Detailed knowledge of at least one major Cloud platform (AWS, Azure, GCP)
Confident in-front of clients and technical stakeholders, explaining design decisions
DevOps and the techniques which enable it, including containerisation, CI/CD and IaC
Relational and non-relational databases
Integration methods and transport protocols e.g. REST API, Kafka etc
Knowledge of Cloud native resources, and their uses and application e.g. Lambdas, Functions, Kubernetes
Experience of working in agile environments
Comfortable working with high-level stakeholders, both internally and externally

Nice to have:

Understanding Integration patterns with MarTech and AdTech products
Digital analytics & tag management – specifically their role in the collect of data and that might be used

About you
You understand differing architecture principles, such as monolith, hybrid or microservices, and are able to articulate their benefits and disadvantages
You are inquisitive and future thinking
You are a strong listener with a superb ability to understand a client requirement, whilst also being able to interrogate and ask questions to get into the detail of solutions
Pragmatic – able to make recommendations that balance the need for new capability vs. the upheaval involved in making change and limiting factors
You are confident in understanding and documenting an as-is architecture and articulating its limitations & challenges
You are an analytical thinker who is able to uniquely think about a problem and create To-Be architectures and phasing which meets a client’s nuanced needs
You will understand interdependencies between systems
You are able to listen to the needs of technical and business stakeholders and interpret them
You are flexible and capable of proactive and reactive communication
You are results driven with a professional approach to project delivery and a successful track record
You have excellent written/verbal English
You are an experienced and effective presenter
You will have superb organisational skills
You have high levels of personal motivation
You are a logical thinker with excellent problem solving
You are commercially confident & able to provide accurate estimations for work
You are a selfless team player who will share knowledge, mentor and develop other members of the team on relevant technology and business trends

title: Category Growth Consultant - Serveware & Buffetware
description:
Serveware & Buffetware – Category Growth Consultant

Libbey is committed to expanding its presence and accelerating growth within the Serveware & Buffetware category. To support this strategic initiative, we are seeking a Category Growth Leader who will serve as the organization's subject matter expert and strategic leader for the category.

As Libbey continues its meaningful entrance into the Serveware & Buffetware market, this role will be responsible for accelerating category knowledge, informing critical strategic and commercial decisions, and establishing a roadmap for sustainable growth. This leader will leverage deep industry expertise to identify market opportunities, guide assortment strategy, strengthen competitive positioning, and help build organizational capabilities within the category.

This leader will partner closely with Sales, Marketing, Product Development, Supply Chain, and Executive Leadership to define where Libbey will compete, how Libbey will win, and how success will be measured.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Lead the development and execution of Libbey's Serveware & Buffetware category growth strategy, establishing a clear roadmap for market expansion and profitable growth.
Validate and refine category opportunities through market analysis, customer insights, competitive intelligence, and industry trends.
Define Libbey's category positioning, assortment architecture, pricing strategy, and product portfolio priorities.
Develop and launch a comprehensive "How to Win" strategy, including target segments, value propositions, and go-to-market recommendations.
Partner with Product Development, Marketing, Sales, Supply Chain, and Leadership teams to align category objectives and execution plans.
Serve as the organization's subject matter expert on Serveware & Buffetware, providing strategic guidance and category insights.
Evaluate competitive offerings and identify opportunities to strengthen Libbey's market position and differentiation.
Establish growth metrics, monitor category performance, and recommend actions to drive revenue and market share growth.
Build commercial capabilities by developing category education, training, and sales enablement programs.
Influence and drive cross-functional decisions that support long-term category growth and customer success.

REQUIREMENTS & QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Hospitality, Culinary Management, or a related field – preferred
10+ years of experience within foodservice, serveware, buffetware, hospitality, tabletop, housewares, or related industries.
Demonstrated success developing and executing category growth, commercial, or go-to-market strategies.
Strong expertise in market assessment, customer segmentation, assortment planning, pricing strategy, and competitive analysis.
Experience influencing and partnering with senior leaders across multiple functions.
Strong strategic thinking, analytical, and problem-solving capabilities.
Excellent presentation, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
Proven ability to drive initiatives from concept through execution and deliver measurable business outcomes.

COMPETENCIES FOR SUCCESS
Behavioral Competencies

Strategy: Consistently share the importance of connecting your functional strategy to Libbey's strategy, leading to successful completion of business goals. Create engagement and understanding by communicating a clear and compelling vision with a concise roadmap and expectations. Live One Libbey, investing in planning and collaboration across functions for the greater good of the company.
Influence: Be a leader who is self-aware, transparent, inclusive, encouraging, and supportive, prioritizing the company's needs. Be a steward of engagement and utilize influence to drive actions that align with Libbey's values. Champion engagement, creating an inclusive, positive, and meaningful experience for all Makers. Develop a legacy of great talent within your function and understand the importance of investing in associates.
Lead & Develop: Coach, mentor, and motivate others to drive high levels of productivity, ongoing learning, and achievement. Inspire and empower others to achieve organizational goals and confidently challenge the status quo. Foster an environment of creativity and encouragement to think outside the box, leading to new ideas and innovations.

Sales Functional Competencies

Customer & Market Understanding: Demonstrates a strong understanding of customers, end users, and the broader market, including key trends, competitive dynamics, and business drivers. Anticipates customer needs by proactively identifying challenges and uncovering opportunities that lead to future projects. Uses insights into customer behavior, product usage, and buying patterns to position Libbey solutions in a way that delivers value beyond the immediate order.
Analysis, Insights & Data-Driven Decision Making: Continuously monitors market conditions, category trends, competitive activity, customer performance, and business trends to anticipate opportunities and risks. Uses insights to inform category strategy, identify growth opportunities, and avoid reactive, short-term decision-making. Leverages strong commercial insight to strengthen business recommendations, prioritize opportunities, and improve outcomes. Balances profitability, competitiveness, customer value, and business objectives when making strategic decisions.
Cross-Functional Partnership, Negotiating & Communication: Partners effectively across Sales, Sales Operations, Marketing, Customer Service, Supply Chain, Product Development, and other internal teams to deliver a consistent, high-value customer experience. Aligns resources and expertise to execute category strategies, solve business challenges, and drive coordinated outcomes. Demonstrates a One Commercial mindset by ensuring alignment across functions in planning and execution. Leverages Libbey's operating rhythms to drive alignment, accountability, and effective solutions.

Assignment Details

This is not a direct hire position. This person will not be classified as a Libbey employee.
This is a consultant role and requires the individual to work as an independent contractor (1099).
The estimated length of the contract assignment is 12 months.
This position will require 40%+ travel (to/from Toledo, OH corporate office, customer visits, territory training, tradeshows, etc.).
This position will report to the Vice President of Foodservice Sales for the United States and Canada, with high levels of engagement with the Vice President of Marketing for the United States and Canada, and the enterprise’s Chief Commercial Officer.

title: Electrical Commissioning Engineer - Data Centers
description:
Position Summary

We are seeking an Electrical Commissioning Engineer to support the planning and execution of commissioning activities for a data center project located in Central Texas. This position will be responsible for developing electrical commissioning scripts and associated test documentation for mission critical systems, while also supporting facility systemization, completions, execution planning, walkdowns, and field leadership during site execution.
The role is expected to work in a hybrid arrangement during the planning and mobilization phase and then transition to site support in 1Q27. Candidates should bring strong technical writing skills, practical commissioning judgment, and the ability to coordinate with project management, design teams, contractors, OEMs, and operations stakeholders in a high-performance data center environment.
Key Responsibilities

Develop detailed electrical commissioning scripts, functional test procedures, readiness plans, and turnover documentation for mission critical electrical systems.
Support facility systemization and subsystem definition, including boundary development, system breakdown structure, and alignment with the overall turnover strategy.
Assist with checksheet assignment in the completions system to support disciplined handover, punch closure, and commissioning progression tracking.
Help develop the commissioning execution plan, including test sequencing, prerequisite management, energization strategy, safety interfaces, vendor support needs, and schedule alignment.
Participate in system walkdowns during execution, verify field readiness, identify deficiencies, and support closeout of outstanding construction and pre-commissioning items.
Help manage commissioning execution at site, including daily interface with contractors, vendors, controls teams, and owner representatives.
Review design drawings, one-lines, control narratives, relay and protection philosophies, specifications, submittals, and vendor manuals to ensure technically sound script development.
Coordinate with project stakeholders to ensure commissioning scripts clearly identify prerequisites, hold points, safe work boundaries, required instrumentation, expected outcomes, alarm responses, and acceptance criteria.
Support integrated systems testing and interface verification with mechanical, controls, EPMS, BMS, and operations teams.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Engineering Technology, or related discipline; equivalent relevant experience will also be considered.
Experience in electrical commissioning, startup, testing, operations, construction support, or related field execution for complex facilities.
Experience with electrical distribution systems utilizing three sources of power, including utility service, gas generator back-up, and BESS.
Strong understanding of medium- and low-voltage distribution systems, including switchgear, UPS, generators, ATS/STS, PDUs, grounding, and associated controls or monitoring interfaces.
Ability to interpret one-line diagrams, schematics, control narratives, vendor documentation, and technical specifications.
Working knowledge of national and Texas regulatory requirements relevant to commissioning execution, electrical safety, hazardous energy control, and construction/startup coordination.
Ability to travel and mobilize to the project site for execution in 1Q27.

Preferred Qualifications

Previous experience supporting data center commissioning or other mission critical facilities.
Understanding of LEED concepts, documentation expectations, and sustainability-related commissioning deliverables.
Familiarity with ASHRAE guidance applicable to mission critical environments and data center design and operation.
Experience using completions or turnover management systems for checksheet assignment, system tracking, and handover progress reporting.
Knowledge of site execution leadership, field issue resolution, and management of commissioning teams during startup and integrated testing.

Work AuthorizationCandidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of application and for the duration of employment. Employer sponsorship of work visas is not available for this position.

Position Title: Quality Control Inspector IReports to: Quality SupervisorDepartment: Quality AssuranceJob Classification: Non-Exempt Labor Category: IndirectStatus: Full Time
Position Description:The Quality Inspector I performs mechanical, visual, electrical, and dimensional inspections of components, assemblies, finished goods, and incoming materials in accordance with approved drawings, specifications, workmanship standards, and procedures. This role verifies documentation accuracy, including DHR entries, supplier documentation (IQC only), certificates of compliance, and labeling, and records inspection results in compliance with Good Documentation Practices (GDP). The Inspector I uses calibrated inspection tools to measure defined product attributes, follows established procedures, escalates issues when guidance is needed, and works under direct to moderate supervision while supporting company values and continuous improvement efforts.
Position Authority:This position has the authority to accept or reject components, assemblies and finished goods to pre-established guidelines to assure acceptable components are approved and nonconforming components, assemblies and finished goods are not released for use or distribution.
Essential Job Functions:• Performs visual, mechanical, electrical, and dimensional inspections of incoming material, in‑process product, labeling, and final assemblies.• Records inspections and reviews DHRs for completeness, correctness, and compliance with GDP practices.• Verifies label accuracy against approved artwork, component specifications, and documentation.• Measures product attributes using calipers, templates, magna‑mike (wall thickness), pin gauges, rulers, and other inspection equipment.• Reviews component specifications (CS/PS) to confirm whether a defect is listed and applicable to the product under inspection.• Documents inspection results accurately into inspection forms, DHRs, or electronic systems.• Performs AQL sampling plans accordingly • Reviews supplier documentation packages; including drawings, purchasing specs, PS/CS, and CoCs for completeness, revision accuracy, and correctness (IQC only).• Initiates nonconformance reports when documentation or product does not meet requirements.• Communicates defects or documentation gaps professionally to Buyer/Planner, Engineering, or Quality leadership.• Adheres to discrepancy reporting methods using NCRs, Quarantine tags, scrap tags, and hold processes.
Knowledge and Education: High school education or equivalent.  Minimum of one year experience in an inspection environment using handheld inspection equipment preferred ASQ certification desirable.
Job Experience:
 Experience using basic inspection tools (e.g., calipers, gauges, simple electronic equipment).  Basic experience performing visual/dimensional inspections per drawings/specifications.  Able to review documentation for accuracy (DHRs and supplier documents). Able to handle chemicals safely.
Skills and Competencies:
 Able to communicate clearly in writing and verbally. Basic computer skills for entering and reviewing inspection records. Follow instructions and apply basic common-sense judgment. Performs basic math for measurement interpretation. Able to review documentation (DHRs, specifications, labels) for accuracy. Able to send clear email notifications when required (IQC only). Comfortable working with inspection tools and documentation systems.
Equipment Used:Mechanical and electrical equipment, calipers, gauges, standard office equipment, carts, ladders, Laminar flow benches, and inspection and testing equipment.
Physical Requirements:
 Light physical activity performing non-strenuous, day-to-day activities of a primarily productive nature.  Moderate lifting (35 lbs.), carrying (10 lbs.), bending, and prolonged sitting.  Manual dexterity is sufficient to reach/handle items, work with fingers, and perceive attributes of objects and material. Intensive handwork. Ability to visually inspect small components and detailed features with normal or corrected vision. Requires the ability to identify and distinguish colors and shapes. Requires the ability to sit and stand for extended periods. Well-lighted, air-conditioned, indoor laboratory/production setting with adequate ventilation.

title: Clinical Consultant (BCBA)
description:
Clinical Consultant – PBIS Full-Time | Pennsylvania (Greater Philly area) | May Institute
Advance Systems. Build Capacity. Lead with Expertise. Join May Institute’s nationally recognized Positive Behavior Interventions and Supports (PBIS) and school consultation team as a Clinical Consultant, where your expertise as a skilled consultant and Board-Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) will drive large-scale impact across schools, districts, and agencies. You’ll provide high-level consultation, coaching, and capacity-building to shape inclusive, data-informed systems that support student success. This is an ideal role for experienced clinicians seeking to expand their influence beyond direct service—offering a dynamic mix of school-based consultation, systems design, professional development, and leadership.
What You’ll Do

Lead School-Based Behavioral Consultation: Deliver expert consultation to public and private schools implementing PBIS and multi-tiered systems of support (MTSS), with a focus on improving equity, access, and behavioral outcomes.
Guide Functional Behavior Assessment & Intervention: Conduct advanced functional behavior assessments (FBAs) and design individualized behavior support plans that align with ethical standards and best practices in the field.
Coach Educators and Leadership Teams: Provide ongoing training, coaching, and technical assistance to school staff and administrators, ensuring fidelity of implementation and staff capacity-building.
Drive Systems-Level Change: Collaborate with district leaders to assess, develop, and refine school-wide systems, practices, and data tools that support sustainable behavioral and academic success.
Lead Data-Driven Decision Making: Support teams in collecting, analyzing, and using data to inform instruction, monitor interventions, and evaluate overall system performance.
Serve as part of a Program Evaluation Team: Assist with program evaluations in collaboration with program stakeholders to assess implementation of evidenced-based practices and inform development of comprehensive recommendations to support program enhancement, professional development for school staff, and maximize outcomes for students.

What You Bring

Certification: Active BCBA certification (Preferred)
Education: Master’s degree in Applied Behavior Analysis, Psychology, or a related field. Ph.D. in Applied Behavior Analysis or related field highly preferred.
Experience: Minimum 3–5 years post-certification, with demonstrated experience in school-based settings, systems-level consultation, and capacity-building.
Expertise: Strong working knowledge of PBIS, MTSS, and function-based behavior support strategies in K–12 environments.
Skills: Exceptional communication, facilitation, and coaching skills with the ability to lead multidisciplinary teams and manage complex organizational dynamics. Demonstrated proficiency with Microsoft 365 and associated applications (Word, Excel, Teams, etc.).
Mindset: Commitment to equity-centered practices, cultural responsiveness, and inclusion for all students.

Why Join Us?

Broaden Your Impact: Work across schools and districts to drive scalable, sustainable changes that benefit thousands of students.
Lead With Autonomy: Take ownership of your consultation portfolio with flexibility, support, and trust in your clinical judgment.
National Reach, Local Focus: Be part of a respected national nonprofit while working directly with regional education partners and school communities.
Professional Excellence: Join a team of experienced BCBAs and clinicians committed to collaboration, innovation, and continuous learning.
Comprehensive Benefits: Enjoy robust benefits including competitive compensation, medical/dental/vision insurance, 403(b) with employer match, tuition reimbursement, student loan support, and more.
$5,000 Sign-On Bonus to welcome you to the team.
CompensationWe recognize and reward your expertise: $78,000 - $85,000

Who We Are: May Institute’s PBIS and School Consultation Division partners with public and private schools to promote inclusive practices, strengthen multi-tiered systems of support, and improve behavioral outcomes for all students. Backed by decades of expertise in applied behavior analysis (ABA), our work blends clinical excellence with a deep commitment to educational equity and social-emotional wellbeing. Ready to lead where clinical skills meet systems change?
Make a positive impact – Apply today!
