title: Director, Performance Engineering & Commissioning - Service Line Development
location: McLean, VA, US; New York, NY, US
description:
SummaryThe Director, Engineering & Commissioning – Service Line Development is a senior technical leader focused on creating, validating, and scaling new performance engineering, commissioning, and decarbonization services for commercial real estate, particularly existing buildings. Positioned initially within the Growth Team, the role shapes market-ready service offerings, expands technical capabilities, validates client demand, and drives revenue growth.
The role partners closely with Account Management and Solutions & Services leadership to align technical solutions with market needs and commercial strategy. While execution is led by established delivery teams, this position provides senior technical guidance and may engage in early-stage or pilot work to test demand and reduce risk.
Designed to evolve over time, the role requires comfort with ambiguity and a proactive approach to defining priorities, structure, and long-term engineering leadership as services mature. It is hybrid-flexible and based in McLean, VA or New York City.
Key Responsibilities

Service Strategy, Definition and Validation

Quickly assess market demand, client needs, internal capabilities and competitor offerings to identify and prioritize new performance engineering, commissioning, and decarbonization service offerings with near term and long term revenue potential.
Define, build and scale new engineering and commissioning service offerings from concept through market validation, translating execution-level expertise into clear, market-ready scopes, methodologies, and value propositions.
Establish technical frameworks, quality standards, and delivery assumptions that enable consistency, rigor, and scalability across portfolios and clients.

Early-Stage Execution & Technical Oversight (as needed)

Provide senior technical oversight during pilot or early stage engagements to validate service approaches, confirm level of effort assumptions, and identify delivery risks or capability gaps.
Engage, where necessary, directly in project execution in coordination with existing technical team members to support early validation, prove demand, or accelerate readiness while delivery capacity is built.
Capture lessons learned from early work and translate them into refined service definitions, standards, and delivery models.

Commercialization, Growth & Internal Enablement

Translate technical capabilities into clear, commercially viable service offerings that can be confidently positioned, sold, and delivered.
Partner closely with Growth, Account Management, and Solutions & Services leadership to support proposals, renewals, and client conversations, ensuring offerings align with client planning and investment decision cycles.
Support business development by contributing technical credibility, scoping input, and client facing narratives that connect services to asset performance, compliance readiness, and value creation.

Organizational Enablement & Talent Development

Partner with delivery leaders to prepare services and delivery model for operational scale, including documentation, standards, and transition plans into Solutions & Services.
Build and mentor technical talent required to sustain new service growth, contributing to the design of future technical leadership pathways informed by service incubation.
Represent RE Tech externally through industry engagement, technical forums, and associations (e.g., BOMA, ASHRAE, USGBC.) contributing to thought leadership and market visibility.

How this Role Operates

This role is accountable for defining and validating what the firm is prepared to sell and scale, rather than owning ongoing project delivery.
Acts as senior technical authority and advisor, accountable for service definition and scale-up rather than day-to-day execution.
Enables delivery through established technical teams.
Focuses on scalability, rigor and repeatability, not bespoke one-off solutions.
Works across the organization during periods of growth and transition.

Essential Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

Ability to translate technical or operational analysis into financial or investment-relevant insights (e.g., impacts to NOI, CapEx, valuation, or risk exposure.)
Ability to advise clients with a strong understanding of how institutional investors make decisions, translating complex analyses into financially relevant, defensible recommendations
aligned with investment objectives, risk management, and long term value creation.
Strong analytical and problem solving skills, with the judgment to synthesize data, evaluate trade offs, and develop practical recommendations that support value creation, risk mitigation, and informed decision making.
Exceptional communication skills (written and verbal), including the ability to produce clear, concise, and executive ready materials and to confidently engage in client discussions, presentations, and internal forums.
Collaborative leadership capability, with demonstrated ability to work effectively across disciplines, levels, and organizations to co create solutions and deliver successful client outcomes.
Ability to operate effectively in fast paced, evolving environments, managing multiple priorities, adapting to changing client needs, and maintaining quality and momentum under time pressure.
Strong stakeholder management skills, including the ability to manage relationships up, down, and across organizations, navigate complex interpersonal dynamics, and build trust with clients, partners, and internal teams.
High degree of initiative, ownership, and follow through, with a proactive approach to identifying opportunities, improving how work is delivered, and supporting business growth.
Sound professional judgment and business ethics, including discretion, integrity, and the ability to handle confidential and proprietary information appropriately.
Growth mindset, with a commitment to continuous learning, professional development, and contributing to a culture of improvement for oneself, colleagues, and client work.
Deep expertise on building enclosure systems.
Expertise in HVAC, electrification, commissioning, and decarbonization.
Strong understanding of CFD, heat transfer, thermal modeling.
Advanced knowledge of ASRHAE, Energy Codes, MEES, CRREM.
Advanced knowledge of LL97 and Building Energy Performance Standards.

Required Education and/or Experience

15+ years of progressive MEP engineering experience.
Professional Engineer (PE) license
Experience working directly with institutional investors or their operating platforms.
Demonstrated experience with portfolio-level decision-making, not just single-asset or one-off project work.
Experience serving in an advisory capacity, where success depended on influencing decisions rather than simply producing outputs.
Experience in supporting business development and sales
Experience leading complex technical work and cross-disciplinary teams, including the following types of engineering and commissioning projects:
MEP modernization and building performance engineering.
Energy studies, modeling, commissioning, IAQ testing, and compliance.
Evaluation of whole-building performance and guide integrated solutions.

Preferred Experience

Experience working in an advisory, consulting, and/or contracting firm, managing client engagements.
Experience with eQuest, DOE-2, DesignBuilder, IES

Travel Requirements Periodic travel is required for the role. title: Sustainability Coordinator
description:
The Breakdown:

The Sustainability Coordinator advances Burton's work across chemistry, climate, and product reporting. This role is a custodian of Burton's chemistry, product and supply chain environmental data and helps translate that data into testing programs and external reporting. This role exists to keep Burton's responsible chemistry program running reliably, to maintain the accuracy of the emissions data behind Burton's climate commitments, and to deliver the certifications, audits, and reporting that substantiate Burton's product claims to certifying bodies and wholesale partners. Reporting to the Product Sustainability Manager and working with global teams, the Coordinator blends technical skill, strong attention to detail, and cross-functional collaboration to help ensure Burton's products, operations, and supply chain meet strict sustainability standards. Burton's sustainability team is small and highly collaborative, so this role also offers real exposure to projects across the wider sustainability portfolio and room to grow into new areas over time.

What You Get to Do:

Conduct seasonal risk-based material testing across all product categories, including verification testing that upholds Burton's PFAS-free commitment. Maintain working knowledge of Burton's restricted substances lists (bluesign, AFIRM) to reduce chemical risk to workers, customers, communities, and the environment.
Conduct research and analysis on materials chemistry and supplier chemical management practices to inform continuous improvement and Burton's responsible chemistry strategy.
Partner with Burton's Compliance Analyst where product chemistry and regulatory compliance intersect, supplying chemical, material, and testing data to support compliance reporting.
Collect and validate Burton Facility Environmental data (Energy, Water, Waste) and partner with regional operations managers to maintain data integrity
Administer Tier 1 and Tier 2 Chemical Management programs including supplier-facing resources, training, and factory onboarding. Contribute to strategies for worker and community health and safety, covering occupational health, waste, pollution, and emissions, to raise standards across Burton's manufacturing base.
Support the Senior Supply Chain Social Impact Lead to collect and analyze Higg FEM reporting with suppliers
Support the Product Sustainability Manager, who owns Burton's product certification portfolio (including bluesign, Forest Stewardship Council, Leather Working Group, and Responsible Down Standard), by compiling and submitting documentation for certification and recertification.
Complete recurring sustainability reporting and questionnaires for key wholesale accounts, including Zalando and REI, partnering with Sales, Merchandising, and Product teams to align submissions with seasonal go-to-market timelines and position Burton favorably in retailer sustainability programs.

What You'll Bring to The Team:

Required

2 - 4 years of experience in sustainability, product quality, environmental health and safety, or a closely related field (ideally within apparel, footwear, outdoor, or consumer products)
Relevant education, training, or experience in environmental science, chemistry, or sustainability
Demonstrated experience managing detailed data sets and delivering accurate reporting against recurring deadlines.

Preferred

Familiarity with restricted substances lists and chemical management frameworks (bluesign, AFIRM, ZDHC) and with material testing protocols.
Exposure to chemical management practices in Tier 1 and Tier 2 manufacturing environments.
Experience working directly with external partners such as suppliers, third-party labs, auditors, or certifying bodies.
Working knowledge of greenhouse gas accounting across Scopes 1, 2, and 3, and experience with a carbon accounting platform such as Watershed.
Experience with certification or audit frameworks such as Higg FEM, B Corp, FSC, or RDS.
Experience completing retailer or customer sustainability questionnaires and scorecards.
Experience collaborating with colleagues and partners across time zones and cultures.

Core Capabilities That Would Help You Succeed in This Role:

Exceptional attention to detail, with the discipline to keep large, technical data sets accurate.
Strong data fluency: comfortable working in Excel and reporting platforms, and able to spot and resolve inconsistencies.
Ability to translate technical chemistry and emissions information into clear guidance for non-technical partners across Product, Sourcing, Sales, and Marketing.
Manages complexity: comfortable supporting many concurrent recurring cycles, seasonal testing, certification renewals, audits, and retailer reporting, without letting deadlines slip.
Collaborates and influences without decision-making authority, building trust with suppliers and internal teams to move standards forward.
Nimble learning and curiosity: the standards, frameworks, and expectations in this space shift constantly, and this role stays ahead of them.
Instills trust through integrity with data and claims, including the judgment to escalate rather than overstate when evidence is incomplete.
Appetite to stretch into unfamiliar areas as the sustainability team’s priorities evolve.

How Your Success Will Be Measured:

Completion of seasonal material testing on schedule, and conformance rates against Burton’s restricted substances lists.
Maintenance of Burton's PFAS-free status across new materials and suppliers.
Supplier participation in and performance improvement across Tier 1 and Tier 2 chemical management programs.
Accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of inputs to carbon measurement.
Timely, complete, and accurate submission of certification documentation and audit materials.
On-time, accurate delivery of wholesale account sustainability reporting.
Progress against Burton’s broader climate and product sustainability goals.
Strength of cross-functional and supplier partnerships.

Work / Physical Environment:

This position is in a typical, stationary office setting. Over 80% of the day will be spent sitting in one location.
Occasional time in warehouse, manufacturing, or lab environments may require safety training and personal protective equipment.
Commitments: Salaried, Exempt, Year-Round.

More Info to Seal the Deal:

Burton’s benefit package includes medical, dental, and vision insurance, flexible spending account, company paid life insurance, company paid short- and long-term disability insurance, great parental benefits, k plan with company match, and paid time-off. Other perks include a discounted season pass, lesson reimbursement program, product discounts, free demo equipment, company ride days, casual work environment, and many more!

This is a full-time salaried role, based at our headquarters in Burlington, Vermont and will be required to be on site at least 4 days per week. We will offer relocation assistance to move to Vermont to any candidate who is hired. The hiring range for this role is $60,000-$75-000, depending on relevant experience and/or education, specific skills, function, and available budget. Please note that the range details above reflect the base pay only and does not include any potential bonus and other benefits that we offer.

title: Controls Installation QA/QC Supervisor
description:

This role is critical in maintaining installation standards, protecting system integrity, and ensuring project schedules are met without compromising quality.
The Controls Installation QA/QC (Coordinator/Inspector/Supervisor) will be responsible for verifying that all BAS/controls installations—including conduit, wiring, devices, controllers, and network infrastructure—are installed in accordance with design documents, specifications, and industry best practices. This individual will serve as the field-level quality authority representing the system integration team, working closely with our mechanical team, controls contractors, electrical contractors, commissioners, and project management.
Key Responsibilities

Installation Quality Assurance & Field Verification
Perform daily field inspections of building automation installation work across active construction projects.
Verify the correct installation of:

Control conduit pathways and support methods
Low-voltage and communication wiring practices (routing, labeling, termination, shielding, grounding)
Field devices (sensors, actuators, valves, dampers, flow switches, etc.)
Control panels, controllers, and network hardware

Ensure installations comply with:

Project specifications and control sequences
Approved submittals and shop drawings
Applicable electrical codes and industry standards
Identify installation deficiencies early and provide clear corrective direction to subcontractors.

Network Infrastructure & Systems Readiness

Validate BAS network architecture readiness, including:

IP network backbone and field-level communication networks
BACnet/IP, MS/TP, and other protocol integrity
Device addressing, termination, and segmentation
Confirm proper installation of network switches, routers, and communication trunks supporting BAS integration.
Coordinate with IT, electrical, and mechanical teams to ensure system connectivity is complete and functional prior to commissioning

Schedule & Construction Coordination

Actively monitor installation progress against project schedules and milestones.
Identify risks to schedule due to incomplete or improper installation.
Work with subcontractors to streamline installation sequencing and eliminate rework.
Participate in coordination meetings with general contractors, electrical contractors, and BAS subcontractors.
Drive accountability for installation productivity without compromising quality.

Read, interpret, and enforce compliance with:

Mechanical, electrical, and controls construction drawings
Control diagrams, riser diagrams, and network architecture drawings
Identify conflicts, design gaps, or constructability issues and develop clear documentation for resolution.

Prepare and submit:

RFIs (Requests for Information) to resolve design ambiguities or conflicts
ASIs (Architect’s Supplemental Instructions) tracking and implementation coordination
Maintain detailed field reports documenting progress, deficiencies, and corrective actions.

Deficiency Tracking & Quality Control Process

Establish and maintain a structured deficiency tracking system.
Categorize issues by severity (safety, functional, schedule impact, compliance).
Ensure timely closure of punch list items related to BAS/controls installation.
Verify corrective work is completed properly before acceptance

Coordination & Contractor Management

Maintain strong working relationships with BAS subcontractors, electrical contractors, and commissioning agents.
Provide firm but collaborative field leadership to enforce installation standards.
Support a solution-driven environment focused on system performance and integration success.
Adapt to dynamic jobsite conditions while maintaining quality expectations.

Required Qualifications

Minimum 5+ years of hands-on experience in BAS/controls installation, field execution, or related commissioning/QA/QC role.
Strong understanding of HVAC systems, BAS architecture, and control system integration.
Ability to read and interpret:
Construction drawings (mechanical, electrical, controls)
Control schematics and sequences of operation
Network risers and panel layouts
Proven field experience with low-voltage wiring, control devices, and BAS network infrastructure.
Working knowledge of communication protocols such as BACnet, Modbus, and IP-based BAS systems.
Experience identifying installation deficiencies and driving corrective actions in a construction environment.
Demonstrated ability to create and manage RFIs and ASIs.

Core Competencies

Strong attention to detail with a quality-first mindset
Excellent communication and field coordination skills
Ability to manage multiple active job sites and competing priorities
Strong problem-solving and critical thinking skills in fast-paced construction environments
Highly motivated, self-directed, and accountable
Flexible and collaborative approach when working with multiple contractors and stakeholders

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with enterprise BAS platforms and integration environments
Familiarity with commissioning processes and functional testing workflows
OSHA certification or strong construction safety awareness
Experience working in large commercial, healthcare, or mission-critical facilities.

Success in This Role Looks Like

BAS installations consistently meet design intent with minimal rework
Reduced installation errors and improved first-pass inspection success
Improved coordination between trades, leading to smoother project execution
Controls systems are fully ready for commissioning without delays caused by installation deficiencies
Construction schedules are protected through proactive field oversight

title: Mechanical Commissioning Engineer - Data Centers
description:
Position Summary

We are seeking a Mechanical Commissioning Engineer to support the planning and execution of commissioning activities for a data center project. This position will be responsible for developing mechanical commissioning scripts and associated test documentation for critical cooling, engine powered generators and support systems, while also supporting facility systemization, completions, execution planning, walkdowns, and field leadership during site execution.
The role is expected to work in a hybrid arrangement during the planning and mobilization phase and then transition to site in 1Q27. Candidates should bring strong technical writing skills, practical commissioning judgment, and the ability to coordinate with project management, design teams, contractors, OEMs, TAB personnel, controls teams, and operations stakeholders in a mission critical environment.
Key Responsibilities

Develop detailed mechanical commissioning scripts, functional test procedures, readiness plans, and turnover documentation for critical cooling and support systems.
Support facility systemization and subsystem definition, including boundary development, mechanical system breakdown structure, and alignment with the overall turnover strategy.
Assist with checksheet assignment in the completions system to support disciplined handover, punch closure, and commissioning progression tracking.
Help develop the commissioning execution plan, including test sequencing, prerequisite management, flushing and cleanliness planning, vendor support needs, and schedule alignment.
Participate in system walkdowns during execution, verify field readiness, identify deficiencies, and support closeout of outstanding construction and pre-commissioning items.
Help manage commissioning execution at site, including daily interface with contractors, OEMs, TAB personnel, controls teams, and owner representatives.
Review P&IDs, equipment submittals, sequences of operation, specifications, vendor manuals, and controls documentation to ensure technically sound script development.
Coordinate with project stakeholders to ensure commissioning scripts clearly identify prerequisites, hold points, safe conditions, required instrumentation, expected outcomes, failure response, and acceptance criteria.
Support integrated systems testing and interface verification with electrical, controls, EPMS, BMS, and operations teams.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Engineering Technology, or related discipline; equivalent relevant experience will also be considered.
Experience in mechanical commissioning, startup, testing, operations, construction support, or related field execution for complex facilities.
Strong working knowledge of data center or commercial and industrial mechanical systems, such as chilled water systems, CRAH/CRAC equipment, pumps, cooling towers or fluid coolers, ventilation, and controls interfaces.
Working knowledge of diesel engine back-up power generation units to support integrated power system testing and commissioning coordination.
Ability to interpret P&IDs, control diagrams, sequences of operation, equipment layouts, vendor documentation, and technical specifications.
Working knowledge of national and Texas regulatory requirements relevant to commissioning execution, mechanical safety, hazardous energy control, and construction/startup coordination.
Ability to travel and mobilize to Temple, Texas for site execution in 1Q27.

Preferred Qualifications

Previous experience supporting data center commissioning or other mission critical facilities.
Understanding of LEED concepts, documentation expectations, and sustainability-related commissioning deliverables.
Familiarity with ASHRAE guidance applicable to mission critical environments and data center thermal performance expectations.
Experience using completions or turnover management systems for checksheet assignment, system tracking, and handover progress reporting.
Knowledge of site execution leadership, field issue resolution, and management of commissioning teams during startup and integrated testing.

Work Authorization
Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of application and for the duration of employment. Employer sponsorship of work visas is not available for this position.

Whether you’re experienced in optics or eager to learn, this is an opportunity to start a fulfilling career in a growing field!
What You’ll Do:

Review prescriptions and work closely with patients to choose the ideal eyewear for both medical needs and aesthetic preferences
Provide honest and thoughtful guidance on frame choices, ensuring patients leave satisfied with their vision and style
Achieve sales goals while delivering outstanding customer service and meeting individual patient needs
Manage and maintain eyewear inventory to ensure a great selection of frames and lenses
Perform adjustments and repairs on eyewear, offering personalized service that makes a lasting impression
Collaborate with physicians to address prescription questions and provide clarity on eye-related concerns

What We’re Looking For:

0-3 years of experience (Optical experience is a plus, but we’ll train the right candidate!)
Strong organizational and multitasking skills to thrive in a fast-paced environment
Coachable attitude—ready to learn and grow in the optical field
Flexibility and adaptability to meet changing patient needs and office demands
Professional phone etiquette and a warm, approachable demeanor

Why You’ll Love Working Here:

Training and growth – Don’t have optical experience? No problem! We provide full training to help you succeed.
Career advancement – The more you learn and grow, the more opportunities there are to advance within the company!
Supportive team environment – Join a group of like-minded professionals dedicated to helping each other and the patients we serve.
Sales incentives and recognition – Achieve goals while helping patients and enjoy rewards for your hard work!

If you’re ready to help people see their best, while building a rewarding career in the optical field, we’d love to meet you. Apply today to start your journey as an Optician!

title: Expeditions and rentals coordinator
description:
As the leader of a team of 15 to 20 seasonal employees, the Expeditions and rentals coordinator (Expedition Program, C-Vert Program, Rentals, Groups and Special Events) is responsible for welcoming clients to the site and ensuring the effective delivery of programs in accordance with the expectations of YMCA Kanawana Camp.
Working closely with the expeditions and rentals management team at YMCA Kanawana Camp, the Supervisor is a member of the camp’s leadership team and collaborates with the full-time staff to maintain and foster a healthy, positive, and impactful culture for all stakeholders of YMCA Kanawana Camp.
The Challenge We Offer You

Plan, manage, and oversee all activities and operations of the YMCA Kanawana Camp Outdoor Education Centre.
Ensure the quality of all services under your responsibility.
Maintain rigorous operational management, including customer service and equipment management related to outdoor education activities.
Develop high-quality programming aligned with YMCA Kanawana’s environmental and human-centered values.
In collaboration with your team, review all programs annually and ensure the integration and adherence to the quality standards established by the association.
Implement risk management and safety standards for activity areas, expedition programs, and the Outdoor Education Centre, in accordance with industry-leading standards (ACQ, AEQ, YMCA Canada, MAPAQ, CITQ, outdoor recreation federations, etc.).
Manage reservations for all Outdoor Education Centre activities in accordance with YMCA customer service standards.
Oversee all human resources functions for the programs under your responsibility (groups, rentals, expeditions, special events), including recruitment, onboarding, orientation, and training.
Coach and supervise staff under your authority and conduct performance evaluations.
Plan and organize employee recognition activities.
Maintain inventory records and monitor equipment at the end of each season to support effective budget management, in collaboration with the Outdoor Education Centre Director.
Manage the purchase of equipment, supplies, and other materials for YMCA Kanawana Camp within established parameters and oversee inventory management.
Be accountable for the overall customer experience at the Outdoor Education Centre and ensure high-quality customer service for all stakeholders, including clients, partners, donors, and others.
Collect, consolidate, and distribute client complaints, comments, and suggestions to the appropriate staff members.
Identify potential customer groups and cultivate relationships during the off-season.
Stay informed about the needs of current clients, prospective clients, and the surrounding community.

Why Join the YMCA?
By joining our team, you will discover an environment where mutual support and collaboration are at the heart of everything we do. Contributing to our organization means having the opportunity to:

Develop your expertise.
Work alongside passionate professionals.
Make a positive social impact.
Collaborate with committed partners.
Create meaningful change in people’s lives.
Enjoy the autonomy needed to take on stimulating challenges.

Our Benefits

Access to an Employee and Family Assistance Program (EFAP).
Free membership to our fitness facilities and employee discounts on various programs and services.
Comprehensive group insurance coverage, including medical, dental, prescription drugs, life insurance, and professional services such as massage therapy, psychology, physiotherapy, naturopathy, and more.
Access to telemedicine services through Dialogue’s Lumino Health platform.
Retirement savings plan with a 5% employee contribution matched by the YMCA.
In addition to annual vacation, paid leave for illness, personal well-being, and family responsibilities.
A bank of 70 hours of paid leave available after the probationary period.

The Ideal Candidate Should

Hold a bachelor’s degree in recreation, education, outdoor leadership, or a related field.
Have at least 3 years of coordination experience in a residential camp or adventure tourism setting, or 5 years in a day camp environment.
Have experience with canoe-camping expeditions; additional experience in tourism and hospitality is considered an asset.
Have experience managing staff in a seasonal coaching and supervision context.
Possess strong knowledge of accredited residential camps and adventure tourism industries.
Have solid knowledge of risk management and administrative processes required to coordinate diverse groups in an outdoor education setting.
Demonstrate creativity and innovation.
Exhibit integrity and strong professional ethics.
Be responsible and organized.
Have a people-centered and caring approach.
Demonstrate excellent customer service and active listening skills.
Be attentive to the needs of clients and partners.
Be proficient in French.
Be proficient in English, as the position requires regular oral and written communication in English.
Have no criminal record restrictions related to the position.

title: Sr. Analytics Program Manager
description:
Sr. Analytics Program Manager

Department: Reporting and AnalyticsLocation: RemoteFLSA Status: Exempt
People Leader: NoTravel: <5%

Summary
Company Summary
Accuity partners with hospitals and health systems through a technology-enabled, physician-led model that improves clinical documentation integrity, coding accuracy, reimbursement optimization, and quality outcomes.

Job Summary
The Sr. Analytics Program Manager is responsible for managing the intake, prioritization, requirements gathering, governance, and delivery coordination processes supporting Accuity's Reporting & Analytics organization. This role serves as the primary liaison between business stakeholders and analytics delivery teams, ensuring reporting, analytics, and decision support initiatives are properly defined, prioritized, documented, and executed.

The Sr. Analytics Program Manager focuses on defining the "what," "why," and "when" behind reporting and analytics initiatives while partnering closely with Client Analytics, Decision Support, Operations, Clinical Operations, Product, Technology, Client Success, Finance, and Executive Leadership teams. By creating structure, transparency, and accountability around analytics requests and priorities, this role enables analytics resources to focus on delivering high-quality insights and business value.

This role plays a critical part in establishing analytics governance, improving stakeholder experience, strengthening reporting standards, supporting data governance efforts, and enhancing the overall effectiveness of the Reporting & Analytics function.

Responsibilities
Analytics Intake and Demand Management

Serve as the primary intake and coordination point for reporting, analytics, dashboard, and decision support requests across the organization.
Establish and maintain intake processes that improve visibility, prioritization, and management of analytics work.
Evaluate incoming requests to ensure sufficient business context, requirements, and justification are provided before work begins.
Partner with stakeholders to clarify objectives, business needs, expected outcomes, and success measures.
Maintain visibility into analytics demand, capacity, priorities, and resource allocation.

Requirements Gathering and Business Analysis

Lead requirements gathering activities for reporting, analytics, and decision support initiatives.
Translate business objectives into clearly documented functional requirements, business rules, data requirements, and acceptance criteria.
Facilitate stakeholder discussions to align expectations, resolve ambiguities, and define desired outcomes.
Document and maintain requirements, process flows, use cases, dependencies, and supporting materials.
Ensure requirements are complete, actionable, and aligned with organizational priorities before work is assigned.

Analytics Governance and Prioritization

Support governance processes that establish clear prioritization, ownership, accountability, and transparency across analytics initiatives.
Facilitate prioritization discussions and elevate competing demands, resource constraints, and business tradeoffs.
Maintain visibility into analytics project portfolios, work queues, and initiative status.
Partner with leadership to align analytics resources with strategic priorities and business objectives.
Promote consistent governance practices across reporting and analytics functions.

Delivery Coordination and Program Management

Partner with Product, Technology, Reporting & Analytics, and business leadership to align reporting and analytics initiatives with enterprise product strategy, platform capabilities, and business priorities.
Coordinate reporting and analytics initiatives from intake through delivery and implementation.
Monitor timelines, milestones, dependencies, risks, and stakeholder commitments.
Define and track success measures for major analytics deliverables, including stakeholder adoption, usage, decision impact, operational efficiency, and business outcomes.
Facilitate communication among business stakeholders, analytics teams, Product, Technology, and operational leaders.
Interface directly with engineering and technology scrum teams to ensure alignment on requirements and delivery
Proactively identify risks and obstacles that may impact successful delivery and drive timely resolution.
Ensure stakeholders remain informed regarding progress, timelines, dependencies, and changes.

Data Governance and Reporting Standards

Support development and maintenance of reporting standards, data definitions, metrics governance, and analytics documentation.
Partner with Reporting & Analytics, Technology, Product, and Operations leadership to establish and maintain a centralized metrics dictionary. Work directly with engineering and technology teams to ensure alignment of metric definitions to underlying data architecture.
Promote consistency in reporting definitions, business rules, and analytics practices across the organization.
Assist in documenting data requirements, source dependencies, and reporting assumptions.
Contribute to data governance initiatives that improve reporting quality, consistency, and stakeholder trust.

Stakeholder Partnership and Communications

Build strong relationships with operational, clinical, financial, product, technology, and executive stakeholders.
Serve as a trusted advisor to business partners seeking analytics and reporting support.
Facilitate productive discussions regarding reporting needs, priorities, tradeoffs, and expectations.
Improve stakeholder understanding of analytics capabilities, processes, and delivery timelines.
Promote collaboration and alignment between business functions and analytics teams.

Process Improvement and Organizational Effectiveness

Identify opportunities to improve analytics intake, governance, requirements management, communication, and delivery processes.
Develop repeatable tools, templates, workflows, and documentation standards that improve operational efficiency.
Support continuous improvement initiatives that enhance the effectiveness and scalability of the Reporting & Analytics organization.
Contribute to organizational maturity in analytics governance, business analysis, and stakeholder management.
Recommend process enhancements that improve stakeholder experience and analytics delivery outcomes.

Other Duties as Assigned

Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned to support business needs.

Qualifications
Education and Credentials

Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Healthcare Administration, Information Systems, Analytics, Finance, Operations, or a related field required.
Master's degree in Business Administration, Healthcare Administration, Analytics, Information Management, or a related discipline preferred.
One or more of the following certifications preferred: Certified Business Analysis Professional (CBAP, Project Management Professional (PMP), Agile Certification, Scrum Certification, and/or other relevant business analysis, project management, or analytics certifications.

Experience

Minimum of 5 years of progressive experience in analytics program management, business analysis, reporting governance, project management, or related disciplines.
Healthcare industry experience required, with analytics, reporting, business intelligence, decision support, or data-driven business experience.
Experience gathering, documenting, and translating business needs into actionable reporting, analytics, technology, or operational requirements.
Experience managing intake, prioritization, governance, or project portfolio processes.
Strong ability to facilitate alignment across business, operational, and technical stakeholders.
Demonstrated success managing competing priorities and influencing stakeholders without direct authority.

Core Competencies

Business Analysis and Requirements Management
Analytics Program Management
Stakeholder Engagement and Relationship Management
Analytics Governance and Prioritization
Strategic Thinking and Problem Solving
Communication and Facilitation Skills
Data Literacy and Analytical Thinking
Process Design and Continuous Improvement
Project and Program Coordination
Executive Communication
Documentation and Organizational Skills
Cross-Functional Collaboration and Influence
Decision Support and Business Acumen
Accountability and Execution Discipline
Organizational Agility and Adaptability
Remote Collaboration Effectiveness

Additional Requirements

Physical Requirements
The requirements described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job with or without reasonable accommodations. Unless otherwise indicated, Accuity positions require interaction with people and technology while either sitting or standing. Employees must be able to communicate via phone, email, etc. and sit for extended periods of time, with or without reasonable accommodations. title: Mechanical BIM Detailer
description:

The Mechanical BIM Detailer will work closely with engineers, project managers, field foremen, and fabrication teams to create accurate construction and fabrication drawings that support efficient installation and prefabrication. In a design-build environment, this role will contribute from conceptual design through project completion, helping identify design conflicts, optimize system routing, and ensure constructability.
Key Responsibilities
Client & Stakeholder Engagement

Coordinate with engineers, project managers, field foremen, and fabrication teams throughout project execution.
Communicate design conflicts, constructability concerns, and coordination issues to project stakeholders.
Collaborate with engineering teams during design-build projects to develop efficient mechanical system layouts.
Support project managers with submittal reviews and coordination activities.

Design, Technical & Operational Execution

Utilize Fabrication CADmep and AutoCAD to create installation and fabrication-ready drawings.
Coordinate mechanical systems with architectural, structural, and other trade disciplines.
Identify and resolve design conflicts and constructability issues prior to installation.
Generate fabrication drawings and material lists to support shop production and field installation.
Optimize routing and layout of systems to improve installation efficiency and reduce costs.
Verify existing field conditions as necessary to support accurate modeling and coordination.

Project & Cross-Discipline Coordination

Review construction documents, plans, specifications, and submittals for accuracy and coordination.
Coordinate with fabrication shops to ensure drawings and project information are transmitted accurately.
Support prefabrication initiatives by developing detailed and coordinated shop drawings.
Participate in coordination meetings and project planning activities.
Work closely with field teams to ensure drawings accurately reflect project requirements and installation needs.

Documentation & Communication

Maintain accurate BIM models, fabrication drawings, and project documentation.
Assist in reviewing and incorporating submittal revisions and design changes.
Document coordination decisions and communicate updates to project teams.
Ensure project files and drawings are organized and maintained according to company standards.

Leadership & Resource Management (Senior Detailer)

Provide technical guidance and mentoring to junior detailers.
Support BIM and detailing standards across projects.
Assist with workload planning and project coordination as assigned.
Promote best practices in modeling, coordination, and fabrication detailing.

Desired Skills and Experience
Education & Credentials

Associate degree, technical certification, or equivalent industry experience preferred.
Completion of or willingness to attend Fabrication CADmep and AutoCAD training.
Union membership with the International Association of Sheet Metal, Air, Rail and Transportation Workers (SMART), or ability to obtain membership if required.

Experience
Mechanical BIM Detailer

Minimum 5 years of field experience in mechanical construction, preferably as a Foreman or Lead Installer.
Experience with mechanical, plumbing, piping, or sheet metal systems.

Senior Mechanical BIM Detailer

5+ years of mechanical detailing experience.
5+ years of experience with plumbing, piping, and/or sheet metal systems.
Demonstrated experience leading coordination efforts and supporting complex projects.

Technical & Professional Skills

Strong ability to read and interpret construction drawings, specifications, and submittals.
Proficiency with Fabrication CADmep, AutoCAD, and related BIM software.
Knowledge of mechanical construction means and methods.
Understanding of prefabrication and shop drawing processes.
Ability to identify design and constructability issues and develop practical solutions.
Strong organizational, time management, and multitasking skills.
Effective verbal and written communication skills.

title: Building Science Engineer
description:
Hey there! Are you an engineering wizard looking for a new challenge? Are you ready to take your engineering skills to the next level? Do you love solving mysteries and puzzles? If yes, CEP Forensic is the best place for you to pursue a career!
Founded in 1972 by 3 engineers, CEP Forensic Inc. now has 10 offices across Canada and employs over 170 professionals. Our Values of Trust, Caring, Excellence, and Adaptability, aren’t just words on paper, they are the foundational pillars that guide our every action and decision.
In over 50 years of existence, CEP Forensic has successfully determined the most probable cause of a loss or a failure in over 125000 cases in a wide range of fields including; Fire Investigation, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical and Biomechanical, Structural and Civil Engineering, Materials Engineering, Metallurgy, Collision Reconstruction, Chemistry and Chemical Engineering as well as Environmental Science.
We're looking for a top-notch engineer to join our awesome team in Calgary, who can tackle complex scenarios and solve mysteries backed by scientific reasonings. If you're someone who takes your job seriously but also has a great sense of humor, we want you on our team.
Would you like to write CEP's future with us?
The quest
As a forensic expert, you'll be solving some of the most peculiar and perplexing cases that come our way. No mystery is too small or too big for you to handle. Here’s what you will typically be doing:
This is a technically demanding, challenging and most rewarding role requiring a thorough understanding of building science engineering and its application in failure investigations. You will:

Perform and manage building science and structural failure investigations and determine root and cause of the failure and damage to buildings, foundations, structures, and building envelope systems.
Attend client meetings and on-site inspections, perform surveys and condition assessments and gather evidence. Review technical documentation including drawings, standards, codes, regulations, material specifications, maintenance records, modifications records, etc. Perform Provincial Codes and Standards compliance analysis and reviews. Determine circumstances surrounding the incident by capturing data, photographs, videos, and interviewing parties associated with the incident. Safely secure evidence for further analysis, and presentation to client and/or in court if required.
Collaborate with other experts and practice leads to deliver holistic and robust analytical reports to clients. Provide expert testimony in the court, if required.
Coach and mentor early career technical staff to support their professional development.
Assist with new business development and represent the company with professionalism and expertise in client interactions and industry events.
Always follow HSE guidelines, procedures, and policies. Ensure safety of self, others, and the assets.

What’s in your bag?

At least a bachelor’s degree in civil, building science or architectural science engineering and P. Eng. designation.
Minimum 6 years of experience of failure and damage analysis, design, construction, maintenance of structures and building envelope systems of commercial, residential, institutional, and industrial buildings and infrastructure.
Concern for efficiency and strong analytical, organizational and time management skills.
Curiosity, good judgment, sense of initiative.
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills with ability to write clear and concise investigation reports.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team and commitment to staying current with industry developments and continuous professional development.
A sense of humor that can brighten up people around you.
A deep understanding of the power of laughter and its ability to make even the toughest of cases seem less daunting.

But here’s the thing – we’re not just looking for someone who meets our requirements alone. We’re looking for someone who will brings to the table a unique personality, passion, and love for the forensic profession where some of the following benefits are waiting for you:
What’s on the table

Hybrid work arrangement that supports work-life harmonization;
Fun and supportive work environment;
Opportunities for professional growth;
Competitive compensation commensurate with experience. Performance bonuses. A benefits package with no waiting period, including health, dental, vision, massages, mental wellbeing, employee and family assistance programs, virtual health consulting, RRSP, fitness and home office allowance, paid time off including your birthday, employee events and fun activities.
A chance to work with some seriously awesome people.

So, if you are proud of your engineering expertise and are known for your passion in finding root cause of failures and damages, and you love the quest, got a bag full of your tools and are excited about this role, be our next top-notch expert!

Makes minor adjustments and repairs to heating, cooling, ventilation, plumbing, electrical and lighting systems.
Performs painting and drywall repair duties.
Ensures adherence to Quality Standards, Wellness Strategies and all Health and Safety Regulations.

title: Campus Director
description:
OVERVIEW

The Campus Director is the senior executive leader of LaSalle College Jakarta (LCJ), accountable for the campus’s full commercial, operational, and academic performance. Reporting into LCI Education’s global network, the Campus Director sets LCJ’s strategic direction, safeguards its regulatory and accreditation standing in Indonesia, and adapts global best practice intelligently to the local market. Most non-academic staff report into this role.

This is a hands-on commercial leadership role: full P&L ownership, budget discipline, and a genuine business mindset are essential, alongside a strong focus on student experience and staff engagement. The Campus Director is also LCJ’s principal link to government, regulators, industry, and accrediting bodies — and, as steward of LCI Education’s values, leads with Respect, drives growth through Entrepreneurship, takes Accountability for outcomes, builds Collaboration across a diverse team, and pursues Quality in everything the campus delivers.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Campus Operations Management: Lead and manage campus operations, including academic and administrative functions, ensuring alignment with LCJ's mission, values, and the LCJ Strategic Plan 2025–2030.
Commercial and Financial Performance: Own the campus P&L in full — revenue, cost base, and operating margin. Partner with the Finance Manager to manage budgets, forecasts, pricing, and resource allocation with strong commercial discipline, ensuring financial sustainability and risk mitigation.
Student Recruitment and Market Growth: Drive enrolment growth, market reach, and revenue diversification in partnership with the Head of Marketing & Admissions APAC, strengthening brand recognition in Indonesia and the wider region.
Regulatory Compliance and Reporting: Oversee compliance with BAN-PT accreditation standards (IAPS 5.0), Kemendiktisaintek/DIKTI requirements, and other applicable statutory regulations. Prepare and present reports to the Executive Director APAC and the Board, providing insight on key performance indicators, strategic initiatives, and campus operations through a disciplined quarterly reporting cadence.
Leadership and Team Collaboration: Chair regular leadership team meetings to foster a collaborative environment and drive strategic discussions. Work closely with the Academic Manager, Finance Manager, IT Manager, and Marketing & Admissions team to increase enrolments and enhance the campus profile.
Event Planning and Execution: Provide leadership in planning and executing key campus events, including graduation, exhibitions, and other significant industry events, ensuring they align with the institution's goals and values.
Student, Alumni and Staff Engagement: Foster strong relationships with students, alumni, staff, industry partners, and government agencies to maintain a vibrant and supportive campus community. Champion student support services to enhance student experience, retention, and lifelong relationships, and build the alumni network.
Policy Development and Enforcement: Develop and enforce campus policies and procedures that support the institution's mission and objectives, ensuring effective communication and implementation across the organisation.
Human Resources and Talent Management: Partner with the Talent & Culture Business Partner on recruitment, onboarding, and professional development. Oversee performance reviews and talent management to ensure effective resourcing across academic and administrative functions.
Quality Assurance and Improvement: Ensure continuous quality improvement across all campus operations and educational offerings and maintain rigorous internal audit readiness against BAN-PT and other accreditation frameworks.
Partnerships and Institutional Relationships: Develop institutional partnerships, linkage agreements, and MOUs (pathway, articulation, and transfer-credit arrangements) with schools, industry, and other academic institutions.

SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE, AND ATTRIBUTES

Communication: Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to connect with diverse stakeholders across government, industry, and academia.
Problem-solving: Strong analytical, commercially minded, and solution-oriented skills, with an ability to translate strategic and financial goals into actionable plans.
Planning & Organising: Effective project and budget management skills, with the ability to manage complexity, competing priorities, and deadlines.
Learning & Technology: Knowledge of educational technologies and commitment to ongoing professional development.
Self-Management: Ability to work independently, exercise sound commercial judgement, and manage competing priorities.
Teamwork: Elevated level of professionalism, diplomacy, and ability to work collaboratively with a range of people across a matrixed international organisation.

REPORTS TO

Through the Executive Director APAC, LCI Education, on operational, financial, academic, and compliance matters. On certain governance items, the Campus Director may be accountable jointly to the Shareholder of LCI Indonesia, who may work directly with the Campus Director on such matters.

Contact drivers.

Executive summaries (WBRs, MBRs, QBRs).

Cost reduction.
Revenue opportunities.
Customer experience improvements.

Contact taxonomy.

CX metrics (Resolution, Sentiment, Effort)

SQL outputs.
Prompt-generated results.
Reporting layers.

Create and maintain engineering documentation including CAD models, drawings, GD&T specifications, BOMs, product specifications, test protocols, test reports, and DHF deliverables.
Ensure documentation is complete, accurate, and compliant with quality system requirements.
Support design verification and validation activities through timely and thorough documentation.

Design Verification & Validation

Develop and execute verification and validation strategies, plans, protocols, and reports.
Define test methods, acceptance criteria, and data collection approaches to demonstrate compliance with product requirements.
Analyze test results, resolve identified issues, and present findings during technical and design reviews.

Verification & Validation Builds

Coordinate prototype, engineering, and production-intent builds.
Partner with Operations, Manufacturing Engineering, Supply Chain, and Quality to ensure build readiness and successful execution.
Track build outcomes, document findings, and drive issue resolution.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Collaborate with Quality, Regulatory, Clinical, Marketing, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Program Management, and Operations teams to achieve project objectives.
Support design transfer, manufacturing readiness, and product launch activities.
Communicate project status, technical risks, and mitigation plans to stakeholders.

Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that enhance product quality and development efficiency

Required

Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
5+ years of product development experience, preferably in the medical device industry.
Experience developing mechanical and/or electromechanical products in a regulated environment.
Strong knowledge of design controls, risk management, and regulated product development processes.
Expertise in product design, DFx, materials selection, manufacturing processes, and mechanical problem-solving.
Experience creating engineering documentation, including drawings, specifications, BOMs, DHF deliverables, and verification/validation documentation.
Proficiency with SolidWorks or similar 3D CAD software, including GD&T and engineering drawing creation.

title: Coordinator, Policy & Planning
description:
The Law Society of BC is seeking a permanent, full-time Coordinator in our Policy department. The Coordinator, Policy & Planning is responsible for coordinating strategic planning, implementation, monitoring and reporting processes for the Policy & Planning department, with a primary focus on supporting the Director in the successful implementation and ongoing coordination of the Law Society’s strategic plan and related strategic initiatives. The position performs intermediate administrative and project coordination work requiring tact, diplomacy, sound judgment, strong organizational ability and the ability to work with a variety of internal and external stakeholders. The position also retains selected committee, meeting and administrative support functions for the department, including support for Benchers, committees, task forces, working groups and other ad hoc groups as required.
The duties of this position include:

Assisting with document management to support strategic planning and reporting processes for the department, maintaining workplans, project trackers, performance measures, milestone schedules and related documentation. Assisting with executing on actionable items from strategic workplan, including supporting measurable actions, timelines, deliverables and progress updates, and coordinating follow-up with departments and business leads to gather information and keep work on track.
Tracking the progress of strategic initiatives as instructed by the Director, identifying issues, risks, gaps, outstanding items or areas requiring adjustment, and communicating practical options or recommendations to the Director.
Coordinating cross-departmental input for strategic initiatives, including scheduling meetings and touchpoints, tracking action items, monitoring deadlines and ensuring timely follow-up to support smooth departmental and organizational operations.
Assisting with the preparation, coordination, formatting and quality control of strategic planning and reporting materials, including reports, dashboards, presentations, briefing materials, templates and correspondence for the Executive Director/Chief Executive Officer, Executive Committee, Benchers, committees, task forces and senior leadership.
Maintaining bring-forward systems, calendars, records and documentation to ensure deadlines are monitored and met, and that appropriate materials are provided in a timely manner.
Providing committee and meeting support for Benchers, committees, task forces, working groups and other ad hoc groups as requested, including initiating agenda creation, coordinating materials, scheduling logistics, attending meetings to take notes as necessary, preparing minutes as necessary, and diarizing recommendations, decisions, deadlines and action items.
Communicating and following up with committee members, staff and other stakeholders on meeting dates, deadlines, deliverables and requests for information.
Arranging, or assisting in arranging workshops, forums, planning sessions and other special events related to the work of the department.
Managing selected scheduling and administrative support for the Director and department, including booking meetings and appointments, arranging travel where required, processing payments, creating and maintaining files, and maintaining departmental filing and records systems.
Ensuring effective communication between the department and all internal and external parties, and exercising tact, diplomacy and discretion when dealing with a broad range of audiences and sensitive information.
Providing back-up administrative support to the department as required.
Such other duties as may be assigned by the Director, Policy & Strategic Initiatives.

Qualifications

A diploma preferably in public administration, business administration, public policy, legal administration or a related field.
Three years of recent relevant experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience in a coordinator or related support role, preferably in a regulatory, public sector, professional or non-profit environment.
Strong organizational, analytical, communication and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities, exercise tact, discretion and confidentiality, and produce clear, accurate work in a fast-paced environment.
Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel and Outlook is required.
Experience supporting committees, task forces or governance bodies, and experience in a legal, regulatory, policy or strategic planning environments are assets.

The salary range for this position is $71,093 to $77,275.
The Law Society of BC is dedicated to promoting equity, diversity, and inclusion in all aspects of our work. We welcome individuals from diverse backgrounds and experiences to contribute to the future of our organization. In accordance with the Law Society of B.C.’s commitment to reconciliation, we seek to create a culturally safe space and to continue further improving relationships with Indigenous peoples.
The closing date for this competition is July 31, 2026. We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.
The Law Society of BC supports hybrid work schedules. This position is located at the Law Society of British Columbia office in the Yaletown area of Vancouver, BC.

title: Solar Engineer Intern/Co-op Summer 2027 - Energy Solutions
description:
The core business of our Energy Solutions division is the delivery of Guaranteed Energy Savings Performance Contracts (ESPCs). Simply put, our ESPCs are a viable way to upgrade and renovate facilities in a budget-neutral or even budget-positive way. The process diverts money already being spent on utilities and directs it into facility upgrades, covering scope development, design, bidding, construction management, commissioning, measurement and verification, and even ongoing energy management services. We have experience in designing the nation’s most energy efficient buildings, including many zero energy buildings. Our knowledge is unparalleled in the Guaranteed ESPC market, which allows us to dive deeper than our competitors. CMTA Energy Solutions has a robust co-op program for college students pursuing a degree in Mechanical Engineering. We offer an immersive experience in the world of Guaranteed Energy Savings Performance Contracting for two or more semesters. Our co-ops build competitive industry skills in a hands-on environment through collaborative project tasks with full-time engineers while under the direct supervision of Professional Engineers. Our program is designed to develop students into full-time caliber employees that contribute to the company’s growth. The ideal candidate will possess excellent interpersonal skills and will be able to work well both as a team member and independently. Our program stands apart from the typical, rehearsed co-op rotation in which every co-op gains the same experience because it is designed for co-ops to stand out and take on challenging projects. Co-ops will be involved with multiple Guaranteed Energy Savings Performance Contracts and will have a role in every stage of their development. Each stage offers a variety of valuable experiences, from initial development through implementation. Whether co-ops are interested in building their skill set in identifying and calculating energy savings measures, developing renovation documents, or hands-on field experience, CMTA Energy Solutions is bound to overcome expectations. Solar Co-ops can expect to get hands on experience with photovoltaic systems. By the end of the program co-ops will have gained the experience to be able to deliver a full photovoltaic design from scratch. Our Solar co-op will directly support our solar project managers. Job Functions: (may include but are not limited to)

  • Assist in all aspects of the project development phase – including site visits, building audits, energy calculations in relation to PV arrays
  • Generate energy models and perform calculations to evaluate feasibility of energy savings measures such as PV arrays
  • Produce detailed construction documents using CAD for new PV arrays
  • Field verify proper installation and implementation of PV array

Requirements:

  • Pursuing a BSEE, preferably a sophomore (2nd year), or junior (3rd year)
  • CAD experience is helpful but not required
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Word and Excel
  • Ability to work both independently and as a team member
  • Ability to travel for field work

No sponsorship is available for this position.

About the site:
Our Wheeling facility combines precision machining and assembly capabilities to deliver high-quality medical device components and finished products.

About the role:
Hours: Monday -Friday 8:00am – 4:00 pm (includes 20 minute paid lunch)
The coordinator supports daily logistics activities and contributes to efficient warehouse operations through effective communication, accurate documentation, and strong problem‑solving skills. Under the direction of the Warehouse & Logistics Supervisor, the Shipping & Receiving Coordinator is responsible for managing all inbound and outbound shipments, as well as the receipt of components, in alignment with established practices and procedures. This role ensures inventory accuracy, shipment timeliness, and compliance with company policies and customer requirements.

We offer market competitive compensation. The potential compensation range for this role is $20/hr. to $25/hr. Actual pay will be determined based on experience, qualifications, geographic location, and other job-related factors permitted by law.

What you’ll do:

Follows all FDA and ISO 134985 specifications & remains current with required training/certifications
Follows all personal and manufacturing Good Manufacturing Practices as defined by Viant practices
Prepare and process inbound/outbound shipments using ERP system
Verify order accuracy, packaging integrity and proper labeling
Insures incoming and outgoing product and inventory are correctly shipped and entered in the ERP system for production planning, accuracy, and traceability purposes
Operate Forklift or other material handling equipment to load and unload materials safely
Assure all materials, components and products are shipped on time to meet customer requirements
Inspect shipments and communicate discrepancies regarding quantities, damage or incorrect items
Prepares proper documentation for US and international shipments as required
Responsible for the receipt of goods, return to vendors, and flow of material throughout incoming process
Maintains 5s principles in all work areas of shipping and receiving
Collaborates with production, purchasing, customer service and quality teams
Flexible schedule will be required to meet business needs, some overtime, weekend, and on call hours may be required
Perform other duties as assigned

Requirements:

Knowledge/Education:

High school diploma or equivalent

Job Experience:

Minimum of 1 year of relevant work, shipping, receiving, overall warehouse experience within manufacturing environment

Skills/Competencies

Knowledge of shipping & receiving product flow, digital scales, ERP system, and cycle counts.
Strong written and verbal communication skills
Ability to work well independently and with fellow team members
Attention to detail and organization skills
Computer skills with proficiency in Microsoft Outlook and Microsoft Office
Excellent vision and hand-eye coordination
Extended periods of bending, lifting, walking and standing
Significant use of hands
Frequently required to lift up to 25 lbs., occasionally up to 50 lbs. with team lift
Warehouse environment with exposure to machinery, noise, and varying temperatures
Use of PPE per departmental standards

Physical Requirements

Working on the production floor of either sitting, walking and standing
